docs.t: Where is total fuel quantity displayed?
docs.x: Where is total fuel quantity displayed? Primary EICAS display. Fuel deck slide 2 Fuel

docs.t: How many fuel tanks does the 787 have, and what are they called?
docs.x: How many fuel tanks does the 787 have, and what are they called? Three: L MAIN, R MAIN, and CENTER. Fuel deck slide 4 Fuel

docs.t: How many pumps are in each main tank, and what are they called?
docs.x: How many pumps are in each main tank, and what are they called? Two: FWD and AFT. Fuel deck slide 4 Fuel

docs.t: How many pumps are in the center tank, and what are they called?
docs.x: How many pumps are in the center tank, and what are they called? Two: L and R. Fuel deck slide 4 Fuel

docs.t: What type of pumps are the center tank fuel pumps, and what is special about their output pressure?
docs.x: What type of pumps are the center tank fuel pumps, and what is special about their output pressure? Override/jettison pumps. Higher output pressure than main tank pumps — center fuel is used before wing fuel. Fuel deck slide 13, FCOM 12.20.1 Fuel

docs.t: Which tank does the APU receive fuel from?
docs.x: Which tank does the APU receive fuel from? Left fuel manifold (L MAIN tank). With no AC power, the L MAIN DC pump runs automatically. Fuel deck slide 3, FCOM 12.20.7 Fuel

docs.t: What are the normal fuel quantity units on the EICAS display?
docs.x: What are the normal fuel quantity units on the EICAS display? KGS x 1000. Fuel deck slide 4 Fuel

docs.t: What units does EICAS switch to when fuel jettison is ARMED?
docs.x: What units does EICAS switch to when fuel jettison is ARMED? LBS x 1000. Fuel deck slide 9, FCOM 12.20.8 Fuel

docs.t: What color is the TO REMAIN target quantity on EICAS when jettison is armed?
docs.x: What color is the TO REMAIN target quantity on EICAS when jettison is armed? Magenta. Fuel deck slide 9 Fuel

docs.t: What is the minimum fuel that remains in each main tank after jettison is complete?
docs.x: What is the minimum fuel that remains in each main tank after jettison is complete? 8,700 lbs per main tank. FCOM 12.20.7 Fuel

docs.t: What does the FUEL TO REMAIN knob do, and how do you activate manual mode?
docs.x: What does the FUEL TO REMAIN knob do, and how do you activate manual mode? Sets fuel quantity to remain after jettison. PULL ON to switch from MLW to manual mode. Rotate to adjust. Push to return to MLW. FCOM 12.10.2 Fuel

docs.t: What type of guard protects the NOZZLE L and R jettison switches?
docs.x: What type of guard protects the NOZZLE L and R jettison switches? Red/white striped hazard guard. Fuel deck slide 6 Fuel

docs.t: What EICAS header change indicates fuel balance has been achieved?
docs.x: What EICAS header change indicates fuel balance has been achieved? FUEL BALANCED replaces FUEL QTY (flashes 5 seconds). FCOM 12.10.4 Fuel

docs.t: What color imbalance pointer appears when imbalance exceeds 200 lbs but the FUEL IMBALANCE message is NOT displayed?
docs.x: What color imbalance pointer appears when imbalance exceeds 200 lbs but the FUEL IMBALANCE message is NOT displayed? Solid white pointer. FCOM 12.10.4 Fuel

docs.t: What does the Nitrogen Generation System (NGS) do?
docs.x: What does the Nitrogen Generation System (NGS) do? Generates nitrogen-enriched air to displace fuel vapors in all tanks — minimizes flammability during flight and ground ops. FCOM 12.20.9 Fuel

docs.t: How is a fuel pump load shed indicated on the flight deck?
docs.x: How is a fuel pump load shed indicated on the flight deck? PRESS light illuminates on the pump switch AND the pump is labeled LOAD SHED on the fuel synoptic. FCOM 12.20.1 Fuel

docs.t: Which EICAS fuel messages are alert (caution) level and require checklist action?
docs.x: Which EICAS fuel messages are alert (caution) level and require checklist action? FUEL QTY LOW, FUEL FLOW ENG, FUEL IMBALANCE, INSUFFICIENT FUEL. Fuel deck slide 5, FCOM 12.30 Fuel

docs.t: Which EICAS fuel messages are advisory only (no immediate checklist)?
docs.x: Which EICAS fuel messages are advisory only (no immediate checklist)? FUEL IN CENTER, FUEL LOW CENTER. Fuel deck slide 5 Fuel

docs.t: What valve connects L MAIN and R MAIN tanks, and what is its normal position?
docs.x: What valve connects L MAIN and R MAIN tanks, and what is its normal position? CROSSFEED valve. Normally CLOSED. Opening it allows any tank pump to supply either engine. FCOM 12.20.3 Fuel

docs.t: What four items are shown in the jettison synoptic footer?
docs.x: What four items are shown in the jettison synoptic footer? MIN FUEL TEMP, FUEL TEMP, TO REMAIN (with MLW), and JETT TIME (minutes remaining). FCOM 12.20.8 Fuel

docs.t: What does a lit amber CROSSFEED VALVE light indicate?
docs.x: What does a lit amber CROSSFEED VALVE light indicate? Crossfeed valve is NOT in the selected position (disagreement). FCOM 12.10.1 Fuel

docs.t: On the expanded EICAS fuel display, in what left-to-right order are tank quantities shown?
docs.x: On the expanded EICAS fuel display, in what left-to-right order are tank quantities shown? L MAIN | CENTER | R MAIN. FCOM 12.10.4 Fuel

docs.t: What minimum fuel temperature is shown on the jettison synoptic? What are the AFM min/max limits (pre-takeoff and inflight)?
docs.x: What minimum fuel temperature is shown on the jettison synoptic? What are the AFM min/max limits (pre-takeoff and inflight)? -37°C shown on synoptic. AFM (L.10.11): pre-takeoff min -29°C, inflight min -42°C (also ≥3°C above freeze point). Takeoff max 49°C, inflight max 65°C. FCOM 12.20.8, L.10.11 Fuel

docs.t: When jettison is ARMED, what two weight references appear on the primary EICAS?
docs.x: When jettison is ARMED, what two weight references appear on the primary EICAS? GROSS WT (current) and MLW (max landing weight) — displayed so crew can determine how much fuel to jettison. FCOM 12.10.5, 12.20.7 Fuel

docs.t: The APU receives fuel from which fuel manifold?
docs.x: The APU receives fuel from which fuel manifold? The left fuel manifold. Fuel deck (full extract) Fuel

docs.t: On the ground with AC power available, which pump automatically supplies APU fuel, and what happens to the DC pump?
docs.x: On the ground with AC power available, which pump automatically supplies APU fuel, and what happens to the DC pump? The left aft AC fuel pump operates automatically regardless of fuel pump switch position; the DC fuel pump turns off. Fuel deck (full extract) Fuel

docs.t: On the ground with no AC power and APU switch ON, which pump runs and how?
docs.x: On the ground with no AC power and APU switch ON, which pump runs and how? The left main tank DC fuel pump runs automatically. Fuel deck (full extract) Fuel

docs.t: How many AC-powered fuel pumps does each fuel tank contain?
docs.x: How many AC-powered fuel pumps does each fuel tank contain? Two. Fuel deck (full extract) Fuel

docs.t: What can a single main tank fuel pump supply?
docs.x: What can a single main tank fuel pump supply? Sufficient fuel to operate one engine under all conditions. Fuel deck (full extract) Fuel

docs.t: What makes the center tank pumps different from main tank pumps?
docs.x: What makes the center tank pumps different from main tank pumps? They are override/jettison pumps with higher output pressure than the main tank pumps. Fuel deck (full extract) Fuel

docs.t: In what order is center tank fuel used relative to wing (main) tank fuel?
docs.x: In what order is center tank fuel used relative to wing (main) tank fuel? Center tank fuel is used before wing tank fuel. Fuel deck (full extract) Fuel

docs.t: What two indications confirm a fuel pump has been load shed?
docs.x: What two indications confirm a fuel pump has been load shed? The pump switch PRESS light is illuminated AND the pump is labeled LOAD SHED on the fuel synoptic. Fuel deck (full extract) Fuel

docs.t: What flight risk exists when an engine is on suction feed at altitude?
docs.x: What flight risk exists when an engine is on suction feed at altitude? Thrust deterioration or engine flameout may occur due to fuel flow reduction. Fuel deck (full extract) Fuel

docs.t: What causes suction feed line restriction as the airplane climbs?
docs.x: What causes suction feed line restriction as the airplane climbs? Dissolved air released from fuel due to decreasing air pressure collects in the suction feed line and restricts fuel flow. Fuel deck (full extract) Fuel

docs.t: What is the long-term consequence of continued use of the crossfeed valve?
docs.x: What is the long-term consequence of continued use of the crossfeed valve? Progressive fuel imbalance. Fuel deck (full extract) Fuel

docs.t: What is the key operational difference between fuel crossfeed and fuel balance?
docs.x: What is the key operational difference between fuel crossfeed and fuel balance? Fuel crossfeed is tank-to-engine; fuel balance is tank-to-tank. Fuel deck (full extract) Fuel

docs.t: List four conditions that cause the fuel balance system to automatically command off.
docs.x: List four conditions that cause the fuel balance system to automatically command off. Fuel is balanced; jettison system is active; FUEL DISAGREE message displayed; FUEL QTY LOW message displayed; airplane is on ground and either engine running. (Any four accepted.) Fuel deck (full extract) Fuel

docs.t: Under what conditions does a flashing white imbalance pointer appear?
docs.x: Under what conditions does a flashing white imbalance pointer appear? Main tank fuel differs by more than 200 lbs AND either the crossfeed valve is open OR the balance system is ON. Fuel deck (full extract) Fuel

docs.t: When the flashing white imbalance pointer is shown, is the FUEL IMBALANCE message displayed?
docs.x: When the flashing white imbalance pointer is shown, is the FUEL IMBALANCE message displayed? No. The FUEL IMBALANCE message is NOT displayed for a flashing white pointer. Fuel deck (full extract) Fuel

docs.t: What replaces the FUEL QTY header when mains are back in balance, and for how long does it flash?
docs.x: What replaces the FUEL QTY header when mains are back in balance, and for how long does it flash? FUEL BALANCED replaces FUEL QTY and flashes for 5 seconds. Fuel deck (full extract) Fuel

docs.t: What fuel quantity does the Jettison ARM switch initialize the "fuel to remain" value to?
docs.x: What fuel quantity does the Jettison ARM switch initialize the "fuel to remain" value to? The MLW (maximum landing weight) fuel quantity. Fuel deck (full extract) Fuel

docs.t: When the Jettison ARM switch is pushed, what display is replaced by the "fuel to remain" readout?
docs.x: When the Jettison ARM switch is pushed, what display is replaced by the "fuel to remain" readout? The fuel temperature and static air temperature displays are replaced. Fuel deck (full extract) Fuel

docs.t: What is the target fuel state when jettison is complete?
docs.x: What is the target fuel state when jettison is complete? The fuel quantity remaining leaves the airplane at maximum landing weight (MLW). Fuel deck (full extract) Fuel

docs.t: Where is jettison time displayed, and in what units?
docs.x: Where is jettison time displayed, and in what units? On the fuel synoptic display, in minutes. Fuel deck (full extract) Fuel

docs.t: At what point does fuel jettison automatically stop?
docs.x: At what point does fuel jettison automatically stop? Just above the FUEL TO REMAIN quantity. Fuel deck (full extract) Fuel

docs.t: True or false: With less than all engines/generators operating there may be insufficient power to operate all fuel pumps, and a load shed is shown on the fuel synoptic.
docs.x: True or false: With less than all engines/generators operating there may be insufficient power to operate all fuel pumps, and a load shed is shown on the fuel synoptic. TRUE. Fuel deck (full extract) Fuel

docs.t: True or false: The two center tank fuel pumps are override/jettison pumps with higher output pressure than main tank pumps, and center tank fuel is used before wing tank fuel.
docs.x: True or false: The two center tank fuel pumps are override/jettison pumps with higher output pressure than main tank pumps, and center tank fuel is used before wing tank fuel. TRUE. Fuel deck (full extract) Fuel

docs.t: What is the total fuel tank capacity of all three tanks on the B787?
docs.x: What is the total fuel tank capacity of all three tanks on the B787? 223,646 lbs. Fuel deck (full extract) Fuel

docs.t: Which of the following is TRUE about APU fuel feed: (A) APU fuel from right manifold; (B) any pump supplying right manifold or right main DC pump; (C) on ground, no AC, APU ON -- DC pump runs automatically; (D) with AC, right aft AC pump auto regardless of switch.
docs.x: Which of the following is TRUE about APU fuel feed: (A) APU fuel from right manifold; (B) any pump supplying right manifold or right main DC pump; (C) on ground, no AC, APU ON -- DC pump runs automatically; (D) with AC, right aft AC pump auto regardless of switch. C. On the ground, with the APU switch ON and no AC power available, the DC pump runs automatically. (The APU feeds from the LEFT manifold, not the right -- all other options describe right-side components, which is incorrect.) Fuel deck (full extract) Fuel

docs.t: Under what conditions does the expanded FUEL QTY display (showing all three tank quantities) appear? (List at least five.)
docs.x: Under what conditions does the expanded FUEL QTY display (showing all three tank quantities) appear? (List at least five.) Crossfeed valve open; fuel tank qty indication(s) inoperative; FUEL IN CENTER message displayed; FUEL QTY LOW message displayed; FUEL LOW CENTER message displayed; FUEL FLOW ENG message displayed; INSUFFICIENT FUEL message displayed; FUEL IMBALANCE message displayed; airplane on ground with both engines off; balance system active; balance system selected on and fuel already balanced. Fuel deck (full extract) Fuel

docs.t: What happens to dissolved air in the fuel tank eventually at cruise altitude, and what does depletion time depend on?
docs.x: What happens to dissolved air in the fuel tank eventually at cruise altitude, and what does depletion time depend on? The dissolved air eventually depletes. Depletion time depends on airplane altitude, fuel temperature, and type of fuel. Once depleted, the engine should effectively operate on suction feed. Fuel deck (full extract) Fuel

docs.x: What caution applies when making a 180-degree turn on a 150 ft wide runway? Requires differential braking/thrust Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.x: How close to the nose must you avoid turning away from an obstacle? Within 55 ft of the nose Cargo Doors (FCOM 1.40.24 / 1.40.25) Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: How many cargo doors does the 787 have? Name them.
docs.x: How many cargo doors does the 787 have? Name them. 3 -- FWD Cargo, AFT Cargo, Bulk Cargo Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: On which side of the fuselage are the FWD and AFT cargo doors located?
docs.x: On which side of the fuselage are the FWD and AFT cargo doors located? Right side Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: How do the FWD and AFT cargo doors open?
docs.x: How do the FWD and AFT cargo doors open? Outside the airplane Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: On which side of the fuselage is the bulk cargo door located?
docs.x: On which side of the fuselage is the bulk cargo door located? Left side Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: How are the FWD and AFT cargo doors normally operated?

docs.t: How is the bulk cargo door operated?

docs.t: What happens to cargo area heating, ventilation, and fire detection when a cargo door is opened?
docs.x: What happens to cargo area heating, ventilation, and fire detection when a cargo door is opened? Nothing -- they are NOT turned off Door Synoptic (FCOM 1.30.14) Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: What does an AMBER door synoptic indication mean for a passenger entry or large cargo door?
docs.x: What does an AMBER door synoptic indication mean for a passenger entry or large cargo door? The door is NOT closed, latched, and locked Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: What does an AMBER door synoptic indication mean for the flight deck overhead door, bulk cargo door, or access door?
docs.x: What does an AMBER door synoptic indication mean for the flight deck overhead door, bulk cargo door, or access door? The door is NOT closed and latched Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: What does a WHITE door synoptic indication mean?
docs.x: What does a WHITE door synoptic indication mean? Door signal is invalid or unknown; door position is unknown Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: What does a green letter "A" on the door synoptic mean?
docs.x: What does a green letter "A" on the door synoptic mean? Passenger door is closed, latched, and locked; slide is in AUTOMATIC mode Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: What does a white letter "M" on the door synoptic mean?
docs.x: What does a white letter "M" on the door synoptic mean? Passenger door is closed, latched, and locked; slide is in MANUAL mode Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: What does a blank slide mode indication on the door synoptic mean?
docs.x: What does a blank slide mode indication on the door synoptic mean? Passenger door is closed, latched, and locked; slide mode is UNKNOWN SEAT BELTS Selector (FCOM 1.30.3 / 1.40.6) Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: What does the SEAT BELTS selector OFF position do to the signs?
docs.x: What does the SEAT BELTS selector OFF position do to the signs? The fasten seat belt and return to seat signs are NOT illuminated Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: What does the SEAT BELTS selector ON position do?
docs.x: What does the SEAT BELTS selector ON position do? The fasten seat belt and return to seat signs ARE illuminated Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: What does the SEAT BELTS selector AUTO position do?
docs.x: What does the SEAT BELTS selector AUTO position do? Signs illuminate or extinguish automatically based on airplane altitude and system configuration Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: List the five conditions that cause the seat belt signs to automatically illuminate in AUTO.
docs.x: List the five conditions that cause the seat belt signs to automatically illuminate in AUTO. (1) Landing gear not up and locked, (2) flap lever at 5 or greater, (3) airplane altitude below 10,000 ft MSL, (4) cabin altitude above 10,000 ft, (5) passenger oxygen on Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: When passenger oxygen deploys, what happens to each sign, regardless of selector position?
docs.x: When passenger oxygen deploys, what happens to each sign, regardless of selector position? FASTEN SEAT BELT illuminates; RETURN TO SEAT extinguishes Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: Are no smoking signs electrically illuminated on the 787?
docs.x: Are no smoking signs electrically illuminated on the 787? No -- no smoking signs are NOT electrically illuminated; placards are installed throughout the airplane OFCR (FCOM 1.46) Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: Where is the Overhead Flight Crew Rest (OFCR) located?

docs.t: Does the OFCR have a fire extinguishing system?
docs.x: Does the OFCR have a fire extinguishing system? No -- it has smoke detection only Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: Who may occupy the OFCR?
docs.x: Who may occupy the OFCR? Flight crew members trained in crew rest evacuation routes, fire fighting, and depressurization procedures Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: What are the OFCR occupancy restrictions during taxi, takeoff, and landing?
docs.x: What are the OFCR occupancy restrictions during taxi, takeoff, and landing? Seat, bunk, and common area may NOT be occupied; OFCR door must be LATCHED CLOSED Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: How many smoke detectors are in the OFCR and where are they located?
docs.x: How many smoke detectors are in the OFCR and where are they located? 4 total -- 1 in common area, 1 in seat area, 1 in each bunk area Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: What does the amber call light above the OFCR entrance do when FLASHING?
docs.x: What does the amber call light above the OFCR entrance do when FLASHING? Smoke has been detected in the crew rest area Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: What does the amber call light above the OFCR entrance do when STEADY?
docs.x: What does the amber call light above the OFCR entrance do when STEADY? An attendant call button on a crew rest PCU has been pushed Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: How long does the OFCR smoke self-test button sound for?
docs.x: How long does the OFCR smoke self-test button sound for? 3 seconds (external alarms also sound) Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: What does the OFCR green status indicator light STEADY mean?
docs.x: What does the OFCR green status indicator light STEADY mean? Smoke detector has power and is operating properly Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: What does the OFCR green status indicator light BLINKING mean?
docs.x: What does the OFCR green status indicator light BLINKING mean? Maintenance is necessary Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: What does the OFCR red status indicator light STEADY mean?
docs.x: What does the OFCR red status indicator light STEADY mean? Smoke has been detected Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: What does the OFCR red status indicator light BLINKING mean?
docs.x: What does the OFCR red status indicator light BLINKING mean? The detector has failed Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: What EICAS message appears when smoke is detected in the OFCR?
docs.x: What EICAS message appears when smoke is detected in the OFCR? SMOKE REST UPR DR 1 (caution) Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: After the Horn Cancel switch is released in the OFCR, how long must smoke be absent before the detector resets?
docs.x: After the Horn Cancel switch is released in the OFCR, how long must smoke be absent before the detector resets? 30 seconds Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: What is the primary evacuation route from the OFCR?
docs.x: What is the primary evacuation route from the OFCR? Down the entrance stairway through the entrance enclosure Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: What is the alternate evacuation route from the OFCR if the main entrance is unusable?
docs.x: What is the alternate evacuation route from the OFCR if the main entrance is unusable? Emergency hatch at the bunk on the RIGHT side Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: What must be done to the lower evacuation hatch after OFCR evacuation, and why?
docs.x: What must be done to the lower evacuation hatch after OFCR evacuation, and why? Must be CLOSED to help prevent the spread of smoke or fire Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: During OFCR decompression, what type of horn sounds and where?

docs.t: What should OFCR occupants do before evacuating during decompression?

docs.x: What effect does pushing HORN SHUT OFF have on the cabin attendant panel SMOKE DETECTED alert? Removes the pop-up window; SMOKE DETECTED appears in small text at the bottom of all cabin attendant panels Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: What type of switch is the OFCR LIGHTS MASTER switch?

docs.t: What does the crew oxygen flow indicator show when oxygen is flowing?

docs.t: Where is crew oxygen quantity checked during Pre-flight?
docs.x: Where is crew oxygen quantity checked during Pre-flight? On the STATUS page (shown in PSI) Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: What reference is used to determine required crew oxygen quantity, and what is the unit caution?
docs.x: What reference is used to determine required crew oxygen quantity, and what is the unit caution? FCOM Performance Dispatch Section 11; first table is in liters, status page is in PSI -- use Table 4 to convert Common Core System (FCOM 1.40) Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: What does the CCS provide?
docs.x: What does the CCS provide? A common computing network and data exchange system for many airplane systems Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: Is CCS operation automatic or manual?
docs.x: Is CCS operation automatic or manual? Automatic Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: What is the main component of the CCS?
docs.x: What is the main component of the CCS? The Common Computing Resource (CCR) Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: How many CCR cabinets are there and where are they located?
docs.x: How many CCR cabinets are there and where are they located? 2 (left and right), located in the Forward EE Bay Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: Are there any CCS controls or indications during normal operations?
docs.x: Are there any CCS controls or indications during normal operations? No Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: Where are the CCR RESET switches located?
docs.x: Where are the CCR RESET switches located? On the overhead panel (L and R) Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: What checklist covers loss of all displays due to a CCR fault?
docs.x: What checklist covers loss of all displays due to a CCR fault? Un-annunciated non-normal checklist: LOSS OF ALL DISPLAYS Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: Which CCR always starts up first?
docs.x: Which CCR always starts up first? The left CCR Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: How long does the left CCR start-up cycle take?
docs.x: How long does the left CCR start-up cycle take? Approximately 2-3 minutes Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: What indicates the left CCR is on-line during battery power start-up?
docs.x: What indicates the left CCR is on-line during battery power start-up? The captain's inboard and lower display units show the default format (CDU pages) Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: What two conditions must be met before the right CCR can begin its start-up cycle?
docs.x: What two conditions must be met before the right CCR can begin its start-up cycle? Left CCR must complete start-up AND a power source other than the battery (APU or external power) must be available Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: What indicates both CCRs are on-line after external power start-up?
docs.x: What indicates both CCRs are on-line after external power start-up? All displays AND the HUD combiners show their default formats Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: How many data networks does the CCS use and what are they called?
docs.x: How many data networks does the CCS use and what are they called? 2 redundant networks -- Channel A and Channel B Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: Name five of the systems whose computing resources are hosted in the CCR cabinets.
docs.x: Name five of the systems whose computing resources are hosted in the CCR cabinets. Any five from: environmental control, communication, electrical, fire protection, fuel, hydraulic, ice and rain protection, indicating and recording, landing gear, lighting, navigation, water and waste, central maintenance and condition monitoring, nitrogen generation, door indication and control Panel Identification Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: What is the name of the panel with selectable pages for VHF, HF, SAT, CAB, GPWS, WXR, and XPDR?
docs.x: What is the name of the panel with selectable pages for VHF, HF, SAT, CAB, GPWS, WXR, and XPDR? Tuning and Control Panel (TCP) Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: What is the name of the panel containing G/S INHIBIT, TRANSPONDER MODE selector, and AURAL CANCEL?
docs.x: What is the name of the panel containing G/S INHIBIT, TRANSPONDER MODE selector, and AURAL CANCEL? Alerting and Transponder Control Panel (ATP) Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: What is the name of the panel with MINS RADIO/BARO, FPV, MTRS, BAROSET, ND mode, MAP, PLAN, MENU, RANGE, WXR, TFC, and TERR?
docs.x: What is the name of the panel with MINS RADIO/BARO, FPV, MTRS, BAROSET, ND mode, MAP, PLAN, MENU, RANGE, WXR, TFC, and TERR? EFIS Control Panel Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: What is the name of the panel with MFD L/R, SYS, CDU, INFO, CHLK, COMM, ND, EICAS arrows, ENG, and CANC/RCL?
docs.x: What is the name of the panel with MFD L/R, SYS, CDU, INFO, CHLK, COMM, ND, EICAS arrows, ENG, and CANC/RCL? Display Select Panel (DSP) Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: What are DUs and how are they labeled on the 787?
docs.x: What are DUs and how are they labeled on the 787? Display Units; labeled outboard, inboard, and lower DUs Aircraft General deck Aircraft General

docs.t: What are the three subsystems that make up Air Systems on the B787?
docs.x: What are the three subsystems that make up Air Systems on the B787? Air Conditioning System, Pressurization System, and Bleed Air System. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: On the B787, engine bleed air is used for which purpose(s)?
docs.x: On the B787, engine bleed air is used for which purpose(s)? Engine core anti-ice and inlet cowl anti-ice operations ONLY. The B787 uses a no-bleed architecture -- bleed air is NOT used for air conditioning or pressurization. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: What flight deck temperature does the FLT DECK TEMP knob set at the mid (12 o'clock) position?
docs.x: What flight deck temperature does the FLT DECK TEMP knob set at the mid (12 o'clock) position? Approximately 75 deg F. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: What is the temperature range of the FLT DECK TEMP control?
docs.x: What is the temperature range of the FLT DECK TEMP control? 65 deg F to 85 deg F. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: What is the temperature range of the CABIN TEMP control (master reference)?
docs.x: What is the temperature range of the CABIN TEMP control (master reference)? 65 deg F to 85 deg F. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: By how much can cabin attendants adjust individual cabin zones from the master temperature?
docs.x: By how much can cabin attendants adjust individual cabin zones from the master temperature? Plus or minus 5 deg F. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: How many total Cabin Air Compressors (CACs) are on the B787, and how are they allocated?
docs.x: How many total Cabin Air Compressors (CACs) are on the B787, and how are they allocated? Four total -- two dedicated to each pack (two to the left pack, two to the right pack). Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: Can a single CAC operate its associated pack in all operating modes?
docs.x: Can a single CAC operate its associated pack in all operating modes? Yes -- a single CAC provides sufficient air to operate its associated pack in all operating modes. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: What controls the B787 cabin temperature and pressurization instead of engine bleed air?
docs.x: What controls the B787 cabin temperature and pressurization instead of engine bleed air? Electrically driven Cabin Air Compressors (CACs) pressurize outside air and supply it to the two air conditioning packs. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: When the EQUIP COOLING FWD switch is selected OFF (AUTO not visible), what happens?
docs.x: When the EQUIP COOLING FWD switch is selected OFF (AUTO not visible), what happens? Both forward equipment cooling supply fans and vent fan are commanded off; the smoke/override valve is commanded open; forward cargo heat becomes inoperative; forward cargo air conditioning becomes inoperative; OVRD illuminates amber. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: What EICAS message indicates the forward equipment cooling system is in override mode?
docs.x: What EICAS message indicates the forward equipment cooling system is in override mode? EQUIP CLG OVRD FWD. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: What EICAS message indicates the aft equipment cooling system is in override mode?
docs.x: What EICAS message indicates the aft equipment cooling system is in override mode? EQUIP CLG OVRD AFT. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: After 30 minutes in equipment cooling override mode at low altitude and low cabin differential pressure, what may happen?
docs.x: After 30 minutes in equipment cooling override mode at low altitude and low cabin differential pressure, what may happen? Non-critical electronic equipment may fail. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: List the seven conditions that cause the FWD equipment cooling system to automatically enter override mode.
docs.x: List the seven conditions that cause the FWD equipment cooling system to automatically enter override mode. (1) FWD EQUIP COOLING switch to OVRD. (2) In flight, both supply fans fail. (3) Both flow sensors fail. (4) In flight, low airflow detected. (5) In flight, excessive temperature detected in forward equipment cooling system. (6) Smoke detected in forward equipment cooling system or forward cargo area. (7) FWD CARGO FIRE ARM switch is ARMED. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: What additional condition applies to the AFT equipment cooling override that is NOT present for FWD?
docs.x: What additional condition applies to the AFT equipment cooling override that is NOT present for FWD? AFT CARGO FIRE ARM switch is ARMED is unique to AFT (FWD has FWD CARGO FIRE ARM instead). Also: smoke in the aft equipment ventilation system. Additionally, if smoke is detected in the aft E/E compartment, the lower recirculation fans are commanded off. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: What type of air does the flight deck receive during normal operation?
docs.x: What type of air does the flight deck receive during normal operation? 100% conditioned outside air. (The passenger cabin receives a mix of outside and recirculated air.) Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: What type of air does the flight deck receive if one pack is off and the associated lower recirculation fan is on?
docs.x: What type of air does the flight deck receive if one pack is off and the associated lower recirculation fan is on? Some recirculated air is supplied to the flight deck. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: What filter type do recirculation fans use?
docs.x: What filter type do recirculation fans use? HEPA filters -- cabin air is drawn through HEPA filters before being reintroduced into the conditioned air distribution system. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: What is the per-flight limit on PACK resets?
docs.x: What is the per-flight limit on PACK resets? A reset of a single PACK is limited to once per flight. Some PACK reset attempts are restricted above 34,000 ft. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: What are the four functions of the AIR COND RESET switch?
docs.x: What are the four functions of the AIR COND RESET switch? (1) Resets any air conditioning faults and attempts to restart normal operation. (2) Resets any trim air valves held closed due to overheat, control failure, or valve failure. (3) Attempts to reset a failed recirculation fan. (4) Resets fault protection. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: Why is resetting an inoperative pack above 34,000 ft potentially dangerous?
docs.x: Why is resetting an inoperative pack above 34,000 ft potentially dangerous? Above 34,000 ft the CACs are close to the surge margin. This may prevent reset of the inoperative pack AND the temporarily reduced CAC flow schedule on the operating pack can cause it to shut down too. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: During engine start, when do packs restart?
docs.x: During engine start, when do packs restart? Not until at least 2 minutes after the engine start sequence is initiated AND the engine is running. If both engines start together and the 2-minute limit is met, packs restart immediately after the second engine is running. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: When is three-CAC operation automatically enabled?
docs.x: When is three-CAC operation automatically enabled? 2 minutes after both engines are running. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: What EICAS message is displayed when a pack is in standby cooling mode?
docs.x: What EICAS message is displayed when a pack is in standby cooling mode? PACK MODE (L, R). Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: How is standby cooling mode indicated on the Air Synoptic?
docs.x: How is standby cooling mode indicated on the Air Synoptic? "STBY COOLING" is displayed in amber. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: What can happen to a pack in standby cooling mode at lower altitudes or higher OAT?
docs.x: What can happen to a pack in standby cooling mode at lower altitudes or higher OAT? The pack may shut down at lower altitudes and higher outside air temperatures. It restarts automatically when altitude and OAT are suitable. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: What CAUTION applies before using external ground conditioned air?
docs.x: What CAUTION applies before using external ground conditioned air? Packs AND lower recirculation fans must be selected off before and during use of external conditioned air. Packs can be damaged if operated while ground air is connected. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: What controls the pack outlet temperature in the trim air system?
docs.x: What controls the pack outlet temperature in the trim air system? The zone requiring the COOLEST temperature controls the pack outlet temperature. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: If the temperature selector is unavailable to the pack temperature controller, what temperature does the pack regulate to?
docs.x: If the temperature selector is unavailable to the pack temperature controller, what temperature does the pack regulate to? Either the last temperature set, or an average cabin temperature of 75 deg F. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: How many zone ducts does each trim air system supply?
docs.x: How many zone ducts does each trim air system supply? Two cabin zone ducts and one flight deck zone duct (each trim air system). Seven total temperature zones. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: When the VENTILATION switch is selected to ALTN, where do the outflow valves reposition, and under what conditions?
docs.x: When the VENTILATION switch is selected to ALTN, where do the outflow valves reposition, and under what conditions? Forward OFV repositions to the 10 o'clock position; aft OFV repositions to the 1 o'clock position. This occurs when airplane is below 13,000 ft and not on the ground. Results in depressurization. Only used with a non-normal checklist. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: How many liquid cooling loops does PECS have, and how many pumps per loop?
docs.x: How many liquid cooling loops does PECS have, and how many pumps per loop? Two independent loops; each loop has one pump package containing two fully redundant pumps. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: What temperature does PECS control the liquid coolant supply to during normal operation?
docs.x: What temperature does PECS control the liquid coolant supply to during normal operation? 80 deg F. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: What is the PECS and ICS coolant mixture and color?
docs.x: What is the PECS and ICS coolant mixture and color? 60/40 percent propylene glycol and deionized water; orange in color. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: What CAUTION applies to PECS after shutting down packs and hydraulic EMP?
docs.x: What CAUTION applies to PECS after shutting down packs and hydraulic EMP? PECS requires a cool-down period to dissipate residual heat from liquid cooled units, preventing damage to the units and degradation of the coolant. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: When does the ICS operate, and what flight deck control does it have?
docs.x: When does the ICS operate, and what flight deck control does it have? The ICS operates anytime the airplane has electrical power. There is no flight deck control. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: How many zonal dryers make up the crown dehumidification system, and where are they?
docs.x: How many zonal dryers make up the crown dehumidification system, and where are they? Two -- one in the forward crown area, one in the aft area. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: When does the flight deck humidification system automatically activate in cruise?
docs.x: When does the flight deck humidification system automatically activate in cruise? 20 minutes into cruise above 25,000 ft, when the HUMID switch is ON. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: When does the humidification system automatically shut off?
docs.x: When does the humidification system automatically shut off? Approximately 1 to 1.5 hours prior to touchdown. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: What temperature does the forward cargo A/C control target at the 12 o'clock (mid) position?
docs.x: What temperature does the forward cargo A/C control target at the 12 o'clock (mid) position? Approximately 60 deg F. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: What is the temperature range and increment of the forward cargo A/C control?
docs.x: What is the temperature range and increment of the forward cargo A/C control? 40 deg F to 80 deg F, in 2 deg F increments. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: When is FWD CARGO FLOW HIGH selected, and what does it do?
docs.x: When is FWD CARGO FLOW HIGH selected, and what does it do? Used for live animal carriage or odorous cargo. Selects high ventilation flow to prevent cargo odors from entering the passenger cabin, or to remove cabin odors. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: What is the bulk cargo heat target temperature when AUTO is selected?
docs.x: What is the bulk cargo heat target temperature when AUTO is selected? 70 deg F. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: If a bulk cargo heater automatic overheat shutdown occurs, can cargo heat be restored in flight?
docs.x: If a bulk cargo heater automatic overheat shutdown occurs, can cargo heat be restored in flight? No -- cargo heat to the related compartment cannot be restored in flight. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: List the five conditions that prevent bulk cargo heating system operation.
docs.x: List the five conditions that prevent bulk cargo heating system operation. (1) Alternate Ventilation System is on. (2) Aft or bulk cargo smoke detection. (3) Bulk cargo zone temperature above 141 deg F. (4) Fault with bulk cargo heating system components. (5) Aft cargo door or bulk cargo door is open. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: Under what OAT condition does the aft cargo heating system operate on the ground?
docs.x: Under what OAT condition does the aft cargo heating system operate on the ground? When outside air temperature is below 45 deg F. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: What is the temperature range of the overhead flight crew rest compartment control?
docs.x: What is the temperature range of the overhead flight crew rest compartment control? 59 deg F (15 deg C) to 80 deg F (27 deg C). Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: What is a key limitation of the crew rest compartment temperature control?
docs.x: What is a key limitation of the crew rest compartment temperature control? The temperature can only be INCREASED above the temperature in the aft cabin area. The system may not achieve the selected temperature under all operating conditions. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: How many outflow valves does the B787 have, and how is flow normally split?
docs.x: How many outflow valves does the B787 have, and how is flow normally split? Two outflow valves (one forward, one aft). Normally, outflow is split equally between them. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: Can either outflow valve alone maintain pressurization?
docs.x: Can either outflow valve alone maintain pressurization? Yes -- either valve alone can maintain cabin altitude and full ventilation rates. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: What is the maximum differential pressure at takeoff and landing?
docs.x: What is the maximum differential pressure at takeoff and landing? 0.11 PSI (MAX delta-P .11 PSI -- takeoff and landing, as shown on the pressurization panel). Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: What data does the pressurization system use to calculate the cabin pressurization schedule?
docs.x: What data does the pressurization system use to calculate the cabin pressurization schedule? Ambient pressure and flight plan data from the FMC. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: What does the pressurization system do just prior to rotation on takeoff?
docs.x: What does the pressurization system do just prior to rotation on takeoff? Supplies a small positive pressurization prior to rotation to cause a smooth cabin altitude transition to the cabin altitude climb schedule. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: What is the normal cabin altitude in cruise?
docs.x: What is the normal cabin altitude in cruise? At or below 6,000 ft. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: How high can cabin altitude be commanded during degraded cruise operations?
docs.x: How high can cabin altitude be commanded during degraded cruise operations? Up to 8,000 ft (more likely with an inoperative pack or CAC). Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: If cruise altitude is unavailable from the FMC in AUTO, what default cruise altitude does the CPCS use?
docs.x: If cruise altitude is unavailable from the FMC in AUTO, what default cruise altitude does the CPCS use? 43,000 ft. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: What source provides the landing altitude barometric pressure correction for descent pressurization?
docs.x: What source provides the landing altitude barometric pressure correction for descent pressurization? The captain's altimeter setting. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: What happens to both outflow valves at touchdown?
docs.x: What happens to both outflow valves at touchdown? Both outflow valves open to depressurize the cabin. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: If landing altitude is unavailable from the FMC and not set manually, what does the CPCS assume and what EICAS message appears?
docs.x: If landing altitude is unavailable from the FMC and not set manually, what does the CPCS assume and what EICAS message appears? Assumes a landing altitude of 2,000 ft. EICAS advisory message LANDING ALTITUDE is displayed. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: During a depressurization event with a takeoff/landing airport below 9,500 ft, at what cabin altitude will the outflow valves begin to open?
docs.x: During a depressurization event with a takeoff/landing airport below 9,500 ft, at what cabin altitude will the outflow valves begin to open? 11,500 ft. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: During a depressurization event with a takeoff/landing airport above 9,500 ft (and at or below 14,000 ft), at what cabin altitude will the outflow valves begin to open?
docs.x: During a depressurization event with a takeoff/landing airport above 9,500 ft (and at or below 14,000 ft), at what cabin altitude will the outflow valves begin to open? 14,500 ft. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: What does CPCS do if cabin altitude reaches 15,000 ft due to any probable failure?
docs.x: What does CPCS do if cabin altitude reaches 15,000 ft due to any probable failure? Outflow valves drive FULL OPEN for the remainder of the flight. Flight crew must NOT attempt to manually close the outflow valves during descent. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: In manual pressurization, if outflow valve position is not available on EICAS, how long must the OUTFLOW VALVE MANUAL switch be held to achieve full valve travel?
docs.x: In manual pressurization, if outflow valve position is not available on EICAS, how long must the OUTFLOW VALVE MANUAL switch be held to achieve full valve travel? 30 seconds. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: What is the LDG ALT selector range?
docs.x: What is the LDG ALT selector range? -2,000 ft (below sea level) to 14,000 ft above sea level. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: What increment does the LDG ALT selector use when turned slowly vs. quickly?
docs.x: What increment does the LDG ALT selector use when turned slowly vs. quickly? Slowly: 100-ft increments. Quickly: 500-ft increments. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: List the conditions under which pressurization indications are automatically displayed on EICAS.
docs.x: List the conditions under which pressurization indications are automatically displayed on EICAS. Landing altitude in MAN; either OFV switch in MAN; cabin altitude above normal range (amber/red); cabin differential pressure above normal range (amber); cabin differential pressure excessive (red); AIR synoptic selected on any MFD; EICAS messages displayed: CABIN ALTITUDE, CABIN ALTITUDE AUTO, LANDING ALTITUDE, PACK L+R, OUTFLOW VALVE AFT, OUTFLOW VALVE FWD, VENTILATION ALTN. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: For what purpose ONLY does the B787 use engine bleed air?
docs.x: For what purpose ONLY does the B787 use engine bleed air? Engine core and inlet cowl anti-ice operations only. (787 no-bleed architecture -- air conditioning and pressurization use electrically driven CACs, not bleed air.) Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: How are the engine anti-ice valves armed, and what opens them?
docs.x: How are the engine anti-ice valves armed, and what opens them? Armed when ENGINE ANTI-ICE selectors are placed to AUTO. Valves open when the ice detection system detects icing conditions, or the selector is set to ON. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: List the five conditions that cause engine anti-ice valves to close automatically.
docs.x: List the five conditions that cause engine anti-ice valves to close automatically. (1) During start. (2) Bleed air over temperature. (3) Bleed air overpressure. (4) Engine fire switch is pulled. (5) Bleed air leak is detected. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: During a go-around with one engine inoperative, if the PACK L+R EICAS message appears momentarily, what crew action is required?
docs.x: During a go-around with one engine inoperative, if the PACK L+R EICAS message appears momentarily, what crew action is required? No crew action is required. This can occur if slat autogap is needed and both packs temporarily load shed; the message is expected and momentary. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: In the Air Synoptic, what color indicates selected temperature vs. actual temperature?
docs.x: In the Air Synoptic, what color indicates selected temperature vs. actual temperature? MAGENTA = selected temperature; WHITE = actual temperature. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: What is the air source for the Forward Cargo Air Conditioning (FCAC) system?
docs.x: What is the air source for the Forward Cargo Air Conditioning (FCAC) system? Air from the forward EE compartment. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: What is the air source for forward cargo HEAT (as opposed to A/C)?
docs.x: What is the air source for forward cargo HEAT (as opposed to A/C)? The forward equipment cooling exhaust fan. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: When does CAC operation use only ONE CAC per pack on the ground?
docs.x: When does CAC operation use only ONE CAC per pack on the ground? At normal ground temperature with both APU Starter Generators (ASG) connected. Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: Why does the AFT equipment cooling system, when in override mode with smoke in the aft E/E compartment, also command the lower recirculation fans off?
docs.x: Why does the AFT equipment cooling system, when in override mode with smoke in the aft E/E compartment, also command the lower recirculation fans off? The lower recirculation fans are commanded off when smoke is detected in the aft E/E equipment compartment to prevent smoke from being circulated into the cabin through the recirculation system. (deck-stated; FCOM ref 2.10.2 not independently confirmed - low risk) Air Systems deck Air Systems

docs.t: How many ice detectors does the Primary Ice Detection System (PIDS) have?
docs.x: How many ice detectors does the Primary Ice Detection System (PIDS) have? Two ice detectors. Anti-Ice and Rain deck Anti-Ice

docs.t: What does the PIDS measure to determine if icing conditions exist?
docs.x: What does the PIDS measure to determine if icing conditions exist? Liquid water content, using TAT and other air data information and temperature sources. Anti-Ice and Rain deck Anti-Ice

docs.t: Where does ice detector data go after it is collected?
docs.x: Where does ice detector data go after it is collected? To the Common Data Network (CDN). Anti-Ice and Rain deck Anti-Ice

docs.t: What data do the ice detectors use to calculate possible ice conditions?
docs.x: What data do the ice detectors use to calculate possible ice conditions? Air Data Reference Function (ADRF) data. Anti-Ice and Rain deck Anti-Ice

docs.t: Below what airspeed is automatic ice detection inhibited on the ground?
docs.x: Below what airspeed is automatic ice detection inhibited on the ground? Below 75 kts. Anti-Ice and Rain deck Anti-Ice

docs.t: How are the PIDS ice detectors kept from icing over themselves on the ground?
docs.x: How are the PIDS ice detectors kept from icing over themselves on the ground? They are heated electrically after engine start. Anti-Ice and Rain deck Anti-Ice

docs.t: What EICAS message appears if the automatic ice detection system fails?
docs.x: What EICAS message appears if the automatic ice detection system fails? [checklist box] ICE DETECTORS (amber caution with checklist box). Anti-Ice and Rain deck Anti-Ice

docs.t: What energy source does engine anti-ice use?
docs.x: What energy source does engine anti-ice use? Bleed air. Anti-Ice and Rain deck Anti-Ice

docs.t: What two areas does engine anti-ice protect?
docs.x: What two areas does engine anti-ice protect? The engine core and the cowl inlet. Anti-Ice and Rain deck Anti-Ice

docs.t: Can engine anti-ice be used on the ground?
docs.x: Can engine anti-ice be used on the ground? Yes -- it can be operated in flight or on the ground (manual). Automatic operation is inhibited on the ground. Anti-Ice and Rain deck Anti-Ice

docs.t: Where on EICAS is the EAI (engine anti-ice) indication displayed?
docs.x: Where on EICAS is the EAI (engine anti-ice) indication displayed? Above the EICAS N1 indication. Anti-Ice and Rain deck Anti-Ice

docs.t: What condition triggers the EAI indication on EICAS?
docs.x: What condition triggers the EAI indication on EICAS? When an engine anti-ice valve is open. Anti-Ice and Rain deck Anti-Ice

docs.t: List the five conditions that cause engine anti-ice valves to close automatically.
docs.x: List the five conditions that cause engine anti-ice valves to close automatically. (1) During start; (2) bleed air overtemperature; (3) bleed air overpressure; (4) engine fire switch pulled; (5) bleed air leak detected. Anti-Ice and Rain deck Anti-Ice

docs.t: What happens if an engine anti-ice duct leak is detected?
docs.x: What happens if an engine anti-ice duct leak is detected? The respective (that engine's) anti-ice valves close. Anti-Ice and Rain deck Anti-Ice

docs.t: What type of heating does wing anti-ice use?
docs.x: What type of heating does wing anti-ice use? Electrical -- thermal anti-icing mats. Anti-Ice and Rain deck Anti-Ice

docs.t: Where specifically are the wing anti-ice thermal mats located?
docs.x: Where specifically are the wing anti-ice thermal mats located? On the leading edge slats -- specifically the 4 slats outboard of each engine pylon. Anti-Ice and Rain deck Anti-Ice

docs.t: Below what airspeed is wing anti-ice inhibited on the ground?
docs.x: Below what airspeed is wing anti-ice inhibited on the ground? Below 75 kts. Anti-Ice and Rain deck Anti-Ice

docs.t: What is the maximum duration that wing anti-ice power can be momentarily shed?
docs.x: What is the maximum duration that wing anti-ice power can be momentarily shed? 30 seconds. Anti-Ice and Rain deck Anti-Ice

docs.t: What event commonly triggers the temporary shedding of wing anti-ice power?
docs.x: What event commonly triggers the temporary shedding of wing anti-ice power? High electrical loads, such as during flap retraction. Anti-Ice and Rain deck Anti-Ice

docs.t: What does the wing anti-ice system do if one thermal mat fails?
docs.x: What does the wing anti-ice system do if one thermal mat fails? It automatically de-powers the opposite thermal mat to prevent asymmetrical wing icing. Anti-Ice and Rain deck Anti-Ice

docs.t: With the WING ANTI-ICE selector in AUTO, when does the system activate in flight?
docs.x: With the WING ANTI-ICE selector in AUTO, when does the system activate in flight? When icing conditions are detected (automatically via PIDS). Anti-Ice and Rain deck Anti-Ice

docs.t: What EICAS indication is displayed when wing anti-ice is active?
docs.x: What EICAS indication is displayed when wing anti-ice is active? WAI. Anti-Ice and Rain deck Anti-Ice

docs.t: With the WING ANTI-ICE selector in ON (manual), what TAT condition must exist for the system to be powered in flight?
docs.x: With the WING ANTI-ICE selector in ON (manual), what TAT condition must exist for the system to be powered in flight? TAT must be below 25 degrees C. Anti-Ice and Rain deck Anti-Ice

docs.t: With flaps out of up, what effect does use of engine or wing anti-ice have on stick shaker speed and minimum maneuvering speed?
docs.x: With flaps out of up, what effect does use of engine or wing anti-ice have on stick shaker speed and minimum maneuvering speed? It increases both, reducing maneuver margin to stick shaker. Anti-Ice and Rain deck Anti-Ice

docs.t: With flaps up, what effect does use of engine or wing anti-ice have on stick shaker speed?
docs.x: With flaps up, what effect does use of engine or wing anti-ice have on stick shaker speed? No effect on stick shaker speed or minimum maneuvering speed. Anti-Ice and Rain deck Anti-Ice

docs.t: What does the pack inlet anti-ice system protect?
docs.x: What does the pack inlet anti-ice system protect? Both ram air inlets for the cabin air compressors. Anti-Ice and Rain deck Anti-Ice

docs.t: What type of heater is used for pack inlet anti-ice?
docs.x: What type of heater is used for pack inlet anti-ice? An electric heater on the leading edge of each inlet. Anti-Ice and Rain deck Anti-Ice

docs.t: How is pack inlet anti-ice controlled?
docs.x: How is pack inlet anti-ice controlled? Automatically, with signals from the automatic ice detection system (PIDS). Anti-Ice and Rain deck Anti-Ice

docs.t: Under what two conditions is pack inlet anti-ice inhibited?
docs.x: Under what two conditions is pack inlet anti-ice inhibited? On the ground, and when TAT is above 10 degrees C. Anti-Ice and Rain deck Anti-Ice

docs.t: What type of heating is used for all flight deck windows?
docs.x: What type of heating is used for all flight deck windows? Electrical heating. Anti-Ice and Rain deck Anti-Ice

docs.t: What protection do the forward flight deck windows have that the side windows do not?
docs.x: What protection do the forward flight deck windows have that the side windows do not? Exterior surface anti-icing (side windows have interior antifogging only). Anti-Ice and Rain deck Anti-Ice

docs.t: What protection do the side windows have?
docs.x: What protection do the side windows have? Interior surface antifogging protection only -- no exterior anti-icing. Anti-Ice and Rain deck Anti-Ice

docs.t: Which window heat switches activate the primary window heat system?
docs.x: Which window heat switches activate the primary window heat system? PRIMARY L SIDE, L FWD, R FWD, and R SIDE (four switches). Anti-Ice and Rain deck Anti-Ice

docs.t: Which windows have BACKUP window heat switches?
docs.x: Which windows have BACKUP window heat switches? Forward windows only -- BACKUP L FWD and R FWD. Anti-Ice and Rain deck Anti-Ice

docs.t: When does the backup antifogging system for forward windows operate?
docs.x: When does the backup antifogging system for forward windows operate? Automatically, when BACKUP L FWD and R FWD switches are ON and the primary window heat system has failed. Anti-Ice and Rain deck Anti-Ice

docs.t: How many wiper speeds do the forward window wipers have, and what are they?
docs.x: How many wiper speeds do the forward window wipers have, and what are they? Three speeds: INT, LOW, and HIGH (plus OFF/stowed). Anti-Ice and Rain deck Anti-Ice

docs.t: What does the WIPER selector in OFF do to the wiper?
docs.x: What does the WIPER selector in OFF do to the wiper? The wiper is off and stowed. Anti-Ice and Rain deck Anti-Ice

docs.t: Which windshields are equipped with a windshield washer system?
docs.x: Which windshields are equipped with a windshield washer system? The Captain's and First Officer's windshields. Anti-Ice and Rain deck Anti-Ice

docs.t: How does the windshield washer system apply fluid?
docs.x: How does the windshield washer system apply fluid? Continuously, while the washer switch is held ON. Anti-Ice and Rain deck Anti-Ice

docs.t: What hazard exists if wipers are used on a dry windshield?
docs.x: What hazard exists if wipers are used on a dry windshield? Windshield scratching may occur. Anti-Ice and Rain deck Anti-Ice

docs.t: How many pitot probes does the B787 have?
docs.x: How many pitot probes does the B787 have? Three (3). Anti-Ice and Rain deck Anti-Ice

docs.t: How many AOA probes does the B787 have?
docs.x: How many AOA probes does the B787 have? Two (2). Anti-Ice and Rain deck Anti-Ice

docs.t: How many TAT probes does the B787 have?
docs.x: How many TAT probes does the B787 have? One (1). Anti-Ice and Rain deck Anti-Ice

docs.t: What triggers probe heat for the pitot and AOA probes?
docs.x: What triggers probe heat for the pitot and AOA probes? Either engine operating. Anti-Ice and Rain deck Anti-Ice

docs.t: What triggers probe heat for the TAT probe?
docs.x: What triggers probe heat for the TAT probe? In flight only. Anti-Ice and Rain deck Anti-Ice

docs.t: Where are the Right and Center pitot probes located on the fuselage?
docs.x: Where are the Right and Center pitot probes located on the fuselage? On the right side of the fuselage nose section (the Left pitot is on the left side of the nose). Anti-Ice and Rain deck Anti-Ice

docs.t: [Knowledge check] TRUE or FALSE: When the BACKUP WINDOW HEAT switches are selected ON, backup window heat anti-fogging is commanded on for the selected windows if the primary window heat system fails.
docs.x: [Knowledge check] TRUE or FALSE: When the BACKUP WINDOW HEAT switches are selected ON, backup window heat anti-fogging is commanded on for the selected windows if the primary window heat system fails. TRUE. Anti-Ice and Rain deck Anti-Ice

docs.t: [Knowledge check] Which statement about the engine anti-ice system is true: (A) EAI displayed above N1 when valve open, (B) can be operated in flight or on the ground, (C) automatic operation inhibited on the ground, (D) ALL the Above?
docs.x: [Knowledge check] Which statement about the engine anti-ice system is true: (A) EAI displayed above N1 when valve open, (B) can be operated in flight or on the ground, (C) automatic operation inhibited on the ground, (D) ALL the Above? D -- ALL the Above. Anti-Ice and Rain deck Anti-Ice

docs.t: Where is the B787 APU located?
docs.x: Where is the B787 APU located? In the airplane tailcone. APU deck APU

docs.t: What is the maximum certified altitude for APU start and operation?
docs.x: What is the maximum certified altitude for APU start and operation? 43,100 ft (no envelope limits). APU deck APU

docs.t: What is the APU fuel burn rate during typical ground operations?
docs.x: What is the APU fuel burn rate during typical ground operations? 480 lb/hr. APU deck APU

docs.t: How many starters and generators does the B787 APU have, and how many are required to start?
docs.x: How many starters and generators does the B787 APU have, and how many are required to start? 2 starters and 2 generators; only one starter and one generator are required to start. APU deck APU

docs.t: What power sources can energize an APU starter?
docs.x: What power sources can energize an APU starter? Forward external power or an engine generator. APU Selector / Controls APU deck APU

docs.t: What three actions does the APU selector ON position accomplish?
docs.x: What three actions does the APU selector ON position accomplish? (1) Opens the APU fuel spar valve and inlet door, (2) activates the AC or DC fuel pump, (3) powers the APU controller. APU deck APU

docs.t: What two things does APU selector OFF accomplish?
docs.x: What two things does APU selector OFF accomplish? Initiates normal shutdown and resets the auto shutdown fault logic. APU deck APU

docs.t: What type of detent is the APU selector START position?
docs.x: What type of detent is the APU selector START position? Momentary, spring-loaded to ON. APU deck APU

docs.t: What does the APU FAULT light (amber) indicate?
docs.x: What does the APU FAULT light (amber) indicate? APU fault and/or fire detected; APU shutdown due to fault/fire; or momentarily during APU controller self-test. APU deck APU

docs.t: If the CCS is not running when START is selected, what happens?
docs.x: If the CCS is not running when START is selected, what happens? The APU controller delays the start until the required common core applications are available. APU Start Sequence APU deck APU

docs.t: Which battery powers the APU controller (APUC), air inlet door, and right starter?
docs.x: Which battery powers the APU controller (APUC), air inlet door, and right starter? The APU battery. APU deck APU

docs.t: Which battery powers the APU fuel shutoff valve, DC fuel pump, and fire detection system?
docs.x: Which battery powers the APU fuel shutoff valve, DC fuel pump, and fire detection system? The main airplane battery. APU deck APU

docs.t: What two batteries must be ON to properly start the APU?
docs.x: What two batteries must be ON to properly start the APU? Both the APU battery and the main airplane battery. APU deck APU

docs.t: What system must be operational (visible indication: CDU page on lower DU) before APU start proceeds?
docs.x: What system must be operational (visible indication: CDU page on lower DU) before APU start proceeds? The Common Core System (CCS). APU deck APU

docs.t: What two conditions must both be true before the APU starter engages?
docs.x: What two conditions must both be true before the APU starter engages? (1) APU air inlet door at full open position, AND (2) required CCS programs running. APU deck APU

docs.t: On battery power only, which APU starter is used?
docs.x: On battery power only, which APU starter is used? Right starter only. APU deck APU

docs.t: At approximately what RPM does the starter disengage and ignition turn off?
docs.x: At approximately what RPM does the starter disengage and ignition turn off? Approximately 50% RPM. APU deck APU

docs.t: When does the EICAS memo APU RUNNING display?
docs.x: When does the EICAS memo APU RUNNING display? When the APU reaches 95% of target speed plus 2 seconds. APU deck APU

docs.t: After an APU start failure, how do you reset the system to enable a restart?
docs.x: After an APU start failure, how do you reset the system to enable a restart? Move the APU selector from ON to OFF (clears APU SHUTDOWN advisory, resets the shutdown system). APU deck APU

docs.t: How many consecutive start attempts will the APU battery support?
docs.x: How many consecutive start attempts will the APU battery support? 2 consecutive start attempts. APU deck APU

docs.t: How long must you wait before a third start attempt if the APU has failed twice?
docs.x: How long must you wait before a third start attempt if the APU has failed twice? 5 minutes. APU Shutdown APU deck APU

docs.t: How long is the normal APU shutdown cooldown cycle?
docs.x: How long is the normal APU shutdown cooldown cycle? 2 minutes. APU deck APU

docs.t: What EICAS message is displayed during the APU cooldown cycle?
docs.x: What EICAS message is displayed during the APU cooldown cycle? APU COOLDOWN (memo). APU deck APU

docs.t: Can the APU be restarted during the cooldown cycle, and if so how?
docs.x: Can the APU be restarted during the cooldown cycle, and if so how? Yes. Place the APU selector back to ON at any time during the 2-minute cooldown. APU deck APU

docs.t: What is simulated at the end of the cooldown period to complete shutdown?
docs.x: What is simulated at the end of the cooldown period to complete shutdown? An overspeed condition is simulated to test the overspeed and fuel shutoff protection, which shuts off fuel. APU deck APU

docs.t: At what RPM does the APUC command the air inlet door to close during shutdown?
docs.x: At what RPM does the APUC command the air inlet door to close during shutdown? 15% RPM. APU Operating Modes APU deck APU

docs.t: Under what conditions is attended mode active?
docs.x: Under what conditions is attended mode active? When either engine is starting or running, OR when the airplane is in flight. APU deck APU

docs.t: Under what conditions is unattended mode active?
docs.x: Under what conditions is unattended mode active? All other ground configurations (neither engine running, on the ground). APU deck APU

docs.t: List the six fault conditions that cause immediate APU shutdown in attended mode.
docs.x: List the six fault conditions that cause immediate APU shutdown in attended mode. APU fire/inlet overtemperature; overspeed/loss of overspeed protection; APU controller failure; speed droop; APU start failure (no rotation, no acceleration, or no light-off); air inlet door failed closed. APU deck APU

docs.t: In attended mode, which three fault conditions trigger APU LIMIT (APU continues running)?
docs.x: In attended mode, which three fault conditions trigger APU LIMIT (APU continues running)? High EGT, high oil temperature, low oil pressure. APU deck APU

docs.t: What EICAS message type is APU SHUTDOWN?
docs.x: What EICAS message type is APU SHUTDOWN? Advisory. APU deck APU

docs.t: What EICAS message type is APU LIMIT?
docs.x: What EICAS message type is APU LIMIT? Caution. APU deck APU

docs.t: Is there a cooldown period when the APU shuts down in attended mode due to a fault?
docs.x: Is there a cooldown period when the APU shuts down in attended mode due to a fault? No. APU deck APU

docs.t: Is there a cooldown period when the APU is manually shut down after an APU LIMIT message?
docs.x: Is there a cooldown period when the APU is manually shut down after an APU LIMIT message? No. APU deck APU

docs.t: Name the additional fault triggers in unattended mode that are NOT immediate shutdown triggers in attended mode.
docs.x: Name the additional fault triggers in unattended mode that are NOT immediate shutdown triggers in attended mode. High EGT/loss of EGT signal; low oil pressure; high oil temperature; APU starter/generator oil filter approaching bypass. (In attended mode these either trigger APU LIMIT or are not listed as immediate shutdown faults.) APU Fuel Feed APU deck APU

docs.t: What is the APU primary fuel pump?
docs.x: What is the APU primary fuel pump? The aft left AC (boost) pump. APU deck APU

docs.t: From which manifold is APU fuel supplied?
docs.x: From which manifold is APU fuel supplied? The left fuel manifold. APU deck APU

docs.t: What happens automatically when the APU switch is moved to ON with no AC power?
docs.x: What happens automatically when the APU switch is moved to ON with no AC power? The left main tank DC fuel pump turns on automatically. APU deck APU

docs.t: When AC power becomes available during APU operation, what happens to the fuel pumps?
docs.x: When AC power becomes available during APU operation, what happens to the fuel pumps? The left aft AC fuel pump operates automatically (regardless of fuel pump switch position) and the DC fuel pump turns off. APU deck APU

docs.t: Up to what altitude in flight can the APU be started with no pumps operating?
docs.x: Up to what altitude in flight can the APU be started with no pumps operating? 14,000 ft pressure altitude. APU Automatic Start APU deck APU

docs.t: What in-flight event triggers an automatic APU start regardless of selector position?
docs.x: What in-flight event triggers an automatic APU start regardless of selector position? Three or more engine generators going offline. APU deck APU

docs.t: How do you shut down the APU if the automatic start condition is no longer valid?
docs.x: How do you shut down the APU if the automatic start condition is no longer valid? Position the selector to ON, then OFF. APU deck APU

docs.t: How do you shut down the APU while the automatic start condition is still valid?
docs.x: How do you shut down the APU while the automatic start condition is still valid? Only by pulling the APU fire switch. APU Fire Detection APU deck APU

docs.t: How many fire detector loops does the APU compartment have?
docs.x: How many fire detector loops does the APU compartment have? 2 (dual fire detector loops). APU deck APU

docs.t: Does the B787 APU have overheat detection?
docs.x: Does the B787 APU have overheat detection? No. There is no APU overheat detection. APU deck APU

docs.t: Normally, how many loops must detect fire to generate an APU fire warning?
docs.x: Normally, how many loops must detect fire to generate an APU fire warning? Both loops. APU deck APU

docs.t: What happens if a fault is detected in one APU fire detector loop?
docs.x: What happens if a fault is detected in one APU fire detector loop? The system automatically switches to single-loop operation. Detection by the remaining operating loop then triggers fire warning and APU shutdown. APU deck APU

docs.t: What EICAS message indicates the APU fire detection system has failed?
docs.x: What EICAS message indicates the APU fire detection system has failed? DET FIRE APU (advisory). APU Fire Warning APU deck APU

docs.t: List the five indications of an APU fire warning.
docs.x: List the five indications of an APU fire warning. (1) Fire bell sounds, (2) master WARNING lights illuminate, (3) EICAS warning message FIRE APU displays, (4) APU fire switch fire warning light illuminates red, (5) APU fire switch unlocks. APU Fire Extinguishing APU deck APU

docs.t: How many APU fire extinguisher bottles are there?
docs.x: How many APU fire extinguisher bottles are there? One. APU deck APU

docs.t: List the five actions that occur when the APU fire switch is pulled OUT.
docs.x: List the five actions that occur when the APU fire switch is pulled OUT. (1) Arms the APU fire extinguisher bottle, (2) closes the APU fuel valve, (3) closes the APU air inlet door, (4) trips the APU generator field and generator breaker, (5) shuts down the APU (if automatic shutdown has not occurred). APU deck APU

docs.t: How is the APU fire extinguisher bottle discharged?
docs.x: How is the APU fire extinguisher bottle discharged? Rotate the APU fire switch in either direction after pulling it out. APU deck APU

docs.t: What is the automatic extinguisher bottle discharge delay after an APU fire signal?
docs.x: What is the automatic extinguisher bottle discharge delay after an APU fire signal? 15 seconds (allows time for the fuel valve to close). APU deck APU

docs.t: On the ground with both engines off, how many fire detector loops are required to trigger APU shutdown and automatic bottle discharge?
docs.x: On the ground with both engines off, how many fire detector loops are required to trigger APU shutdown and automatic bottle discharge? Either loop (single loop is sufficient when both engines are off). APU deck APU

docs.t: What does the APU BTL DISCH light (amber) indicate?
docs.x: What does the APU BTL DISCH light (amber) indicate? The extinguisher bottle is discharged or has low pressure. APU deck APU

docs.t: What EICAS message displays when the APU extinguisher bottle is discharged or low pressure?
docs.x: What EICAS message displays when the APU extinguisher bottle is discharged or low pressure? BOTTLE DISCH APU (advisory). APU Inflight Fuel Flow Penalty (PI.17.11) APU deck APU

docs.t: What does the APU inflight fuel flow penalty table account for?
docs.x: What does the APU inflight fuel flow penalty table account for? Both APU fuel flow AND the effect of increased drag from the open APU door. APU deck APU

docs.t: What is the APU fuel flow penalty at 43,000 ft pressure altitude?
docs.x: What is the APU fuel flow penalty at 43,000 ft pressure altitude? 190 lb/hr. APU deck APU

docs.t: What is the APU fuel flow penalty at 20,000 ft pressure altitude?
docs.x: What is the APU fuel flow penalty at 20,000 ft pressure altitude? 370 lb/hr. APU deck APU

docs.t: What is the APU fuel flow penalty at 5,000 ft pressure altitude?
docs.x: What is the APU fuel flow penalty at 5,000 ft pressure altitude? 530 lb/hr. APU deck APU

docs.t: In general, how does the APU fuel flow penalty change with altitude?
docs.x: In general, how does the APU fuel flow penalty change with altitude? The penalty increases as altitude decreases (530 lb/hr at 5,000 ft vs. 190 lb/hr at 43,000 ft). APU deck APU

docs.t: What are the three main communications control panels on the B787 flight deck?
docs.x: What are the three main communications control panels on the B787 flight deck? TCP (Tuning and Control Panel), ACP (Audio Control Panel), and the MFD Communications page. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: Where is the ATC transponder squawk code displayed on the outboard PFD?
docs.x: Where is the ATC transponder squawk code displayed on the outboard PFD? In the XPDR data block, showing the current code as set on the TCP XPDR page. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: Where is the flight number displayed on the outboard PFD, and where is it set?
docs.x: Where is the flight number displayed on the outboard PFD, and where is it set? The FLT # data block; it is set on the RTE 1/X page. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: What EICAS message annunciates an incoming COMM system message, and where does the text appear?
docs.x: What EICAS message annunciates an incoming COMM system message, and where does the text appear? EICAS advisory message ATC (communications message) with an aural chime; text appears in the ATC Data Block. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: How are arriving company uplink messages annunciated?
docs.x: How are arriving company uplink messages annunciated? Optionally by EICAS COMM message, optional EICAS PRINTER message, and/or optional aural chime; text displayed via NEW MESSAGE menu selection. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: When you push a CAB transmitter select switch twice within one second on the ACP, what happens?
docs.x: When you push a CAB transmitter select switch twice within one second on the ACP, what happens? It places a priority call to a selected cabin station. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: What is the important note regarding the second push of the CAB select switch?
docs.x: What is the important note regarding the second push of the CAB select switch? It deselects the transmitter and receiver audio only after 1 second has elapsed from the first push. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: When the ACP suffers an uncommanded reset/restart, how long does it blank, and what state does it revert to?
docs.x: When the ACP suffers an uncommanded reset/restart, how long does it blank, and what state does it revert to? It blanks intermittently for approximately 5 seconds and reverts to the last configuration set prior to the last aircraft power-down. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: What are the three ways to transmit on the B787?
