docs.x: What are the three ways to transmit on the B787? (1) MIC/INT switch on the control wheel or ACP, (2) control wheel push-to-talk (PTT) switch, (3) glareshield MIC switch. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: Which VHF radio is configured for voice communication only?
docs.x: Which VHF radio is configured for voice communication only? VHF L (left). Communications deck Communications

docs.t: Which VHF radio is normally used for data communication?
docs.x: Which VHF radio is normally used for data communication? VHF C (center). Communications deck Communications

docs.t: How many VHF radios can operate in data mode simultaneously?
docs.x: How many VHF radios can operate in data mode simultaneously? Only one VHF radio can operate in data mode at a time. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: What happens when any VHF radio is tuned to 121.5 MHz?
docs.x: What happens when any VHF radio is tuned to 121.5 MHz? All flight crew automatically monitor the radio; receiver lights on all audio control panels illuminate. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: How is an inoperative VHF or HF radio indicated on the TCP?
docs.x: How is an inoperative VHF or HF radio indicated on the TCP? The display shows ------- - X - ------- where X is the affected radio designation. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: Which VHF radio and TCP continue to operate on standby power in the event of electrical power loss?
docs.x: Which VHF radio and TCP continue to operate on standby power in the event of electrical power loss? The left VHF radio and left TCP. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: How is data mode selected or deselected on a VHF or HF radio?
docs.x: How is data mode selected or deselected on a VHF or HF radio? By pushing the frequency transfer (XFR) switch when the word DATA is displayed on the active radio line. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: How is a VHF or HF radio returned to voice mode from data mode?
docs.x: How is a VHF or HF radio returned to voice mode from data mode? By transferring a voice frequency into the ACTIVE frequency window. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: Are HF datalink transmissions allowed on the ground?
docs.x: Are HF datalink transmissions allowed on the ground? No -- HF datalink transmissions are inhibited on the ground. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: How long must a VHF or HF radio transmit in flight before the RADIO TRANSMIT EICAS advisory appears?
docs.x: How long must a VHF or HF radio transmit in flight before the RADIO TRANSMIT EICAS advisory appears? More than 30 seconds. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: What EICAS message is displayed for a stuck mic in flight?
docs.x: What EICAS message is displayed for a stuck mic in flight? RADIO TRANSMIT CAPT, F/O, or OBS (advisory message). Communications deck Communications

docs.t: How long before a VHF radio is automatically disabled on the ground due to a stuck mic?
docs.x: How long before a VHF radio is automatically disabled on the ground due to a stuck mic? Approximately 35 seconds. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: How is a ground-disabled stuck-mic radio re-enabled?
docs.x: How is a ground-disabled stuck-mic radio re-enabled? By releasing the microphone switch for that radio. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: How many HF radios are installed on the B787?
docs.x: How many HF radios are installed on the B787? Two -- HF L (left) and HF R (right). Communications deck Communications

docs.t: How many pages of HF frequencies can be stored in the TCP, and what is the total number of frequencies?
docs.x: How many pages of HF frequencies can be stored in the TCP, and what is the total number of frequencies? Up to 3 pages, 24 total stored frequencies. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: How many previously tuned HF frequencies are stored in memory?
docs.x: How many previously tuned HF frequencies are stored in memory? The last 100 tuned frequencies. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: What does an HF antenna tuning tone lasting longer than 7 seconds indicate?
docs.x: What does an HF antenna tuning tone lasting longer than 7 seconds indicate? Failure of the system to tune. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: What two modes do the HF radios operate in, and how do you toggle between them?
docs.x: What two modes do the HF radios operate in, and how do you toggle between them? USB (upper side band) and AM (amplitude modulation); toggled with the USB/AM key on the main HF page. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: Can both HF radios receive simultaneously?
docs.x: Can both HF radios receive simultaneously? Yes -- both can receive simultaneously as long as neither is transmitting. When one HF radio is transmitting, the antenna is disconnected from the other. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: What indicator appears in the TCP scratchpad when a frequency is received via ATC uplink?
docs.x: What indicator appears in the TCP scratchpad when a frequency is received via ATC uplink? The frequency is preceded by a UL indicator (e.g., UL 121.875). Communications deck Communications

docs.t: What two things happen when you line select an ATC uplink frequency into the active, standby, or stored position?
docs.x: What two things happen when you line select an ATC uplink frequency into the active, standby, or stored position? The scratchpad is cleared AND the uplink frequency turns green in the uplink data block. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: If a clearance contains both a radio frequency and a transponder code, when does each appear in the scratchpad?
docs.x: If a clearance contains both a radio frequency and a transponder code, when does each appear in the scratchpad? Each appears only when the appropriate TCP page is displayed (VHF page 1 for VHF frequencies, HF page 1 for HF frequencies, transponder page for transponder codes). Communications deck Communications

docs.t: What are the four ADS functions controllable on the ADS page?
docs.x: What are the four ADS functions controllable on the ADS page? ADS ARM, ADS OFF, ADS EMERGENCY, and ADS EMERGENCY OFF. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: What does ADS EMERGENCY do?
docs.x: What does ADS EMERGENCY do? Sends an alert to ATC indicating an emergency situation. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: When does ADS EMERGENCY automatically reset to ADS EMERGENCY OFF?
docs.x: When does ADS EMERGENCY automatically reset to ADS EMERGENCY OFF? At power-up (also via Datalink System Reset). Communications deck Communications

docs.t: How many ADS facilities can the airplane be in contact with at one time?
docs.x: How many ADS facilities can the airplane be in contact with at one time? Up to 5 different facilities. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: How many ATSPs can be inhibited at one time on the ADS page?
docs.x: How many ATSPs can be inhibited at one time on the ADS page? Only one. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: How is an incoming SATCOM call annunciated?
docs.x: How is an incoming SATCOM call annunciated? By a SELCAL chime and illumination of a CALL light on the audio control panel. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: How do you answer an incoming SATCOM call?
docs.x: How do you answer an incoming SATCOM call? Press the respective transmitter select switch on the ACP to connect the call to the pilot headset/hand mic. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: How is a SATCOM call terminated?
docs.x: How is a SATCOM call terminated? When the CALL light extinguishes (ground party hang-up or pilot ends call). Communications deck Communications

docs.t: What EICAS message indicates an incoming SATCOM message requiring flight crew attention?
docs.x: What EICAS message indicates an incoming SATCOM message requiring flight crew attention? SATCOM CALL (communications message). Communications deck Communications

docs.t: What are the four SATCOM call priority levels?
docs.x: What are the four SATCOM call priority levels? EMG (Emergency), HGH (High), LOW (Low), PUB (Public). Communications deck Communications

docs.t: What type of calls does SATCOM EMG priority activate?
docs.x: What type of calls does SATCOM EMG priority activate? Emergency and distress calls; activates the ground station alarm. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: What SATCOM priority level is SBB limited to?
docs.x: What SATCOM priority level is SBB limited to? PUB (Public) priority only. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: What is the procedure to establish a cabin/SATCOM conference call?
docs.x: What is the procedure to establish a cabin/SATCOM conference call? (1) Establish communication with desired SATCOM ground station, (2) Establish cabin interphone communication with the cabin crew (steps 1 and 2 may be in any order), (3) Select both CAB and SAT transmitter select switches on the observer ACP. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: Which ACP must be used to initiate a cabin/SATCOM conference?
docs.x: Which ACP must be used to initiate a cabin/SATCOM conference? The observer ACP (both CAB and SAT selected on the same ACP). Communications deck Communications

docs.t: What is the limitation on the conferencing ACP during a cabin/SATCOM conference?
docs.x: What is the limitation on the conferencing ACP during a cabin/SATCOM conference? The conferencing ACP is unusable by the flight crew for other communications while the conference is in progress. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: What are the four components of the interphone communication system?
docs.x: What are the four components of the interphone communication system? Flight interphone, cabin interphone, service interphone, and passenger address (PA). Communications deck Communications

docs.t: How is the cabin interphone operated, compared to the other interphone systems?
docs.x: How is the cabin interphone operated, compared to the other interphone systems? The cabin interphone is operated through the TCP or the flight deck handset; the other systems (flight interphone, service interphone, PA) are normally operated through the audio select panel (ACP). Communications deck Communications

docs.t: What EICAS message indicates a ground crew initiated call?
docs.x: What EICAS message indicates a ground crew initiated call? GROUND CALL (communications alert message); also accompanied by an aural alert chime and CALL light on the ACP. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: How is the service interphone connected to the flight interphone system?
docs.x: How is the service interphone connected to the flight interphone system? Through the service interphone switch on the overhead panel. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: How do you get direct access to all PA areas from the flight deck?
docs.x: How do you get direct access to all PA areas from the flight deck? Push a PA mic switch on an audio control panel. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: What is the PA sales mode function, and how is it selected?
docs.x: What is the PA sales mode function, and how is it selected? It allows flight crew and flight attendants to make cabin announcements without interrupting passenger IFE audio and video; selected by using the appropriate dial code. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: What are the cabin PA announcement priorities, highest to lowest?
docs.x: What are the cabin PA announcement priorities, highest to lowest? (1) Flight deck announcements from an ACP (Black PA Button), (2) priority all-area announcements via TCP cabin interphone menu, (3) normal announcements from flight attendant or flight deck handsets. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: After a Datalink System Reset, which VHF radio is selected as default?
docs.x: After a Datalink System Reset, which VHF radio is selected as default? The center VHF radio. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: After a Datalink System Reset, what mode is the default VHF radio set to on the ground vs. in the air?
docs.x: After a Datalink System Reset, what mode is the default VHF radio set to on the ground vs. in the air? Data mode on the ground; voice mode in the air. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: After a Datalink System Reset, which HF radio is selected as default and what mode?
docs.x: After a Datalink System Reset, which HF radio is selected as default and what mode? The right HF radio; set to voice mode. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: Does a Datalink System Reset occur at power-up?
docs.x: Does a Datalink System Reset occur at power-up? No -- this reset does NOT occur at power-up. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: If the AMI automatic reset option is selected, when does the automatic datalink reset occur after landing?
docs.x: If the AMI automatic reset option is selected, when does the automatic datalink reset occur after landing? Approximately 10 minutes after the last engine is shut down, with any entry door open. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: What systems' datalink capability is NOT reset by the Datalink System Reset or AMI auto-reset?
docs.x: What systems' datalink capability is NOT reset by the Datalink System Reset or AMI auto-reset? Datalink capability for FMS, OMS, EICAS maintenance functions, and cabin functions. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: When is the oxygen mask microphone enabled?
docs.x: When is the oxygen mask microphone enabled? When the oxygen mask stowage doors are open (boom mic is disabled at the same time). Communications deck Communications

docs.t: How is the oxygen mask microphone disabled and boom mic re-enabled?
docs.x: How is the oxygen mask microphone disabled and boom mic re-enabled? When the left oxygen mask stowage box door is closed AND the RESET/TEST lever is pushed. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: Does the CVR record flight deck audio independent of microphone/interphone switch positions?
docs.x: Does the CVR record flight deck audio independent of microphone/interphone switch positions? Yes -- the CVR records crewmember boom, oxygen mask, and hand microphones independent of switch positions; all inputs are recorded continuously. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: What are the two ways to use the flight interphone without the FLT transmitter selector?
docs.x: What are the two ways to use the flight interphone without the FLT transmitter selector? Select the INT position on the control wheel mic/interphone switch, or select the INT position on the ACP mic/interphone switch. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: What is the indication when a conditional clearance condition has been met?
docs.x: What is the indication when a conditional clearance condition has been met? The communications management system sends a COMM SYSTEM MESSAGE to notify the flight crew. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: How do you cancel a conditional clearance monitor?
docs.x: How do you cancel a conditional clearance monitor? Select CONDITIONAL CLEARANCES from the ATC menu, then choose DELETE on the CONDITIONAL MONITOR page. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: What is the ADS facility identifier format when a previous connection WAS established vs. was NOT established?
docs.x: What is the ADS facility identifier format when a previous connection WAS established vs. was NOT established? 4-character ICAO identifier if a previous connection was established; 7-character ACARS address if not. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: What marker beacon audio note applies to all ACP positions?
docs.x: What marker beacon audio note applies to all ACP positions? Marker beacon audio is available in all ACP positions. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: What effect does selecting MIC/INT, PTT, or glareshield MIC have on flight deck speaker volume?
docs.x: What effect does selecting MIC/INT, PTT, or glareshield MIC have on flight deck speaker volume? Voice level from the flight deck speakers decreases. Communications deck Communications

docs.t: How many variable frequency starter/generators does the B787 have in total, and how are they distributed between engines and APU?
docs.x: How many variable frequency starter/generators does the B787 have in total, and how are they distributed between engines and APU? 6 total -- 4 engine VFSGs (L1, L2 on left engine; R1, R2 on right engine) plus 2 APU VFSGs (L and R). Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: What voltage do the engine and APU starter/generators produce?
docs.x: What voltage do the engine and APU starter/generators produce? 235 Vac, variable frequency. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: List all 8 categories of electrical power sources on the B787.
docs.x: List all 8 categories of electrical power sources on the B787. (1) 4 engine VFSGs, (2) 2 APU VFSGs, (3) 3 external AC power receptacles, (4) 1 RAT, (5) 1 main battery, (6) 1 APU battery, (7) 3 flight control PMGs, (8) 2 EEC PMAs. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: Why does the B787 use variable frequency power instead of constant frequency?
docs.x: Why does the B787 use variable frequency power instead of constant frequency? Electronic frequency conversion is more fuel efficient than the mechanical conversion process used on other airplanes. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: Name five systems that the B787 electrical system powers that go beyond traditional electrically powered systems.
docs.x: Name five systems that the B787 electrical system powers that go beyond traditional electrically powered systems. Engine start, pressurization, wing ice protection, stabilizer trim, and wheel brake systems. Engine Generators Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: Where are the L1/L2 and R1/R2 VFSGs physically mounted?
docs.x: Where are the L1/L2 and R1/R2 VFSGs physically mounted? L1 and L2 are mounted on the left engine gearbox; R1 and R2 are mounted on the right engine gearbox. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: During engine start, how many starter/generators engage and why?
docs.x: During engine start, how many starter/generators engage and why? Both starter/generators on that engine engage automatically to provide optimal start torque. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: What can a flight crew member NOT do after disconnecting an engine generator drive?
docs.x: What can a flight crew member NOT do after disconnecting an engine generator drive? Once disconnected, the drive cannot be reconnected by the flight crew. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: What type of switch is the generator drive disconnect switch?
docs.x: What type of switch is the generator drive disconnect switch? A guarded switch -- requires crew confirmation prior to disconnecting. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: What condition triggers an automatic engine generator drive disconnect?
docs.x: What condition triggers an automatic engine generator drive disconnect? Sump oil temperature exceeding a predetermined temperature. APU Generators Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: When APU battery is the sole power source for APU start (no engines running, no external power), which starter/generator is used?
docs.x: When APU battery is the sole power source for APU start (no engines running, no external power), which starter/generator is used? The right starter/generator is always used. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: How long must you wait after the left CCR comes online before initiating an APU start?
docs.x: How long must you wait after the left CCR comes online before initiating an APU start? 15 seconds. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: What indicates that the left CCR is online?
docs.x: What indicates that the left CCR is online? Captain's inboard and lower display unit showing the default formats. External Power Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: Where are the forward external power receptacles located?
docs.x: Where are the forward external power receptacles located? Two receptacles (L and R) on the left forward fuselage. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: Where is the aft external power receptacle located?
docs.x: Where is the aft external power receptacle located? On the fuselage aft of the left wing. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: What voltage is the external power system?
docs.x: What voltage is the external power system? 115 Vac. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: What is the minimum external power requirement for engine start without the APU?
docs.x: What is the minimum external power requirement for engine start without the APU? Two 90 kVA rated forward external power sources. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: When using external power for engine start without the APU, which engine must be started first to benefit from the aft power source?
docs.x: When using external power for engine start without the APU, which engine must be started first to benefit from the aft power source? The right engine must be started first. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: Does connecting the aft receptacle reduce engine start time?
docs.x: Does connecting the aft receptacle reduce engine start time? No -- it only reduces load shedding; it does not decrease engine start time. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: If two forward external power sources are connected, which one is used?
docs.x: If two forward external power sources are connected, which one is used? The first source connected. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: What does the FWD EXT PWR AVAIL light (white) indicate?
docs.x: What does the FWD EXT PWR AVAIL light (white) indicate? Forward external power is plugged in and power quality is acceptable. It extinguishes when the ON light illuminates. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: What does the aft EXT PWR ON selection power?
docs.x: What does the aft EXT PWR ON selection power? The large motor power system for right engine start. RAT Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: What are the RAT operating limitations?
docs.x: What are the RAT operating limitations? None -- no operating time limits, airspeeds, or altitude limitations. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: List all five conditions that trigger automatic RAT deployment in flight.
docs.x: List all five conditions that trigger automatic RAT deployment in flight. (1) Both engines have failed. (2) All three hydraulic system pressures are low. (3) Loss of all electrical power to captain's and first officer's flight instruments. (4) Loss of all four EMPs and faults in the flight control system occur on approach. (5) Loss of all four EMPs and an engine fails on takeoff or landing. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: Where is the manual RAT deployment switch located?
docs.x: Where is the manual RAT deployment switch located? On the hydraulic panel (RAM AIR TURBINE switch). Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: What does the RAT supply if all main AC power is unavailable?
docs.x: What does the RAT supply if all main AC power is unavailable? Variable frequency 230V AC power to the backup bus. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: Can the RAT be retracted in flight?
docs.x: Can the RAT be retracted in flight? No -- the RAT cannot be retracted in-flight. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: What is the normal source of standby power?
docs.x: What is the normal source of standby power? The RAT generator. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: What powers the standby system until the RAT deploys?
docs.x: What powers the standby system until the RAT deploys? The main battery. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: Describe the complete power path from the RAT to the instrument buses.
docs.x: Describe the complete power path from the RAT to the instrument buses. RAT -- RAT control breaker -- backup bus -- C1 and C2 TRUs -- 28V DC -- instrument buses. Batteries Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: What type of batteries does the B787 use?
docs.x: What type of batteries does the B787 use? Lithium-ion. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: Where is the main battery located? Where is the APU battery located?
docs.x: Where is the main battery located? Where is the APU battery located? Main battery: FWD E/E bay. APU battery: AFT E/E bay. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: What material and thickness are the battery enclosures?
docs.x: What material and thickness are the battery enclosures? 1/8-inch stainless steel. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: Does the APU battery have a flight deck power switch?
docs.x: Does the APU battery have a flight deck power switch? No -- it functions automatically and has no flight deck power switch. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: What bus is the main battery connected to?
docs.x: What bus is the main battery connected to? The HOT Battery Bus. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: Name three loads powered by the HOT Battery Bus.
docs.x: Name three loads powered by the HOT Battery Bus. Engine fire extinguishing, APU fire extinguishing, and CCR cabinet internal clocks and memories. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: Name the six functions the main battery provides power for.
docs.x: Name the six functions the main battery provides power for. Airplane power-up, APU start (APU fire detection and extinguishing), refueling operations, towing operations, electric braking (backup), and captain's flight instruments after power failure until RAT deployment. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: What does the APU battery power on the ground?
docs.x: What does the APU battery power on the ground? APU start, and navigation lights when Towing Power mode is active. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: True or False: The APU battery provides primary power to the aircraft brakes.
docs.x: True or False: The APU battery provides primary power to the aircraft brakes. False. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: What happens when the battery protection system detects a fault?
docs.x: What happens when the battery protection system detects a fault? It stops battery charging and, if necessary, isolates the battery electrically. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: What activates if battery heat and gases reach a level associated with cell failure?
docs.x: What activates if battery heat and gases reach a level associated with cell failure? A burst disk on the enclosure activates, venting gases directly overboard through a vent tube in the fuselage. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: How long is the delay after selecting the battery switch OFF before On-Ground Battery Only mode de-energizes?
docs.x: How long is the delay after selecting the battery switch OFF before On-Ground Battery Only mode de-energizes? Up to 2 minutes. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: What does selecting the battery switch ON initiate first?
docs.x: What does selecting the battery switch ON initiate first? The L CCR start-up sequence. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: What amber light indicates the BATTERY switch is OFF?
docs.x: What amber light indicates the BATTERY switch is OFF? The Battery OFF light (illuminated amber). PMGs and PMAs Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: How many flight control PMGs does the B787 have, and where are they located?
docs.x: How many flight control PMGs does the B787 have, and where are they located? 3 -- engine-driven, contained within the VFSG housing. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: What are PMGs independent from?
docs.x: What are PMGs independent from? Independent from the main airplane electrical system and independent from each other. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: What is the secondary source of power for flight control electronics?
docs.x: What is the secondary source of power for flight control electronics? The airplane's 28 Vdc bus distribution system and the main battery; plus 2 dedicated batteries for temporary interruptions. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: How many PMAs does the B787 have, and what do they power?
docs.x: How many PMAs does the B787 have, and what do they power? 2 PMAs (one per engine) -- primary power source for the EEC. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: What is the secondary source of EEC power?
docs.x: What is the secondary source of EEC power? The airplane's 115V AC bus distribution system (also provides initial EEC power during engine start). Power Distribution and Conversion Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: What are the two methods of power distribution on the B787?
docs.x: What are the two methods of power distribution on the B787? Primary (higher amperage loads direct from bus panels in E/E bays) and remote (lower amperage loads via 17 RPDUs). Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: How many RPDUs does the B787 have?
docs.x: How many RPDUs does the B787 have? 17. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: What is the amperage threshold between bus system and RPDU distribution?
docs.x: What is the amperage threshold between bus system and RPDU distribution? Greater than 10 amps = bus system; 10 amps or less = RPDU. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: What do ATRUs convert, and what is the output?
docs.x: What do ATRUs convert, and what is the output? 235V AC to +/- 270V DC for the Common Motor Starter Controllers. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: What do TRUs convert?
docs.x: What do TRUs convert? Variable frequency 235V AC to 28V DC (feeds the 28V DC buses). Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: Are ATUs bidirectional?
docs.x: Are ATUs bidirectional? Yes -- they convert 235V AC to 115V AC or vice versa. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: What does the EBPSU convert and for what purpose?
docs.x: What does the EBPSU convert and for what purpose? 28V DC to +/- 130V DC for the brake system. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: What does the GATU do?
docs.x: What does the GATU do? Converts 235V AC to 115V AC for the aft galley only. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: Where are the four main 235 Vac buses located?
docs.x: Where are the four main 235 Vac buses located? Aft E/E bay. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: Where are the 115 Vac and 28 Vdc primary buses located?
docs.x: Where are the 115 Vac and 28 Vdc primary buses located? Forward E/E bay. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: What do CMSCs do?
docs.x: What do CMSCs do? Convert +/- 270V DC to the specific AC voltage and frequency required by the motor being controlled. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: Name the seven system types powered by the high voltage (+/-270V DC) system.
docs.x: Name the seven system types powered by the high voltage (+/-270V DC) system. Cabin Air Compressors, hydraulic pumps, ram air fans, override/jettison pumps, Nitrogen Generation System, main engine starting, APU starting. Bus Architecture Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: On the ground with only forward external power ON (no APU, no engine), how are the 235 Vac buses energized?
docs.x: On the ground with only forward external power ON (no APU, no engine), how are the 235 Vac buses energized? The 115 Vac distribution system energizes the 235 Vac buses through power conversion devices (ATUs operating in reverse direction). Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: On the ground with only APU power, how many 235 Vac buses does each APU generator energize?
docs.x: On the ground with only APU power, how many 235 Vac buses does each APU generator energize? Each APU generator energizes two of the four main 235 Vac buses. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: With one engine running and no APU or external power, how are all four 235 Vac buses powered?
docs.x: With one engine running and no APU or external power, how are all four 235 Vac buses powered? The running engine's two related buses are energized directly; the other two are energized by the powered buses. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: With both engines running and one generator fails, how is the affected bus powered?
docs.x: With both engines running and one generator fails, how is the affected bus powered? Its related main bus is energized by another main 235 Vac bus. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: What EICAS message indicates a main 235 Vac bus is inoperative?
docs.x: What EICAS message indicates a main 235 Vac bus is inoperative? ELEC AC BUS (L1, L2, R1, or R2). PECS Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: What does PECS cool, and when is it energized?
docs.x: What does PECS cool, and when is it energized? Dissipates heat from high voltage motor controllers. Energized when one or both engines running, APU running, or forward external power connected and selected ON. Electrical Modes Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: What mode is active when BATTERY switch is ON, airplane on ground, no other power sources?
docs.x: What mode is active when BATTERY switch is ON, airplane on ground, no other power sources? On-Ground Battery Only mode. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: What is the purpose of On-Ground Battery Only mode?
docs.x: What is the purpose of On-Ground Battery Only mode? To support the airplane power-up sequence. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: What mode is active when the first forward external power receptacle is connected but not selected ON?
docs.x: What mode is active when the first forward external power receptacle is connected but not selected ON? Ground Handling mode. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: Which takes priority -- Ground Handling mode or On-Ground Battery Only mode?
docs.x: Which takes priority -- Ground Handling mode or On-Ground Battery Only mode? Ground Handling mode has priority, and it initializes regardless of BATTERY switch position. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: How is Ground Service mode activated?
docs.x: How is Ground Service mode activated? GROUND SERVICE switch on the master attendant switch panel selected ON while in Ground Handling Mode. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: What single load does In-Air RAT Only mode have that In-Air Battery Only mode lacks?
docs.x: What single load does In-Air RAT Only mode have that In-Air Battery Only mode lacks? Center pitot heat. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: With battery power only, which display units are active and what do they show?
docs.x: With battery power only, which display units are active and what do they show? Captain's inboard DU (EICAS) and lower center DU (default CDU display) -- 2 DUs total. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: With external power available (plugged in, not selected ON), which DU is active?
docs.x: With external power available (plugged in, not selected ON), which DU is active? Lower center DU only (default CDU display). Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: With external power selected ON, how many DUs show?
docs.x: With external power selected ON, how many DUs show? All 5 DUs show. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: What loads are additionally powered when a second forward external power cord is connected and selected ON (vs. one cord)?
docs.x: What loads are additionally powered when a second forward external power cord is connected and selected ON (vs. one cord)? NGS, limited hydraulics, and both PECS loops (first cord powers flight deck equipment, cabin lighting, cabin systems, single PECS loop). Load Management Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: What is the difference between load inhibit and load shed?
docs.x: What is the difference between load inhibit and load shed? Load inhibit: loads inhibited at predefined phases (system not needed or power temporarily required elsewhere). Load shed: loads shed in priority order to stay within available power capacity. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: How are load shed items indicated on synoptics?
docs.x: How are load shed items indicated on synoptics? In white on the affected system synoptic, with "LOAD SHED" text next to the affected equipment symbol on the electrical synoptic. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: Give an example of load inhibiting.
docs.x: Give an example of load inhibiting. Both CENTER PUMP PRESS lights stay illuminated until after engine start due to load inhibiting. CBIC Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: What is the difference in CBIC capability between ECBs and TCBs?
docs.x: What is the difference in CBIC capability between ECBs and TCBs? ECBs: indication AND control (can open/close). TCBs: indication only (cannot reset thermal CBs via CBIC). Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: Is it recommended to reset a tripped circuit breaker in flight?
docs.x: Is it recommended to reset a tripped circuit breaker in flight? No -- in flight, flight crew reset of a tripped circuit breaker is not recommended. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: How do you access the CBIC display?
docs.x: How do you access the CBIC display? Push SYS display switch, select ELEC, then CB key on the MFD; or MFK -- SYS -- ECB. Overhead Electrical Panel Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: What does the IFE/PASS SEATS switch control?
docs.x: What does the IFE/PASS SEATS switch control? IFE system, passenger seat systems, video surveillance cameras, and flight deck personal electronic device power outlets. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: What does the CABIN/UTILITY switch control?
docs.x: What does the CABIN/UTILITY switch control? Galleys, most cabin lights, and other non-essential cabin utility loads. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: How many GEN CTRL switches are on the overhead electrical panel?
docs.x: How many GEN CTRL switches are on the overhead electrical panel? 4 -- L1, L2, R1, R2 -- each with a DRIVE indication. Electrics deck Electrical

docs.t: What is the engine model installed on the B787?
docs.x: What is the engine model installed on the B787? General Electric GEnx-1B74/75 Engines deck Engines

docs.t: What is the takeoff thrust rating of each B787 engine?
docs.x: What is the takeoff thrust rating of each B787 engine? 74,100 lbs per engine Engines deck Engines

docs.t: What components make up the N1 rotor?
docs.x: What components make up the N1 rotor? Fan, low-pressure compressor, and low-pressure turbine on a common shaft Engines deck Engines

docs.t: What components make up the N2 rotor?
docs.x: What components make up the N2 rotor? High-pressure compressor and high-pressure turbine on a common shaft Engines deck Engines

docs.t: What drives the engine accessory gearbox?
docs.x: What drives the engine accessory gearbox? The high speed N2 shaft Engines deck Engines

docs.t: Are the N1 and N2 rotors mechanically linked?
docs.x: Are the N1 and N2 rotors mechanically linked? No - they are mechanically independent Engines deck Engines

docs.t: What two parameters are displayed full time on the EICAS as primary engine indications?
docs.x: What two parameters are displayed full time on the EICAS as primary engine indications? N1 and EGT Engine Indications Engines deck Engines

docs.t: What does REV displayed in amber mean?
docs.x: What does REV displayed in amber mean? The thrust reverser is in transit Engines deck Engines

docs.t: What does REV displayed in green mean?
docs.x: What does REV displayed in green mean? The thrust reverser is fully deployed Engines deck Engines

docs.t: What color is the Maximum N1 line on the N1 display?
docs.x: What color is the Maximum N1 line on the N1 display? Amber Engines deck Engines

docs.t: When is Reference/Target N1 displayed in magenta (rather than green)?
docs.x: When is Reference/Target N1 displayed in magenta (rather than green)? When VNAV is active and the autothrottle is connected in THR or THR REF mode, or the autothrottle is disconnected Engines deck Engines

docs.t: When does the vibration source display "BB"?
docs.x: When does the vibration source display "BB"? When the vibration source is unknown; average vibration is then displayed Engines deck Engines

docs.t: What does black numbers on a white background on the vibration display indicate?
docs.x: What does black numbers on a white background on the vibration display indicate? High vibration Engines deck Engines

docs.t: Name three conditions that cause automatic display of secondary engine indications.
docs.x: Name three conditions that cause automatic display of secondary engine indications. Any three of: displays initially receive electrical power; FUEL CONTROL switch moved to CUTOFF in flight; engine fire switch pulled in flight; secondary engine parameter exceeded; N2 RPM below idle in flight; start selector in START; FUEL FLOW ENG L/R Advisory shown Engines deck Engines

docs.t: Can automatically-displayed secondary engine indications be cleared while the triggering condition is still present?
docs.x: Can automatically-displayed secondary engine indications be cleared while the triggering condition is still present? No - they cannot be cleared until the condition is no longer present EEC Engines deck Engines

docs.t: How many control modes does the EEC have, and what are they?
docs.x: How many control modes does the EEC have, and what are they? Two - normal mode and alternate mode Engines deck Engines

docs.t: What parameter does the EEC use to control the engine in both normal and alternate modes?
docs.x: What parameter does the EEC use to control the engine in both normal and alternate modes? N1 RPM Engines deck Engines

docs.t: What rotor does the EEC monitor for overspeed protection?
docs.x: What rotor does the EEC monitor for overspeed protection? N2 Engines deck Engines

docs.t: What does the EEC do if N2 overspeed persists after RPM limiting fails?
docs.x: What does the EEC do if N2 overspeed persists after RPM limiting fails? Commands fuel shutoff to shut down the engine; EICAS caution ENG FAIL (L or R) is then displayed with an aural beeper Engines deck Engines

docs.t: What EICAS message indicates RPM limiting is in effect?
docs.x: What EICAS message indicates RPM limiting is in effect? ENG RPM LIMITED (amber caution) Engines deck Engines

docs.t: What are the two static port locations on the fan cowl used as an alternate ADRS source?
docs.x: What are the two static port locations on the fan cowl used as an alternate ADRS source? Lower portion of the fan cowl at the 4 o'clock and 8 o'clock positions Engines deck Engines

docs.t: What powers the EEC during engine start?
docs.x: What powers the EEC during engine start? Airplane power Engines deck Engines

docs.t: What powers the EEC after engine start-up?
docs.x: What powers the EEC after engine start-up? The Permanent Magnet Alternator (PMA) Engines deck Engines

docs.t: What is the backup EEC power source if the PMA fails?
docs.x: What is the backup EEC power source if the PMA fails? Airplane power Engines deck Engines

docs.t: In EEC normal mode, how is maximum rated thrust obtained?
docs.x: In EEC normal mode, how is maximum rated thrust obtained? By moving the thrust levers to the full forward position Engines deck Engines

docs.t: What is the difference between "soft" and "hard" EEC alternate mode?
docs.x: What is the difference between "soft" and "hard" EEC alternate mode? Soft - EEC automatically switches to alternate mode; Hard - ALTN manually selected on the EEC mode switch Engines deck Engines

docs.t: Are autothrottles connected or disconnected when the EEC is in alternate mode?
docs.x: Are autothrottles connected or disconnected when the EEC is in alternate mode? Connected - autothrottles remain connected in both soft and hard alternate mode Engines deck Engines

docs.t: In alternate mode, how does thrust compare to normal mode for the same thrust lever position?
docs.x: In alternate mode, how does thrust compare to normal mode for the same thrust lever position? Equal or greater Engines deck Engines

docs.t: Is thrust protection available in EEC alternate mode?
docs.x: Is thrust protection available in EEC alternate mode? No - thrust protection is not provided in alternate mode Engines deck Engines

docs.t: What hazard exists when the thrust levers are at full forward in alternate mode?
docs.x: What hazard exists when the thrust levers are at full forward in alternate mode? Thrust overboost can occur; maximum rated thrust is reached before full forward lever position Engines deck Engines

docs.t: What EICAS message is displayed if the thrust lever commands N1 greater than maximum rated thrust in alternate mode?
docs.x: What EICAS message is displayed if the thrust lever commands N1 greater than maximum rated thrust in alternate mode? ENG LIMIT PROT (L, R) caution Engines deck Engines

docs.t: Is N1/N2 redline protection available in alternate mode?
docs.x: Is N1/N2 redline protection available in alternate mode? Yes Engines deck Engines

docs.t: What are the three conditions that must ALL be met for the EEC to automatically shut down an engine?
docs.x: What are the three conditions that must ALL be met for the EEC to automatically shut down an engine? Airplane is on the ground, AND thrust lever is at idle, AND engine is above idle speed and not decelerating normally Engines deck Engines

docs.t: When is thrust ramping active?
docs.x: When is thrust ramping active? Only on the ground with the EEC in normal mode Thrust Reverser Engines deck Engines

docs.t: What type of actuation does the B787 thrust reverser use?
docs.x: What type of actuation does the B787 thrust reverser use? Hydraulic Engines deck Engines

docs.t: During what phase(s) of flight is the thrust reverser available?
docs.x: During what phase(s) of flight is the thrust reverser available? Ground only Engines deck Engines

docs.t: What two things happen when the reverse thrust levers are pulled aft to the interlock position?
docs.x: What two things happen when the reverse thrust levers are pulled aft to the interlock position? Autothrottle disengages and auto speedbrakes deploy Engines deck Engines

docs.t: What do the fan flow blocker doors do during reverser operation?
docs.x: What do the fan flow blocker doors do during reverser operation? Rotate into place to direct fan air through stationary cascade guide vanes Fuel Control / Start Engines deck Engines

docs.t: What does moving the FUEL CONTROL switch to RUN do? (three actions)
docs.x: What does moving the FUEL CONTROL switch to RUN do? (three actions) Opens the spar fuel valve; arms the engine fuel valve (EEC opens when required); arms the selected igniters (EEC turns on when required) Engines deck Engines

docs.t: What does moving the FUEL CONTROL switch to CUTOFF do? (three actions)
docs.x: What does moving the FUEL CONTROL switch to CUTOFF do? (three actions) Closes the engine fuel valve (and spar fuel valve if START selector not in START); removes igniter power; unlocks the engine fire switch Engines deck Engines

docs.t: Can B787 engines be started manually (non-autostart)?
docs.x: Can B787 engines be started manually (non-autostart)? No - engines can only be started using the autostart system Engines deck Engines

docs.t: What two power sources can provide starter power?
docs.x: What two power sources can provide starter power? APU and forward external power Engines deck Engines

docs.t: What conditions are required to perform a simultaneous engine start?
docs.x: What conditions are required to perform a simultaneous engine start? APU must be running and both APU starter/generators must be operational Engines deck Engines

docs.t: What happens if both engines are commanded to start with an inadequate power configuration?
docs.x: What happens if both engines are commanded to start with an inadequate power configuration? The second start command is ignored Engines deck Engines

docs.t: Does load shed occur during engine start?
docs.x: Does load shed occur during engine start? Yes - load shed always occurs during engine start Engines deck Engines

docs.t: Name the items that are load-shed during engine start.
docs.x: Name the items that are load-shed during engine start. AIR, CABIN LOADS, COMM/NAV, EXT LIGHTS, FUEL, MISC HEATERS, WINDOW HEAT Engines deck Engines

docs.t: What commands starter cutout during an engine start?
docs.x: What commands starter cutout during an engine start? The EEC, when the engine reaches idle speed; the START selector then releases to NORM Engines deck Engines

docs.t: In the fuel system flow path, what component preheats the fuel?
docs.x: In the fuel system flow path, what component preheats the fuel? The fuel/oil heat exchanger (between first and second stage fuel pumps) Engines deck Engines

docs.t: What is the function of the Fuel Metering Unit (FMU)?
docs.x: What is the function of the Fuel Metering Unit (FMU)? Adjusts fuel flow to meet thrust requirements Engines deck Engines

docs.t: Where is fuel flow measured in the engine fuel system?
docs.x: Where is fuel flow measured in the engine fuel system? After passing through the engine fuel valve Engine Failure / TAP Engines deck Engines

docs.t: On takeoff, between what speeds does a red ENG FAIL appear on the PFDs and HUDs?
docs.x: On takeoff, between what speeds does a red ENG FAIL appear on the PFDs and HUDs? Between 65 knots and 6 knots prior to V1 (when actual thrust is less than commanded thrust) Engines deck Engines

docs.t: What accompanies the red ENG FAIL on the PFD/HUD?
docs.x: What accompanies the red ENG FAIL on the PFD/HUD? Master WARNING lights and voice annunciation "Engine Fail" Engines deck Engines

docs.t: What does the EICAS caution ENG FAIL indicate in flight?
docs.x: What does the EICAS caution ENG FAIL indicate in flight? An engine has unexpectedly decelerated to less than idle speed Engines deck Engines

docs.t: What must happen for the EICAS caution ENG FAIL to clear?
docs.x: What must happen for the EICAS caution ENG FAIL to clear? Engine recovers to above idle speed, or the FUEL CONTROL switch is moved to CUTOFF Engines deck Engines

docs.t: What is Thrust Asymmetry Protection (TAP)?
docs.x: What is Thrust Asymmetry Protection (TAP)? An automatic system that limits thrust on the higher thrust engine during takeoff or go-around; for engine-out, reduces operating engine thrust to ensure sufficient rudder authority Engines deck Engines

docs.t: What two conditions are required for TAP to be available?
docs.x: What two conditions are required for TAP to be available? Flight controls in Normal mode AND EEC in normal or alternate mode Transient Bleed System Engines deck Engines

docs.t: What is the purpose of the Transient Bleed System?
docs.x: What is the purpose of the Transient Bleed System? To unload the compressor during engine acceleration Engines deck Engines

docs.t: What controls the TBV and based on what signal?
docs.x: What controls the TBV and based on what signal? The EEC, based on N2 rotor speed Engines deck Engines

docs.t: When does the EEC command the TBV to open?
docs.x: When does the EEC command the TBV to open? During above idle acceleration Engines deck Engines

docs.t: If the TBV fails open before reverser deployment, what is the result?
docs.x: If the TBV fails open before reverser deployment, what is the result? The associated thrust reverser becomes inhibited Engines deck Engines

docs.t: If the TBV fails open and the reverser is already deployed, what is the result?
docs.x: If the TBV fails open and the reverser is already deployed, what is the result? Thrust reverser deployment is limited to idle (to protect structural integrity from hot gases) EEC Idle Selection Engines deck Engines

docs.t: What are the three EEC idle modes?
docs.x: What are the three EEC idle modes? Minimum idle, approach idle, and icing idle Engines deck Engines

docs.t: When does the EEC select approach idle?
docs.x: When does the EEC select approach idle? When flaps are commanded to 25 or greater, or landing gear is selected DOWN Engines deck Engines

docs.t: What is the benefit of approach idle?
docs.x: What is the benefit of approach idle? Decreases acceleration time for go-around Engines deck Engines

docs.t: When does the EEC transition from approach idle back to minimum idle?
docs.x: When does the EEC transition from approach idle back to minimum idle? After touchdown Engines deck Engines

docs.t: When does the EEC select icing idle?
docs.x: When does the EEC select icing idle? When engine anti-ice is on Ice Crystal Anti-Ice (ICA) Engines deck Engines

docs.t: Is the ICA function automatic or pilot-initiated?
docs.x: Is the ICA function automatic or pilot-initiated? Automatic Engines deck Engines

docs.t: At what altitude does the ICA function activate?
docs.x: At what altitude does the ICA function activate? Only above 30,000 ft Engines deck Engines

docs.t: How long does the ICA function remain active at minimum, and in what increments can it continue?
docs.x: How long does the ICA function remain active at minimum, and in what increments can it continue? At least 30 minutes; may continue in 15-minute increments Engines deck Engines

docs.t: At what altitude does descent terminate the ICA function?
docs.x: At what altitude does descent terminate the ICA function? Below 28,500 ft Engines deck Engines

docs.t: How is ICA activation indicated in the cockpit?
docs.x: How is ICA activation indicated in the cockpit? "ICA" shown in green on the N1 display (one or both engines) Engines deck Engines

docs.t: Does ICA activating on one engine mean the other engine also activates ICA?
docs.x: Does ICA activating on one engine mean the other engine also activates ICA? No - each engine's ICA function is independent; the indication may appear on one, both, or neither Engines deck Engines

docs.t: Does an ICA indication confirm the engine is currently in ICI conditions?
docs.x: Does an ICA indication confirm the engine is currently in ICI conditions? No - an ICA indication does not mean the engine is currently encountering ICI conditions Engines deck Engines

docs.t: After an engine change or EEC change, how long might ICA show in cruise?
docs.x: After an engine change or EEC change, how long might ICA show in cruise? 75 minutes or more, in any weather conditions Engine Oil Engines deck Engines

docs.t: What is the minimum oil quantity limit for the B787 engine?
docs.x: What is the minimum oil quantity limit for the B787 engine? There is no minimum oil quantity limit (no amber or red line limit) Engines deck Engines

docs.t: What are the crew procedures when low oil quantity is displayed?
docs.x: What are the crew procedures when low oil quantity is displayed? There are no flight crew procedures based solely on a response to low oil quantity Engines deck Engines

docs.t: How is low oil quantity displayed on the secondary engine display?
docs.x: How is low oil quantity displayed on the secondary engine display? Automatic display of secondary engine indications; oil quantity shown as black numbers on a white background Engines deck Engines

docs.t: Which zones on the B787 have BOTH fire detection AND fire extinguishing systems?
docs.x: Which zones on the B787 have BOTH fire detection AND fire extinguishing systems? APU, cargo compartments, engines, and lavatories. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: Which zones have fire detection but NO fire extinguishing?
docs.x: Which zones have fire detection but NO fire extinguishing? Main gear wheel wells, overhead flight crew rest compartment, and overhead flight attendant rest compartment. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: Does the nose wheel well have fire or overheat detection?
docs.x: Does the nose wheel well have fire or overheat detection? No. The nose wheel well has no fire or overheat detection system. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: Besides fire detection, what additional detection do the engines have that other zones do not?
docs.x: Besides fire detection, what additional detection do the engines have that other zones do not? Overheat detection. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: What does the FIRE/OVHT TEST switch do when pushed and held?
docs.x: What does the FIRE/OVHT TEST switch do when pushed and held? Sends fire/overheat test signals to the engine, APU, wheel well, and cargo compartment fire detector systems, and tests flight deck fire and overheat indications. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: What EICAS message indicates the engine fire detection system has failed?
docs.x: What EICAS message indicates the engine fire detection system has failed? DET FIRE ENG (L or R) -- advisory. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: What EICAS message indicates the APU fire detection system has failed?
docs.x: What EICAS message indicates the APU fire detection system has failed? DET FIRE APU -- advisory. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: What EICAS message indicates cargo smoke detection is inoperative?
docs.x: What EICAS message indicates cargo smoke detection is inoperative? DET FIRE CARGO (FWD or AFT) -- advisory. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: What happens if a fault is detected in one channel of the engine fire detection system?
docs.x: What happens if a fault is detected in one channel of the engine fire detection system? The system automatically reconfigures for single channel operation; the remaining channel continues to provide fire and overheat detection. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: How many detector channels are in each engine nacelle, and what does each channel detect?
docs.x: How many detector channels are in each engine nacelle, and what does each channel detect? Multiple dual-channel detector assemblies; each channel provides both fire and overheat detection. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: Under normal conditions, what is required to trigger an engine fire warning or overheat caution?
docs.x: Under normal conditions, what is required to trigger an engine fire warning or overheat caution? At least one element on each channel must detect the fire or overheat condition. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: What are the indications of an engine overheat?
docs.x: What are the indications of an engine overheat? Caution beeper sounds; master CAUTION lights illuminate; EICAS caution message OVERHEAT ENG (L or R) displayed. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: What are the indications of an engine fire warning?
docs.x: What are the indications of an engine fire warning? Fire bell sounds; master WARNING lights illuminate; EICAS warning message FIRE ENG (L or R) displayed; engine fire switch warning light illuminates; engine fire switch unlocks; engine FUEL CONTROL switch warning light illuminates. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: Under what two conditions does the engine fire switch automatically unlock?
docs.x: Under what two conditions does the engine fire switch automatically unlock? Automatically on a fire warning, or when the FUEL CONTROL switch is placed to CUTOFF. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: When the engine fire switch is pulled out, what seven actions occur?
docs.x: When the engine fire switch is pulled out, what seven actions occur? (1) Arms both engine fire extinguishers; (2) closes engine and spar fuel valves; (3) closes engine anti-ice valves; (4) trips engine generators off; (5) shuts off hydraulic fluid to engine-driven pump; (6) depressurizes engine-driven hydraulic pump; (7) removes power to thrust reverser isolation valve. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: When the engine fire switch is pulled out, what happens to the fuel system?
docs.x: When the engine fire switch is pulled out, what happens to the fuel system? Closes the associated engine AND spar fuel valves. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: When the engine fire switch is pulled out, what happens to the generators?
docs.x: When the engine fire switch is pulled out, what happens to the generators? Trips the associated engine generators off. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: When the engine fire switch is pulled out, what happens to the hydraulic system?
docs.x: When the engine fire switch is pulled out, what happens to the hydraulic system? Shuts off hydraulic fluid to and depressurizes the associated engine-driven hydraulic pump. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: When the engine fire switch is pulled out, what happens to the thrust reverser?
docs.x: When the engine fire switch is pulled out, what happens to the thrust reverser? Removes power to the thrust reverser isolation valve. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: When the engine fire switch is pulled out, what happens to the fire extinguishers?
docs.x: When the engine fire switch is pulled out, what happens to the fire extinguishers? Arms both engine fire extinguishers. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: How many engine fire extinguisher bottles are there, and how are they discharged?
docs.x: How many engine fire extinguisher bottles are there, and how are they discharged? Two bottles (cross-connected to both engines). The engine fire switch is rotated to position 1 or 2 to discharge the selected bottle. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: What does an amber ENG BTL DISCH light indicate?
docs.x: What does an amber ENG BTL DISCH light indicate? The extinguisher bottle is discharged or has low pressure. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: How many fire detector loops does the APU compartment have?
docs.x: How many fire detector loops does the APU compartment have? Two (dual loops). Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: Does the APU have overheat detection?
docs.x: Does the APU have overheat detection? No. There is no APU overheat detection. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: Under normal conditions, how many APU detector loops must detect a fire to produce a fire warning?
docs.x: Under normal conditions, how many APU detector loops must detect a fire to produce a fire warning? Both loops must detect a fire. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: Under what condition is a single APU detector loop sufficient to cause APU shutdown and bottle discharge?
docs.x: Under what condition is a single APU detector loop sufficient to cause APU shutdown and bottle discharge? On the ground with both engines off -- a signal from either loop is sufficient. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: What are the indications of an APU fire warning?
docs.x: What are the indications of an APU fire warning? Fire bell sounds; master WARNING lights illuminate; EICAS warning message FIRE APU displayed; APU fire switch warning light illuminates; APU fire switch unlocks. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: What automatic actions occur when an APU fire is detected?
docs.x: What automatic actions occur when an APU fire is detected? The APU shuts down immediately; the extinguisher bottle automatically discharges after a 15-second delay to allow the fuel valve to close. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: Why is there a 15-second delay before the APU extinguisher bottle auto-discharges?
docs.x: Why is there a 15-second delay before the APU extinguisher bottle auto-discharges? To allow time for the APU fuel valve to close. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: How many APU fire extinguisher bottles are there?
docs.x: How many APU fire extinguisher bottles are there? One. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: What does rotating the APU fire switch do, and in which direction?
docs.x: What does rotating the APU fire switch do, and in which direction? Discharges the APU fire extinguisher into the APU compartment; rotation in either direction works. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: What two indications confirm the APU extinguisher bottle has discharged or has low pressure?
docs.x: What two indications confirm the APU extinguisher bottle has discharged or has low pressure? APU BTL DISCH light illuminates (amber) and EICAS advisory message BOTTLE DISCH APU is displayed. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: When the APU fire switch is pulled out, what does it do to the APU air inlet?
docs.x: When the APU fire switch is pulled out, what does it do to the APU air inlet? Closes the APU air inlet door. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: When the APU fire switch is pulled out, what does it do to the APU generator?
docs.x: When the APU fire switch is pulled out, what does it do to the APU generator? Trips the APU generator field and generator breaker. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: Does the main wheel well have a fire extinguishing system?
docs.x: Does the main wheel well have a fire extinguishing system? No. There is fire and overheat detection, but no fire extinguishing system. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: What are the indications of a main wheel well fire?
docs.x: What are the indications of a main wheel well fire? Fire bell sounds; master WARNING lights illuminate; EICAS warning message FIRE WHEEL WELL displayed. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: What are the indications of a main wheel well overheat?
docs.x: What are the indications of a main wheel well overheat? Caution beeper sounds; master CAUTION lights illuminate; EICAS caution message OVERHEAT WHEEL WELL displayed. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: How many sensors are in each main wheel well, and how many detectors does each sensor have?
docs.x: How many sensors are in each main wheel well, and how many detectors does each sensor have? Six sensors per well; each sensor has two detectors (A and B). Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: At what wheel well temperature do Spoilers 6 and 9 open to provide cooling?
docs.x: At what wheel well temperature do Spoilers 6 and 9 open to provide cooling? Greater than 140 degrees F. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: What is the Boeing term for the slight opening of Spoilers 6 and 9 for wheel well cooling?
docs.x: What is the Boeing term for the slight opening of Spoilers 6 and 9 for wheel well cooling? Spoiler gap. The spoiler gap draws cooling air into the wheel well. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: How many smoke detectors are installed in the forward cargo compartment?
docs.x: How many smoke detectors are installed in the forward cargo compartment? 18 detectors. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: How many smoke detectors are installed in the aft cargo compartment system, and how are they distributed?
docs.x: How many smoke detectors are installed in the aft cargo compartment system, and how are they distributed? 11 total -- 9 in the aft compartment and 2 in the bulk compartment. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: Is the bulk cargo compartment part of the forward or aft cargo fire detection and extinguishing system?
docs.x: Is the bulk cargo compartment part of the forward or aft cargo fire detection and extinguishing system? Aft cargo. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: Under normal conditions, how many smoke detectors must activate simultaneously to trigger a cargo fire warning?
docs.x: Under normal conditions, how many smoke detectors must activate simultaneously to trigger a cargo fire warning? Two detectors in the same compartment must detect a fire or overheat condition at the same time. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: If one cargo smoke detector fails, how many remaining detectors are required to trigger a fire warning?
docs.x: If one cargo smoke detector fails, how many remaining detectors are required to trigger a fire warning? One -- a single detector is sufficient if one has already failed. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: What are the indications of a cargo compartment fire warning?
docs.x: What are the indications of a cargo compartment fire warning? Fire bell sounds; master WARNING lights illuminate; EICAS warning message FIRE CARGO (FWD or AFT) displayed; CARGO FIRE (FWD or AFT) fire warning light illuminates. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: How many total cargo fire extinguisher bottles are installed?
docs.x: How many total cargo fire extinguisher bottles are installed? Six. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: What cargo fire suppression duration is the system designed for in ETOPS operations?
docs.x: What cargo fire suppression duration is the system designed for in ETOPS operations? 240 minutes. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: In flight, when a cargo fire warning occurs, how many bottles discharge immediately?
docs.x: In flight, when a cargo fire warning occurs, how many bottles discharge immediately? Two bottles discharge immediately at full (total) discharge into the affected compartment. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: In flight, after the 15-minute delay following initial cargo fire bottle discharge, what happens?
docs.x: In flight, after the 15-minute delay following initial cargo fire bottle discharge, what happens? The remaining four bottles discharge at a reduced flow rate into the affected compartment. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: If the aircraft lands within the 15-minute delay period, what happens to the remaining bottles?
docs.x: If the aircraft lands within the 15-minute delay period, what happens to the remaining bottles? One bottle discharges at the reduced rate on touchdown. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: On the ground, if the CARGO FIRE DISCHARGE switch is pushed, how many bottles discharge and how?
docs.x: On the ground, if the CARGO FIRE DISCHARGE switch is pushed, how many bottles discharge and how? Three bottles discharge simultaneously; the third bottle discharges at a reduced (metered) flow rate. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: What are the two indications when the first two cargo extinguisher bottles begin to discharge?
docs.x: What are the two indications when the first two cargo extinguisher bottles begin to discharge? The CARGO FIRE DISCHARGE switch light illuminates, and EICAS advisory message BOTTLE DISCH CARGO is displayed. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: What does arming the CARGO FIRE ARM switch do to the packs?
docs.x: What does arming the CARGO FIRE ARM switch do to the packs? Commands the packs to provide the minimum air flow required to provide pressurization. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: When the AFT CARGO FIRE ARM switch is armed, what happens to the bulk cargo ventilation?
docs.x: When the AFT CARGO FIRE ARM switch is armed, what happens to the bulk cargo ventilation? The bulk cargo compartment ventilation system is shut down (aft cargo arm only). Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: What happens to the NGS when a CARGO FIRE ARM switch is armed?
docs.x: What happens to the NGS when a CARGO FIRE ARM switch is armed? The Nitrogen Generation System (NGS) is turned off. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: What happens to the outflow valves when a CARGO FIRE ARM switch is armed?
docs.x: What happens to the outflow valves when a CARGO FIRE ARM switch is armed? Outflow valves move to a 50/50 flow split for air flow stability. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: What EICAS message indicates smoke in the overhead flight crew rest compartment?
docs.x: What EICAS message indicates smoke in the overhead flight crew rest compartment? SMOKE REST UPR DR 1 -- caution. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: What EICAS message indicates smoke in the overhead flight attendant rest compartment?
docs.x: What EICAS message indicates smoke in the overhead flight attendant rest compartment? SMOKE REST UPR DR 4 -- caution. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: How many smoke detectors does each lavatory have?
docs.x: How many smoke detectors does each lavatory have? One. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: What are the indications when a lavatory smoke detector activates?
docs.x: What are the indications when a lavatory smoke detector activates? Aural alert sounds in the lavatory and in the cabin; lavatory call light flashes; master call light at the associated attendant station illuminates; EICAS advisory message SMOKE LAVATORY displayed. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: How many fire extinguisher bottles does each lavatory have, and how does it discharge?
docs.x: How many fire extinguisher bottles does each lavatory have, and how does it discharge? One bottle; discharges automatically through two nozzles into the waste container. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: Is there a flight deck indication when a lavatory fire extinguisher discharges?
docs.x: Is there a flight deck indication when a lavatory fire extinguisher discharges? No. There is no flight deck indication of lavatory extinguisher discharge. Fire Protection deck Fire Protection

docs.t: What is the signal path in Normal mode?
docs.x: What is the signal path in Normal mode? Pilot inputs > ACEs > PFCs > ACEs > Flight Control Surfaces Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: What is the signal path in Direct mode?
docs.x: What is the signal path in Direct mode? Pilot inputs > ACEs > Flight Control Surfaces (PFCs bypassed) Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: What is the signal path in Secondary mode?
docs.x: What is the signal path in Secondary mode? Pilot inputs > ACEs > PFCs (simplified computations) > ACEs > Flight Control Surfaces Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: What EICAS message indicates Secondary mode is active?
docs.x: What EICAS message indicates Secondary mode is active? FLIGHT CONTROL MODE (advisory) Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: What EICAS message indicates Direct mode is active?
docs.x: What EICAS message indicates Direct mode is active? PRI FLIGHT COMPUTERS (advisory) Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: Can Secondary mode be manually selected?
docs.x: Can Secondary mode be manually selected? No. It cannot be manually selected; it is automatic only. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: Can Direct mode be manually selected?
docs.x: Can Direct mode be manually selected? Yes. Move the Primary Flight Computers switch to DISC (normal position is AUTO). Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: What two conditions automatically trigger Secondary mode?
docs.x: What two conditions automatically trigger Secondary mode? Loss of all slat and flap position data, OR inertial/air data insufficient for Normal mode. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: What triggers automatic reversion to Direct mode?
docs.x: What triggers automatic reversion to Direct mode? All 3 PFCs fail (or are switched off manually). Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: What does the mnemonic AARTS GOD stand for?
docs.x: What does the mnemonic AARTS GOD stand for? Autopilot, Auto speedbrakes, Roll/yaw asymmetry compensation, Tail strike protection, Stall protection, Gust suppression, Overspeed protection, Degraded yaw damper. These are the functions lost in Secondary and Direct modes. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: How does aircraft handling compare between Secondary and Direct modes?
docs.x: How does aircraft handling compare between Secondary and Direct modes? Aircraft handles similarly; the same AARTS GOD functions are lost in both. Flight Control Surfaces Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: How many spoilers does the B787 have total, and how are they numbered?
docs.x: How many spoilers does the B787 have total, and how are they numbered? 14 spoilers (7 per side), numbered 1 through 14. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: How many flap panels are there per wing, and how are they arranged?
docs.x: How many flap panels are there per wing, and how are they arranged? 2 per wing (one inboard, one outboard). Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: How many slats are there per wing, and how are they arranged?
docs.x: How many slats are there per wing, and how are they arranged? 6 per wing (one inboard, five outboard). Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: What is the purpose of the Krueger flap?
docs.x: What is the purpose of the Krueger flap? Provides a seal between the inboard slat and the engine nacelle. One per side, two-position. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: What powers the elevator?
docs.x: What powers the elevator? Hydraulic power. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: What powers the stabilizer?
docs.x: What powers the stabilizer? Electrical power. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: What hydraulic systems power the rudder?
docs.x: What hydraulic systems power the rudder? All three hydraulic systems (and the RAT when deployed). Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: When are ailerons locked out?
docs.x: When are ailerons locked out? At high speeds. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: Is there an aileron trim on the B787?
docs.x: Is there an aileron trim on the B787? No. Roll trim is built into the flight control laws; there is no separate aileron trim. FCS Lock Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: What EICAS message appears when the flight control surfaces lock is engaged?
docs.x: What EICAS message appears when the flight control surfaces lock is engaged? FLT CONTROL LOCKED (advisory) Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: At what groundspeed do flight control surfaces automatically unlock?
docs.x: At what groundspeed do flight control surfaces automatically unlock? Groundspeed greater than 40 knots. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: What does the FAIL light on the FCS lock panel indicate?
docs.x: What does the FAIL light on the FCS lock panel indicate? The surfaces failed to lock. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: What should you always do before moving the FCS lock switch from LOCK to NORM?
docs.x: What should you always do before moving the FCS lock switch from LOCK to NORM? Check with Mx (maintenance) staff. Pitch Control and Trim Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: What does pitch trim do in Normal mode in flight?
docs.x: What does pitch trim do in Normal mode in flight? It changes the Trim Reference Speed. It does NOT directly move the stabilizer. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: What is the Trim Reference Speed?
docs.x: What is the Trim Reference Speed? The airspeed at which the aircraft is stable with no control column inputs. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: In what modes does pitch trim directly move the stabilizer?
docs.x: In what modes does pitch trim directly move the stabilizer? Secondary mode, Direct mode, and on the ground. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: Does trim move the control column?
docs.x: Does trim move the control column? No. Trim never moves the column. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: Is pitch trim available with the autopilot engaged?
docs.x: Is pitch trim available with the autopilot engaged? No. Trim is inhibited with autopilot engaged. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: How do the alternate pitch trim switches differ from the primary trim switches?
docs.x: How do the alternate pitch trim switches differ from the primary trim switches? Alternate trim switches have a direct electrical connection to the stabilizer for backup, but otherwise work exactly like the primary trim switches. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: What buses power the stabilizer control units when STAB switches are in NORM?
docs.x: What buses power the stabilizer control units when STAB switches are in NORM? 235 Vac buses L2 and R2. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: If the stabilizer shuts down or fails in Normal mode, is pitch trim still available?
docs.x: If the stabilizer shuts down or fails in Normal mode, is pitch trim still available? Yes. Pitch trim is still available through the elevators. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: What is the default takeoff trim green band range before FMC data is entered?
docs.x: What is the default takeoff trim green band range before FMC data is entered? 4 to 9 units of trim. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: What is the stabilizer memory item?
docs.x: What is the stabilizer memory item? STAB cutout switches (both) - CUTOUT. Do not exceed the current airspeed. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: For turns up to how many degrees of bank is no aft column pressure needed to maintain altitude?
