docs.x: For turns up to how many degrees of bank is no aft column pressure needed to maintain altitude? Up to 30 degrees of bank. Rudder Trim Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: In which flight control modes is rudder trim available?
docs.x: In which flight control modes is rudder trim available? All 3 modes (Normal, Secondary, Direct). Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: What triggers automatic rudder trim zeroing on takeoff?
docs.x: What triggers automatic rudder trim zeroing on takeoff? Groundspeed exceeds 30 knots. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: When is rudder trim inhibited?
docs.x: When is rudder trim inhibited? With LAND 3 engaged. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: How long is rudder trim shown on EICAS/synoptic after takeoff?
docs.x: How long is rudder trim shown on EICAS/synoptic after takeoff? Until gear up + 10 seconds OR liftoff + 60 seconds. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: Describe the rudder trim rate behavior.
docs.x: Describe the rudder trim rate behavior. Low trim rate initially, then high rate when the selector is rotated past the detent. Speedbrake and Spoiler Operation Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: With speedbrake ARMED, when do spoilers extend on landing?
docs.x: With speedbrake ARMED, when do spoilers extend on landing? When gear trucks untilt AND thrust levers are not in the takeoff range. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: With speedbrake DOWN, when do spoilers extend?
docs.x: With speedbrake DOWN, when do spoilers extend? If thrust levers are moved to idle on takeoff above 85 knots, or whenever reverse idle is selected. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: What automatically causes the speedbrake to retract in flight?
docs.x: What automatically causes the speedbrake to retract in flight? Thrust levers moved forward of 70% full travel. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: What powers the spoilers, and are any electrically powered?
docs.x: What powers the spoilers, and are any electrically powered? Hydraulic power; except two pairs which are electrical. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: Why do spoilers move slightly during engine start and taxi?
docs.x: Why do spoilers move slightly during engine start and taxi? To prevent contact with moving flaps. Flaps and Slats Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: Above what speed and altitude is flap/slat extension inhibited?
docs.x: Above what speed and altitude is flap/slat extension inhibited? Above 260 KIAS or 20,000 feet (primary and secondary mode only). Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: Moving the flap lever to position 1 - what moves?
docs.x: Moving the flap lever to position 1 - what moves? Slats move to the middle position; flaps do not move. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: Moving the flap lever to position 25 - what moves?
docs.x: Moving the flap lever to position 25 - what moves? Slats move to the fully extended position; flaps do not move. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: What hydraulic requirement must be met before flaps move on the ground?
docs.x: What hydraulic requirement must be met before flaps move on the ground? All 3 hydraulic systems must be pressurized. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: What gates are present on the flap lever and what do they prevent?
docs.x: What gates are present on the flap lever and what do they prevent? Gate at flap 20 prevents inadvertent retraction past 20 on a go-around; gate at flap 1 prevents retraction past 1 (slats mid position). Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: What is autogap and when is it available?
docs.x: What is autogap and when is it available? At high AOA with slats in the middle position, slats fully extend to increase lift and margin to stall. Available in Normal mode only, slats in middle position, speed below 240 knots. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: What replaces autogap in Secondary mode, and why?
docs.x: What replaces autogap in Secondary mode, and why? Pregap replaces autogap because the system is too slow for autogap in secondary mode. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: When does pregap keep slats fully extended?
docs.x: When does pregap keep slats fully extended? When the flap lever is not UP and speed is less than 240 knots. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: What flap positions does flap load relief cover?
docs.x: What flap positions does flap load relief cover? Flap positions 15 through 30. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: What is the minimum flap position flap load relief will retract to?
docs.x: What is the minimum flap position flap load relief will retract to? Flap 5 (never less than flap 5). Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: In what mode is flap load relief available?
docs.x: In what mode is flap load relief available? Primary (Normal) mode only. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: What is slat load relief and what triggers it?
docs.x: What is slat load relief and what triggers it? Part of slat pregap functionality; retracts fully extended slats to middle position when airspeed exceeds 240 KIAS. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: In what mode is slat load relief available?
docs.x: In what mode is slat load relief available? Slat secondary mode only. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: What happens to slats after slat load relief when speed decreases below 240 KIAS?
docs.x: What happens to slats after slat load relief when speed decreases below 240 KIAS? For all lever positions except UP, slats are driven back to the extended position. Protections and Automatic Functions Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: In what mode are flight envelope protections available?
docs.x: In what mode are flight envelope protections available? Normal mode only. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: When is tail strike protection active?
docs.x: When is tail strike protection active? During takeoff and landing. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: How does tail strike protection work and can the pilot override it?
docs.x: How does tail strike protection work and can the pilot override it? PFCs decrease elevator deflection to avoid tail contact; no feedback in the control column; pilot can override with continued pitch input. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: What crew action is required for HLFC failures?
docs.x: What crew action is required for HLFC failures? None. There are no crew procedures and no alert messages for HLFC failures. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: In what mode is asymmetry compensation available?
docs.x: In what mode is asymmetry compensation available? Normal mode only. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: During an engine failure above 60 knots groundspeed, what does asymmetry compensation do and do the pedals move?
docs.x: During an engine failure above 60 knots groundspeed, what does asymmetry compensation do and do the pedals move? Most (but not all) yaw is countered; in this situation the pedals DO move. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: During normal takeoff and landing with a crosswind, do the rudder pedals move due to asymmetry compensation?
docs.x: During normal takeoff and landing with a crosswind, do the rudder pedals move due to asymmetry compensation? No. Pedals do not move; the pilot assists in maintaining directional control. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: What two EICAS messages are associated with large or severe yaw asymmetry?
docs.x: What two EICAS messages are associated with large or severe yaw asymmetry? ROLL/YAW ASYMMETRY (large asymmetry); ROLL LEFT/RIGHT AUTHORITY (severe case with limited roll control). Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: What does gust suppression do and in what mode is it available?
docs.x: What does gust suppression do and in what mode is it available? Enhances passenger comfort in gusts/turbulence; Normal mode only; does not move pilot controls. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: What autopilot modes are required for vertical gust suppression?
docs.x: What autopilot modes are required for vertical gust suppression? Altitude hold or VNAV level modes. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: What is autodrag and what control surfaces does it use?
docs.x: What is autodrag and what control surfaces does it use? Assists in glideslope/glidepath capture when on or above the vertical path; deflects ailerons upward and raises the two most outboard spoilers. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: When is autodrag active and when is it removed?
docs.x: When is autodrag active and when is it removed? Normal mode, landing configuration (Flaps 25 or 30, thrust idle); gradually removed below 500 feet AGL. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: What is the Landing Attitude Modifier (LAM)?
docs.x: What is the Landing Attitude Modifier (LAM)? Automatic function that increases pitch and nose gear height when landing flaps are selected at higher speeds, by partially raising lateral control surfaces to reduce lift. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: Are there any EICAS messages or crew procedures associated with LAM?
docs.x: Are there any EICAS messages or crew procedures associated with LAM? No. No associated crew procedures or alert messages. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: What are the operating parameters for cruise flaps?
docs.x: What are the operating parameters for cruise flaps? Normal mode only, above 25,000 feet, between 0.54 and 0.87 Mach. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: What EICAS message indicates a cruise flaps system failure?
docs.x: What EICAS message indicates a cruise flaps system failure? CRUISE FLAPS SYS Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: What is the consequence of a cruise flaps failure in an increased drag condition?
docs.x: What is the consequence of a cruise flaps failure in an increased drag condition? May decrease range. Degraded/Failure Scenarios Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: With total hydraulic power loss, what flight controls remain available?
docs.x: With total hydraulic power loss, what flight controls remain available? The electrically actuated stabilizer and two electric spoiler pairs. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: With complete loss of flight control signaling, what remains for control?
docs.x: With complete loss of flight control signaling, what remains for control? Direct wiring to the stabilizer and a spoiler pair. Use alternate pitch trim for pitch; control wheel for roll. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: What is the wheel-to-rudder cross-tie, and when is it available?
docs.x: What is the wheel-to-rudder cross-tie, and when is it available? A function that reduces maximum sideslip and vertical fin loads; available only in Secondary and Direct modes. Flight Controls deck Flight Controls

docs.t: How far ahead does the Speed Trend Vector predict airspeed?
docs.x: How far ahead does the Speed Trend Vector predict airspeed? 10 seconds, based on current acceleration or deceleration. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What is the height (in knots) of the Selected Speed Bug on the airspeed tape?
docs.x: What is the height (in knots) of the Selected Speed Bug on the airspeed tape? 5 knots. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What does the Selected Speed Bug point to when the MCP IAS/MACH window is blank?
docs.x: What does the Selected Speed Bug point to when the MCP IAS/MACH window is blank? FMC computed airspeed. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What happens to the Selected Speed Bug when selected speed is off scale?
docs.x: What happens to the Selected Speed Bug when selected speed is off scale? The bug is parked at the top or bottom of the tape with only one half the bug visible. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What color does the current airspeed box turn when airspeed is below minimum maneuvering speed?
docs.x: What color does the current airspeed box turn when airspeed is below minimum maneuvering speed? Amber. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What three limiting values determine the Maximum Speed (red/black bar) on the airspeed tape?
docs.x: What three limiting values determine the Maximum Speed (red/black bar) on the airspeed tape? The lowest of: VMO/MMO, landing gear placard speed, or flap placard speed. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: At what bank angle in level flight does 1.3 g maneuver capability occur?
docs.x: At what bank angle in level flight does 1.3 g maneuver capability occur? 40 degrees of bank in level flight. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: VR is displayed as just "R" on the airspeed tape under what condition?
docs.x: VR is displayed as just "R" on the airspeed tape under what condition? When VR is within 4 knots of V1 or V2. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: When are V1 and VR removed from the PFD airspeed tape?
docs.x: When are V1 and VR removed from the PFD airspeed tape? At lift-off. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What are the three conditions that cause V2 to be removed from the airspeed tape?
docs.x: What are the three conditions that cause V2 to be removed from the airspeed tape? (1) When flap retraction begins; (2) after 10 minutes have passed without flap lever movement; (3) after VREF has been selected for a turn-back. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What is displayed on the airspeed tape if V speeds are not entered on the CDU?
docs.x: What is displayed on the airspeed tape if V speeds are not entered on the CDU? NO VSPD. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: At approximately what altitude are flap maneuvering speeds no longer displayed on the PFD?
docs.x: At approximately what altitude are flap maneuvering speeds no longer displayed on the PFD? Above approximately 20,000 ft. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: When does the minimum maneuvering speed (top of amber bar) first appear on the airspeed tape?
docs.x: When does the minimum maneuvering speed (top of amber bar) first appear on the airspeed tape? With the first flap retraction after takeoff. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What is the minimum speed indicator (bottom of the amber band)?
docs.x: What is the minimum speed indicator (bottom of the amber band)? The airspeed where stick shaker activates. PFD - Attitude Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: At what bank angle does the bank pointer fill and turn amber?
docs.x: At what bank angle does the bank pointer fill and turn amber? 35 degrees or more. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What is the maximum positive value to which the Pitch Limit Indication is limited?
docs.x: What is the maximum positive value to which the Pitch Limit Indication is limited? +30 degrees. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: In what increments is the pitch scale marked on the PFD attitude display?
docs.x: In what increments is the pitch scale marked on the PFD attitude display? 2.5 degree increments. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What are the bank scale mark values on the PFD?
docs.x: What are the bank scale mark values on the PFD? 0, 10, 20, 30, 45, and 60 degrees. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: Under what conditions is the Pitch Limit Indication displayed?
docs.x: Under what conditions is the Pitch Limit Indication displayed? When flaps are not up, or at slow speeds with flaps up. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What color does the slip/skid indication turn when bank angle reaches 35 degrees?
docs.x: What color does the slip/skid indication turn when bank angle reaches 35 degrees? Amber. PFD - Steering / FPV Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What two conditions cause the Flight Path Vector (FPV) to display on the PFD?
docs.x: What two conditions cause the Flight Path Vector (FPV) to display on the PFD? FPV selected on the EFIS control panel, or FPA selected on the MCP. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What are the bank and pitch angle limits for the Horizon Line Heading Scale to display?
docs.x: What are the bank and pitch angle limits for the Horizon Line Heading Scale to display? Bank angle less than 50 degrees AND absolute pitch angle less than 20 degrees. PFD - Radio Altitude / Rising Runway Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: Below what altitude does the Radio Altitude display appear on the PFD?
docs.x: Below what altitude does the Radio Altitude display appear on the PFD? Below 2,500 ft AGL. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: For how long is the Radio Altitude display box highlighted white when passing below 2,500 ft?
docs.x: For how long is the Radio Altitude display box highlighted white when passing below 2,500 ft? 10 seconds. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What color does the Radio Altitude display turn when below radio altitude minimums?
docs.x: What color does the Radio Altitude display turn when below radio altitude minimums? Amber. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: When does the Rising Runway symbol move toward the airplane symbol?
docs.x: When does the Rising Runway symbol move toward the airplane symbol? Below 200 ft radio altitude. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: When does the stem of the Rising Runway symbol flash?
docs.x: When does the stem of the Rising Runway symbol flash? When localizer deviations cause the diamond to flash. PFD - Altitude Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: How far ahead does the Altitude Trend Vector predict altitude?
docs.x: How far ahead does the Altitude Trend Vector predict altitude? 6 seconds, based on current vertical speed. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: In what increments does the altitude display in meters when MTRS is selected?
docs.x: In what increments does the altitude display in meters when MTRS is selected? 10 meter increments. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: At what range from selected altitude does the current altitude box turn white?
docs.x: At what range from selected altitude does the current altitude box turn white? Between 900 ft and 200 ft prior to reaching the selected altitude. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: When does the current altitude box turn amber?
docs.x: When does the current altitude box turn amber? When deviating beyond 200 ft from selected altitude. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What happens to the amber altitude box highlight if the deviation continues beyond 900 ft?
docs.x: What happens to the amber altitude box highlight if the deviation continues beyond 900 ft? The amber highlight is removed. PFD - Landing Altitude / Minimums Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What does the white portion of the Landing Altitude Reference Bar indicate?
docs.x: What does the white portion of the Landing Altitude Reference Bar indicate? 500 to 1,000 ft above landing altitude. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What does the amber portion of the Landing Altitude Reference Bar indicate?
docs.x: What does the amber portion of the Landing Altitude Reference Bar indicate? 0 to 500 ft above landing altitude (height above touchdown). Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: How long does the Minimums annunciation flash when the airplane descends below selected minimums?
docs.x: How long does the Minimums annunciation flash when the airplane descends below selected minimums? 3 seconds. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.x: How long does the departure runway/airport landing altitude remain displayed on the PFD? Until 400 NM or one-half the distance to the destination, whichever occurs first. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What does BARO minimums represent in feet?
docs.x: What does BARO minimums represent in feet? Feet MSL. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What does RADIO minimums represent in feet?
docs.x: What does RADIO minimums represent in feet? Radio altitude feet AGL. PFD - Barometric Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: When both Flight Directors are turned on, which barometric source is used for the autopilot/flight director?
docs.x: When both Flight Directors are turned on, which barometric source is used for the autopilot/flight director? L (left EFIS control panel) is displayed. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What does the UL annunciation next to the barometric preselect field indicate?
docs.x: What does the UL annunciation next to the barometric preselect field indicate? A barometric setting uplink has been accepted. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: When is the barometric setting boxed in amber?
docs.x: When is the barometric setting boxed in amber? If a barometric setting is set and altitude climbs above transition altitude, or if STD is set and altitude descends below the transition flight level. NPS / Navigation Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What shape is the NPS Deviation Pointer?

docs.t: When does the NPS Deviation Pointer become unfilled?

docs.t: On what scale is the NPS vertical deviation pointer only displayed?
docs.x: On what scale is the NPS vertical deviation pointer only displayed? Only in the descent phase of flight. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: After how long in the bar area does the NPS pointer begin to flash, and for how long does it flash?
docs.x: After how long in the bar area does the NPS pointer begin to flash, and for how long does it flash? After 5 seconds in the bar area; it flashes for 10 seconds. Navigation Display Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What ND range triggers automatic Airport Map display?

docs.x: What ANP value is required for Airport Map to display automatically? 0.02 NM or less. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: In ND Plan mode, what is the orientation of the display?
docs.x: In ND Plan mode, what is the orientation of the display? True North up. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What ND annunciation appears when predictive windshear is detected but weather radar is not displayed?
docs.x: What ND annunciation appears when predictive windshear is detected but weather radar is not displayed? MONITOR RADAR DISP. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What is the symbol for GPS position on the ND?

docs.t: What is the symbol for IRU position on the ND?

docs.x: What color represents terrain at Reference Altitude + 2,000 ft on the TERR display? High Density Red. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What color represents terrain at Reference Altitude + 1,000 ft on the TERR display?
docs.x: What color represents terrain at Reference Altitude + 1,000 ft on the TERR display? High Density Amber. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.x: At what time from projected terrain impact does the voice "CAUTION OBSTACLE" sound? 40 to 60 seconds from projected impact. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: Where is the TERR indication displayed when the TERR switch is selected ON?
docs.x: Where is the TERR indication displayed when the TERR switch is selected ON? On the left side of the NDs and mini-maps. GND PROX Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.x: What switch inhibits the below-glideslope alert, and at what altitude is it triggered? The GND PROX G/S INHIBIT switch on the ATP; triggered below 1,000 ft RA. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What callout occurs 500 ft above minimums?
