docs.x: What does the ENG switch on the DSP do? Toggles the display of secondary engine information on the EICAS display. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What does the EICAS transfer switch on the DSP do?
docs.x: What does the EICAS transfer switch on the DSP do? Toggles the EICAS display between the inboard half of the Captain and First Officer inboard DUs. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What display switches are available on the DSP for MFD window selection?
docs.x: What display switches are available on the DSP for MFD window selection? SYS, CDU, INFO, CHKL, COMM, or ND. ISFD Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What information does the ISFD display?
docs.x: What information does the ISFD display? Attitude, airspeed, altitude, ILS, GLS, and heading. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What is the airspeed and altitude source for the ISFD?
docs.x: What is the airspeed and altitude source for the ISFD? The center pitot and static air data modules. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What is the attitude source for the ISFD?
docs.x: What is the attitude source for the ISFD? Internal inertial sensors. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What is the ILS/GLS source for the ISFD?
docs.x: What is the ILS/GLS source for the ISFD? The left INR receiver. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What ISFD message requires the crew to push the Attitude Reset switch?
docs.x: What ISFD message requires the crew to push the Attitude Reset switch? ATT:RST. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What message displays during the attitude reset process?
docs.x: What message displays during the attitude reset process? ATT 10s. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What are the requirements for performing an ISFD attitude reset in flight?
docs.x: What are the requirements for performing an ISFD attitude reset in flight? Wings level, non-accelerated flight maintained for 10 seconds. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What are the requirements for performing an ISFD attitude reset on the ground?
docs.x: What are the requirements for performing an ISFD attitude reset on the ground? The airplane must be stationary. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: If the ISFD attitude reset is unsuccessful, what happens?
docs.x: If the ISFD attitude reset is unsuccessful, what happens? The ATT:RST message remains displayed and attitude is not shown. Radio Altimeter Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: How many RA systems does the B787 have?
docs.x: How many RA systems does the B787 have? Two - left and right. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What EICAS message displays if both RA systems are inoperative or degraded?
docs.x: What EICAS message displays if both RA systems are inoperative or degraded? RADIO ALTIMETER L+R (advisory). Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What additional indication appears on the PFD and HUD if both RA systems fail?
docs.x: What additional indication appears on the PFD and HUD if both RA systems fail? "RA" is displayed on both PFD and HUD. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What systems receive data from the RA systems?
docs.x: What systems receive data from the RA systems? Autopilot, Autothrottle, GPWS, TCAS, Weather Radar, and Primary Flight Control System. AUX Display Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What information is displayed in the upper portion of the AUX display?
docs.x: What information is displayed in the upper portion of the AUX display? Flight number, UTC time, MIC readout, date, transponder code, elapsed flight time, SELCAL, chrono dial and readout, and airplane tail number. AOA Speed Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: When is AOA SPD automatically displayed?
docs.x: When is AOA SPD automatically displayed? When pitot and/or static pressure from the ADRS is erroneous or unavailable (NAV AIRSPEED DATA or NAV AIR DATA SYS condition), or when both pilots manually select the AIR DATA/ATT source selector to ALTN. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What flight control law change occurs when AOA SPD is displayed?
docs.x: What flight control law change occurs when AOA SPD is displayed? Simplified flight control laws are used, which may result in increased pitch control sensitivity to abrupt pitch inputs. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: To what values are maximum speed indications reduced when AOA SPD is active?
docs.x: To what values are maximum speed indications reduced when AOA SPD is active? From 360 kt / 0.90 M reduced to 300 kt / 0.85 M. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: How many TAT sensor inputs does the ADRS use?
docs.x: How many TAT sensor inputs does the ADRS use? 6 inputs. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What is the ADRS TAT source when on the ground below 50 kts CAS?
docs.x: What is the ADRS TAT source when on the ground below 50 kts CAS? Sensors in the CAC inlets; ADRS selects the lower of the two CAC inlet temperatures (two sensors per inlet). Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: To what factors is AOA SPD subject to indication variations?
docs.x: To what factors is AOA SPD subject to indication variations? Configuration changes, maneuvering, and speedbrake use. VSD Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: How is the VSD selected for display?
docs.x: How is the VSD selected for display? From the map information selections on the MAP mode drop-down menu. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What is the range of the full-display VSD?
docs.x: What is the range of the full-display VSD? Twice the ND range - from 10 NM to 2,560 NM. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: Up to what ND range does the VSD depict a consistent 3-degree glidepath?
docs.x: Up to what ND range does the VSD depict a consistent 3-degree glidepath? 80 NM range. Checklists Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What are the 10 normal checklists in sequence?
docs.x: What are the 10 normal checklists in sequence? PREFLIGHT, BEFORE START, BEFORE TAXI, BEFORE TAKEOFF, AFTER TAKEOFF, DESCENT, APPROACH, LANDING, SHUTDOWN, SECURE. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What EICAS message alerts crew that a critical normal checklist line item is incomplete before the corresponding phase of flight?
docs.x: What EICAS message alerts crew that a critical normal checklist line item is incomplete before the corresponding phase of flight? CHKL INCOMPLETE NORM (caution). Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What does the normal checklist key color change to when a normal checklist is incomplete?
docs.x: What does the normal checklist key color change to when a normal checklist is incomplete? Amber. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What is the checklist icon on an EICAS alert message?
docs.x: What is the checklist icon on an EICAS alert message? A white box to the left of the message. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What does no checklist icon on an EICAS message indicate?
docs.x: What does no checklist icon on an EICAS message indicate? The checklist is complete, there is no checklist for the message, or another checklist inhibits the icon. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What EICAS message displays when a non-normal checklist is in the queue, the EICAS message is blank, and ECL is not open?
docs.x: What EICAS message displays when a non-normal checklist is in the queue, the EICAS message is blank, and ECL is not open? CHKL NON-NORMAL (advisory). Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What color does an action item show when it is overridden or inactive?
docs.x: What color does an action item show when it is overridden or inactive? Cyan. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What color does an action item show when complete?
docs.x: What color does an action item show when complete? Green. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: When is the use of RESET NON-NORMAL or RESET ALL not recommended?
docs.x: When is the use of RESET NON-NORMAL or RESET ALL not recommended? In flight. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What is the checklist priority on the ground with both fuel control switches CUTOFF?
docs.x: What is the checklist priority on the ground with both fuel control switches CUTOFF? (1) Checklists for EICAS warning messages; (2) NORMAL checklists. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: In what order do checklists appear in the non-normal checklist queue?
docs.x: In what order do checklists appear in the non-normal checklist queue? Same order as the messages appear on EICAS; unannunciated checklists appear after all annunciated checklists. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What happens to a completed non-normal checklist when its EICAS alert message remains active?
docs.x: What happens to a completed non-normal checklist when its EICAS alert message remains active? The EICAS message can still show but the checklist is removed from the queue. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: How can an unannunciated non-normal checklist be removed from the queue without completing it?
docs.x: How can an unannunciated non-normal checklist be removed from the queue without completing it? The checklist must be overridden. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What is a consequential EICAS alert message?
docs.x: What is a consequential EICAS alert message? An alert message caused by a primary failure condition rather than a separate system failure; crews should do the checklist for the primary message, not the consequential message. Video Surveillance Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What action will disable the video surveillance cameras outside the flight deck entrance?
docs.x: What action will disable the video surveillance cameras outside the flight deck entrance? Selecting the flight deck IFE/PASS SEATS power switch OFF. Flight Instruments deck Flight Instruments

docs.t: What activates the HUD projector and displays symbology?
docs.x: What activates the HUD projector and displays symbology? Deploying the combiner. There is no ON/OFF switch. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: How do you manually adjust HUD brightness?
docs.x: How do you manually adjust HUD brightness? Pull the brightness control out, then rotate it. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: How do you set automatic brightness adjustment on the HUD?
docs.x: How do you set automatic brightness adjustment on the HUD? Push the brightness control in, set the initial level by rotating, and brightness then adjusts automatically with changing background lighting. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: What message appears if the HUD combiner is not properly aligned with the projector?
docs.x: What message appears if the HUD combiner is not properly aligned with the projector? ALIGN HUD -- displayed left or right of the airplane symbol on the combiner screen. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: Is the locking lever required when stowing the HUD combiner?
docs.x: Is the locking lever required when stowing the HUD combiner? No. Lift the combiner up and back until the latch engages; the locking lever is not required for stowing. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: What is the purpose of the combiner breakaway position?
docs.x: What is the purpose of the combiner breakaway position? To prevent the pilot's head from impacting the combiner during a sudden and sustained deceleration. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: How do you release the combiner from the breakaway position?
docs.x: How do you release the combiner from the breakaway position? Push forward to relieve pressure on the latch, slide the locking lever to the right, then reposition to desired position. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: Because the HUD is monochromatic, how are amber color alerts from the PFD conveyed on the HUD?
docs.x: Because the HUD is monochromatic, how are amber color alerts from the PFD conveyed on the HUD? Through flashing, shape filling/blanking, and highlight box symbology. Some alerts have no distinct HUD equivalent. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: Is the partial compass rose displayed in full symbology mode during ground operations?
docs.x: Is the partial compass rose displayed in full symbology mode during ground operations? No. The partial compass rose is not displayed in full symbology mode during ground operations. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: What does decluttered mode do to airspeed and altitude information?
docs.x: What does decluttered mode do to airspeed and altitude information? Eliminates the tapes and shows digital values only. The partial compass rose is also removed. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: How do you toggle between full symbology and decluttered modes on the HUD?
docs.x: How do you toggle between full symbology and decluttered modes on the HUD? Using the symbology switch on the pilot's yoke control wheel. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: At what radio altitude does the guidance cue appear on a normal (non-HUD) takeoff?
docs.x: At what radio altitude does the guidance cue appear on a normal (non-HUD) takeoff? 50 feet RA. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: When does the guidance cue appear if a HUD takeoff has been selected?
docs.x: When does the guidance cue appear if a HUD takeoff has been selected? At the same time as the flight path vector (not delayed to 50 ft RA). HUD deck HUD

docs.t: How does the guidance cue change during a windshear alert?
docs.x: How does the guidance cue change during a windshear alert? It changes from hollow to solid (filled). HUD deck HUD

docs.t: To follow flight director guidance on the HUD, how should you position the flight path vector symbol?
docs.x: To follow flight director guidance on the HUD, how should you position the flight path vector symbol? Position the circular body of the flight path vector symbol around the guidance cue (small circle). HUD deck HUD

docs.t: During a takeoff roll, at what ground speed does the TO/GA reference line (pitch target) become visible?
docs.x: During a takeoff roll, at what ground speed does the TO/GA reference line (pitch target) become visible? When ground speed is greater than 65 knots. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: In TO/GA mode, what must you do to comply with vertical flight director guidance on the HUD?
docs.x: In TO/GA mode, what must you do to comply with vertical flight director guidance on the HUD? Place the airplane reference symbol on the TO/GA reference line (horizontal dashed line). HUD deck HUD

docs.t: For HUD takeoff ground deviation indications to become active, what two conditions must be met?
docs.x: For HUD takeoff ground deviation indications to become active, what two conditions must be met? (1) Airplane heading within 45 degrees of runway heading, AND (2) airplane within 2 degrees of the ILS localizer centerline. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: What happens when the airplane deviates more than 7 meters (23 feet) from the runway centerline during a HUD takeoff?
docs.x: What happens when the airplane deviates more than 7 meters (23 feet) from the runway centerline during a HUD takeoff? A flashing triangle appears, pointing in the direction of the runway centerline to assist in correction. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: Where is HUD takeoff guidance selected?
docs.x: Where is HUD takeoff guidance selected? On the FMC. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: What are the projected runway dimensions used for the HUD runway edge lines symbol?
docs.x: What are the projected runway dimensions used for the HUD runway edge lines symbol? 8,000 feet long by 200 feet wide. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: What is the runway edge lines centerline based on?
docs.x: What is the runway edge lines centerline based on? The localizer course, not the geographic orientation of the runway. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: At what radio altitude are runway edge lines enabled, and when are they removed?
docs.x: At what radio altitude are runway edge lines enabled, and when are they removed? Enabled at 300 feet RA; removed at 60 feet. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: In which HUD display mode do runway edge lines appear?
docs.x: In which HUD display mode do runway edge lines appear? Decluttered mode only. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: If radio altitude is unavailable, what does the runway edge lines system use instead?
docs.x: If radio altitude is unavailable, what does the runway edge lines system use instead? Barometric altitude above touchdown. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: What do the two tick marks on the runway edge lines symbol represent?
docs.x: What do the two tick marks on the runway edge lines symbol represent? The touchdown aiming point (glideslope intercept point). HUD deck HUD

docs.t: During approach, how is the glideslope angle shown on the HUD?
docs.x: During approach, how is the glideslope angle shown on the HUD? As a horizontal dashed line across the HUD pitch scale, with the numerical glideslope angle value digitally displayed adjacent to the line. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: How do you use the glideslope reference line during a visual approach?
docs.x: How do you use the glideslope reference line during a visual approach? Overlay the glideslope reference line on the runway touchdown zone and maintain the flight path vector symbol on the glideslope reference line. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: When does the ground deceleration scale appear during a takeoff?
docs.x: When does the ground deceleration scale appear during a takeoff? It is not initially displayed, but appears if deceleration is sensed when ground speed is above 50 knots and the airplane is still on the ground. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: What three conditions cause the ground deceleration scale to be removed?
docs.x: What three conditions cause the ground deceleration scale to be removed? Ground speed decreases below 25 knots, the airplane begins accelerating, or the airplane lifts off. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: What autobrake settings does the ground deceleration scale reference?
docs.x: What autobrake settings does the ground deceleration scale reference? 1, 2, 3, 4, and MAX AUTO. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: When is the flight path slip/skid indicator displayed?
docs.x: When is the flight path slip/skid indicator displayed? Only during a takeoff or a low-altitude go-around. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: What is the purpose of the flight path slip/skid indicator?
docs.x: What is the purpose of the flight path slip/skid indicator? To provide additional yaw reference in the case of an engine failure. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: How is a TCAS corrective advisory depicted on the HUD?
docs.x: How is a TCAS corrective advisory depicted on the HUD? As a double lined box called the "fly-to box," showing where to position the flight path vector to obtain vertical separation from traffic. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: On the HUD NAV Performance Scales, what do the outer tic marks represent?
docs.x: On the HUD NAV Performance Scales, what do the outer tic marks represent? RNP (Required Navigation Performance). HUD deck HUD

docs.t: On the HUD NAV Performance Scales, what do the bars represent?
docs.x: On the HUD NAV Performance Scales, what do the bars represent? ANP (Actual Navigation Performance). HUD deck HUD

docs.t: What does the area between the ANP bars on the NPS indicate?
docs.x: What does the area between the ANP bars on the NPS indicate? The margin available to remain within RNP criteria. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: When do the bars on the NPS vertical scale display?
docs.x: When do the bars on the NPS vertical scale display? Only during the FMC descent phase of flight. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: During an ILS approach with LNAV or VNAV active (or LNAV armed), when are NPS indications removed?
docs.x: During an ILS approach with LNAV or VNAV active (or LNAV armed), when are NPS indications removed? At localizer or glideslope capture. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: What is the appearance of the HUD localizer pointer when it first appears?
docs.x: What is the appearance of the HUD localizer pointer when it first appears? Unfilled diamond. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: When does the HUD localizer pointer become a filled diamond?
docs.x: When does the HUD localizer pointer become a filled diamond? When within 2.5 dots from the center. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: When does the expanded localizer scale display?
docs.x: When does the expanded localizer scale display? When the autopilot or flight director is in LOC mode and the airplane is close to runway centerline. Also displays during HUD takeoff operations. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: What deviation does one rectangle equal on the expanded localizer scale?
docs.x: What deviation does one rectangle equal on the expanded localizer scale? 0.5 dot deviation. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: What is the appearance of the HUD glideslope pointer when it first appears?
docs.x: What is the appearance of the HUD glideslope pointer when it first appears? Unfilled diamond. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: When does the HUD glideslope pointer become a filled diamond?
docs.x: When does the HUD glideslope pointer become a filled diamond? When within 2.5 dots from the scale center. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: What does a hollow landing altitude reference bar indicate?
docs.x: What does a hollow landing altitude reference bar indicate? The airplane is 500 to 1,000 feet above landing altitude. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: What does a filled landing altitude reference bar indicate?
docs.x: What does a filled landing altitude reference bar indicate? The airplane is 0 to 500 feet above landing altitude. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: How does the BARO minimums line behave when the airplane descends below minimums?
docs.x: How does the BARO minimums line behave when the airplane descends below minimums? It flashes for 3 seconds, then goes steady. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: What units are used for BARO minimums on the HUD?
docs.x: What units are used for BARO minimums on the HUD? Feet MSL. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: What units are used for RADIO minimums on the HUD?
docs.x: What units are used for RADIO minimums on the HUD? Radio altitude feet AGL. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: How does the minimums reference display behave when descending below selected minimum altitude?
docs.x: How does the minimums reference display behave when descending below selected minimum altitude? Flashes for 3 seconds, then goes steady. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: What does the flight path acceleration symbol above the wing of the flight path vector indicate?
docs.x: What does the flight path acceleration symbol above the wing of the flight path vector indicate? The airplane is accelerating. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: What does the flight path acceleration symbol below the wing of the flight path vector indicate?
docs.x: What does the flight path acceleration symbol below the wing of the flight path vector indicate? The airplane is decelerating. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: When is the flight path acceleration symbol removed from the HUD display?
docs.x: When is the flight path acceleration symbol removed from the HUD display? When a low-level, decreasing performance windshear is detected below 400 ft AGL. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: What is the reference airspeed used by the speed error tape on takeoff?
docs.x: What is the reference airspeed used by the speed error tape on takeoff? V2. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: What is the flight director guidance airspeed on takeoff (relevant to the speed error tape)?
docs.x: What is the flight director guidance airspeed on takeoff (relevant to the speed error tape)? V2 + 15 knots. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: Why is the speed error tape not displayed immediately on takeoff?
docs.x: Why is the speed error tape not displayed immediately on takeoff? To prevent incorrect interpretation -- it is not displayed until the first flap retraction. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: What is the maximum error the speed error tape can display?
docs.x: What is the maximum error the speed error tape can display? 15 knots. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: If indicated airspeed is faster than selected speed, which direction does the speed error tape symbol move?
docs.x: If indicated airspeed is faster than selected speed, which direction does the speed error tape symbol move? Rises above the wing. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: If indicated airspeed is slower than selected speed, which direction does the speed error tape symbol move?
docs.x: If indicated airspeed is slower than selected speed, which direction does the speed error tape symbol move? Falls below the wing. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: At what pitch angle does the downward pointing pitch scale chevron appear?
docs.x: At what pitch angle does the downward pointing pitch scale chevron appear? +30 degrees (excessively high pitch). HUD deck HUD

docs.t: At what pitch angle does the upward pointing pitch scale chevron appear?
docs.x: At what pitch angle does the upward pointing pitch scale chevron appear? -20 degrees (excessively low pitch). HUD deck HUD

docs.t: What is the purpose of pitch scale chevrons?
docs.x: What is the purpose of pitch scale chevrons? To direct the pilot to pitch the airplane back toward the horizon when at excessively high or low pitch angles. HUD deck HUD

docs.t: How many hydraulic systems does the B787 have, and are they interconnected?
docs.x: How many hydraulic systems does the B787 have, and are they interconnected? 3 systems (Left, Center, Right); they are NOT connected to each other. Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: What is the rated pressure of each B787 hydraulic system?
docs.x: What is the rated pressure of each B787 hydraulic system? 5000 psi. Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: What are the reservoir capacities for the Left, Center, and Right hydraulic systems?
docs.x: What are the reservoir capacities for the Left, Center, and Right hydraulic systems? Left = 5 gal; Center = 11 gal; Right = 5 gal. Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: What does a reservoir QTY indication of 1.00 represent?
docs.x: What does a reservoir QTY indication of 1.00 represent? Normal service level (100% of normal fill level). Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: What color and abbreviation is displayed when hydraulic reservoir quantity is low?
docs.x: What color and abbreviation is displayed when hydraulic reservoir quantity is low? Amber - LO. Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: What does OF (white) mean on the hydraulic synoptic?
docs.x: What does OF (white) mean on the hydraulic synoptic? Reservoir is over-full. Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: What does RF (white) mean on the hydraulic synoptic?
docs.x: What does RF (white) mean on the hydraulic synoptic? Reservoir requires refilling. Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: Are OF and RF reservoir indications inhibited in flight?
docs.x: Are OF and RF reservoir indications inhibited in flight? Yes, both OF and RF are inhibited in-flight. Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: Is the LO reservoir quantity indication inhibited in flight?
docs.x: Is the LO reservoir quantity indication inhibited in flight? No - LO is NOT inhibited in flight, and an ECL must be accomplished. Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: Where are LO hydraulic quantity indications displayed?
docs.x: Where are LO hydraulic quantity indications displayed? EICAS, STATUS page, and Hydraulic synoptic. Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: Where are LOAD SHED indications displayed?
docs.x: Where are LOAD SHED indications displayed? On the Hydraulic synoptic page. Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: What type of primary pump does the Left hydraulic system use?
docs.x: What type of primary pump does the Left hydraulic system use? Engine Driven Pump (EDP). Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: What type of primary pump does the Right hydraulic system use?
docs.x: What type of primary pump does the Right hydraulic system use? Engine Driven Pump (EDP). Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: What type of pumps does the Center hydraulic system use?
docs.x: What type of pumps does the Center hydraulic system use? Two Electric Motor Pumps (EMPs) operating at 235V AC - designated C-1 and C-2. Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: How do C-1 and C-2 center pumps relate to each other?
docs.x: How do C-1 and C-2 center pumps relate to each other? They alternate between acting as primary (operates continuously) and demand (operates during high demand) pump. Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: What are the three conditions that illuminate a hydraulic pump FAULT light?
docs.x: What are the three conditions that illuminate a hydraulic pump FAULT light? Low pump pressure; excessive fluid temperature; pump selected OFF. Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: What components does the Left hydraulic system power?
docs.x: What components does the Left hydraulic system power? Flight controls, left engine thrust reverser, and left and right wing spoilers. Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: What components does the Right hydraulic system power?
docs.x: What components does the Right hydraulic system power? Flight controls, right engine thrust reverser, and right and left wing spoilers. Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: What components does the Center hydraulic system power?
docs.x: What components does the Center hydraulic system power? Flight controls, nose gear actuation and steering, main landing gear actuation, spoilers, leading edge slats, and trailing edge flaps. Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: What is the purpose of L/R Electric Motor Demand Pumps (EMPs)?
docs.x: What is the purpose of L/R Electric Motor Demand Pumps (EMPs)? Augment hydraulic power during high load demands and provide redundancy if the primary EDP fails. Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: In AUTO, when do the L/R demand pumps operate?
docs.x: In AUTO, when do the L/R demand pumps operate? When primary (EDP) pressure is low, or when the system anticipates a large demand. Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: How long do L/R demand pumps run after the second engine is started?
docs.x: How long do L/R demand pumps run after the second engine is started? First 3 minutes. Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: During takeoff, when do L/R demand pumps activate and deactivate?
docs.x: During takeoff, when do L/R demand pumps activate and deactivate? Activate at takeoff thrust set; deactivate when flaps are retracted. Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: During landing, what triggers L/R demand pump activation?
docs.x: During landing, what triggers L/R demand pump activation? Gear lever placed DOWN OR radio altitude less than 1000 feet. Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: During landing rollout, at what groundspeed do L/R demand pumps stop?
docs.x: During landing rollout, at what groundspeed do L/R demand pumps stop? Less than 40 knots (or when thrust reversers are no longer operating). Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: What additional trigger activates center demand pumps that does NOT apply to L/R demand pumps?
docs.x: What additional trigger activates center demand pumps that does NOT apply to L/R demand pumps? Anytime flaps or slats are in motion. Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: During takeoff, when do center demand pumps deactivate? How does this differ from L/R?
docs.x: During takeoff, when do center demand pumps deactivate? How does this differ from L/R? Center: radio altitude exceeds 2000 ft. L/R: flaps retracted. (Center uses RA, L/R uses flap position.) Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: During landing, what triggers center demand pump activation? How does this differ from L/R?
docs.x: During landing, what triggers center demand pump activation? How does this differ from L/R? Center: gear lever DOWN AND RA less than 2000 ft (both conditions required). L/R: gear lever DOWN OR RA less than 1000 ft (either condition sufficient). Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: During landing rollout, at what groundspeed do center demand pumps stop?
docs.x: During landing rollout, at what groundspeed do center demand pumps stop? Less than 60 knots. Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: What is the difference in landing approach logic between L/R and center demand pumps?
docs.x: What is the difference in landing approach logic between L/R and center demand pumps? L/R uses OR logic (gear down OR RA <1000 ft); center uses AND logic (gear down AND RA <2000 ft). Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: What type of valves does the Left/Right system use for non-normal conditions?
docs.x: What type of valves does the Left/Right system use for non-normal conditions? Shutoff valves (SOV). Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: What type of valves does the Center system use for non-normal conditions?
docs.x: What type of valves does the Center system use for non-normal conditions? Isolation valves (ISLN). Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: What happens to the hydraulic system when an engine fire switch is pulled?
docs.x: What happens to the hydraulic system when an engine fire switch is pulled? The engine-driven pump hydraulic supply shutoff valve closes, and the EDP is depressurized. Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: What three isolation valves make up the center system isolation function, plus what fourth element?
docs.x: What three isolation valves make up the center system isolation function, plus what fourth element? Nose Gear Isolation Valve (NGIV), Reserve Steering Isolation Valve (RSIV), Alternate Extend Isolation Valve (AEIV), and the reservoir standpipe. Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: Who controls the center hydraulic isolation valves during a non-normal event?
docs.x: Who controls the center hydraulic isolation valves during a non-normal event? No one - they operate automatically and cannot be controlled by the crew. Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: What is the purpose of the center hydraulic isolation system?
docs.x: What is the purpose of the center hydraulic isolation system? To ensure the flight crew can lower the landing gear and that nose wheel steering is operational for landing, rollout, and taxi even in the event of a leak. Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: Where is the RAM Air Turbine located?
docs.x: Where is the RAM Air Turbine located? In a compartment aft of the right main landing gear. Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: How can the RAT be deployed?
docs.x: How can the RAT be deployed? Automatically or manually (by pushing the RAM AIR TURBINE switch on the hydraulic panel). Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: Can the RAT be stowed in flight after deployment?
docs.x: Can the RAT be stowed in flight after deployment? No - once deployed, the RAT cannot be stowed in flight. Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: What pressure does the RAT provide, and what does the PRESS white light indicate?
docs.x: What pressure does the RAT provide, and what does the PRESS white light indicate? RAT seeks 5000 psi; PRESS white light illuminates when RAT is deployed and pressure is greater than 3000 psi. Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: What does the amber UNLKD light on the RAT switch indicate?
docs.x: What does the amber UNLKD light on the RAT switch indicate? The RAT is not stowed and locked. Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: What does the RAT power hydraulically?
docs.x: What does the RAT power hydraulically? Only the Center system flight controls. Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: What does the RAT power electrically?
docs.x: What does the RAT power electrically? Electrical power throughout the flight envelope (primarily instrument displays). Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: List the five conditions that cause automatic RAT deployment in flight.
docs.x: List the five conditions that cause automatic RAT deployment in flight. 1) Both engines have failed; 2) All three hydraulic system pressures are low; 3) Loss of all electrical power to captain's and first officer's flight instruments; 4) Loss of all four EMPs AND flight control system faults on approach; 5) Loss of all four EMPs AND an engine fails on takeoff or landing. Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: What positions do the TAIL and WINGS flight control lockout switches have?
docs.x: What positions do the TAIL and WINGS flight control lockout switches have? NORM (surface electronically unlocked) and LOCK (surface electronically locked). Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: What does the FAIL light on a flight control lockout switch indicate?
docs.x: What does the FAIL light on a flight control lockout switch indicate? The switch is in LOCK position but one or more of the associated surfaces did not lock. Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: At what groundspeed do flight control surfaces automatically unlock?
docs.x: At what groundspeed do flight control surfaces automatically unlock? When groundspeed exceeds 40 knots. Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: The HYD PRESS SYS L+C+R caution message indicates what condition?
docs.x: The HYD PRESS SYS L+C+R caution message indicates what condition? All hydraulic system pressures are low. Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: What is the aural alert level for HYD PRESS SYS C, L, or R caution messages?
docs.x: What is the aural alert level for HYD PRESS SYS C, L, or R caution messages? Beeper (caution level with beeper aural). Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: What is the message and level for a hydraulic pump overheat?
docs.x: What is the message and level for a hydraulic pump overheat? HYD OVERHEAT C1/C2/DEM L,R/PRI L,R - Advisory level (no aural). Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: The RAT UNLOCKED EICAS message is what level?
docs.x: The RAT UNLOCKED EICAS message is what level? Advisory. Hydraulics deck Hydraulics

docs.t: What type of hydraulic system provides power for landing gear retraction, extension, and steering?
docs.x: What type of hydraulic system provides power for landing gear retraction, extension, and steering? The center hydraulic system. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: How many Electric Brake Actuator Controllers (EBACs) does the B787 have, and what does each one control?
docs.x: How many Electric Brake Actuator Controllers (EBACs) does the B787 have, and what does each one control? 4 EBACs; each one controls the brake force of a fore-aft wheel pairing. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: How many Electric Brake Actuators (EBAs) are on the B787, and how many are on each wheel?
docs.x: How many Electric Brake Actuators (EBAs) are on the B787, and how many are on each wheel? 32 total (4 per wheel x 8 main gear wheels). Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: When do EBAs consume electrical power?
docs.x: When do EBAs consume electrical power? Only when they change position. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: Where are the weight-on-wheels sensors located?
docs.x: Where are the weight-on-wheels sensors located? On each main landing gear beam. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: On the ground, what holds the gear lever in the DN position?
docs.x: On the ground, what holds the gear lever in the DN position? An automatic lever lock. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: How is the landing gear lever lock released in flight?
docs.x: How is the landing gear lever lock released in flight? Automatically through air/ground sensing. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: If the lever lock fails to release in flight, how does the crew override it?
docs.x: If the lever lock fails to release in flight, how does the crew override it? By pushing and holding the landing gear lever LOCK OVRD switch. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: How soon after lift-off does the early doors function pre-open the main gear doors?
docs.x: How soon after lift-off does the early doors function pre-open the main gear doors? 1 second after lift-off. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: What happens if the crew does not move the gear lever to UP within 30 seconds of the early doors opening?
docs.x: What happens if the crew does not move the gear lever to UP within 30 seconds of the early doors opening? The main gear doors return to the closed position. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: During a touch-and-go, when does the early doors function activate?
docs.x: During a touch-and-go, when does the early doors function activate? Only after the airplane has been on the ground for more than 30 seconds. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: What color and style does the EICAS gear indication show when gear is in transit?
docs.x: What color and style does the EICAS gear indication show when gear is in transit? White crosshatch (in-transit indication). Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: How long does the UP indication remain displayed before blanking after gear retraction?
docs.x: How long does the UP indication remain displayed before blanking after gear retraction? 10 seconds. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: When is the landing gear hydraulic system automatically depressurized?
docs.x: When is the landing gear hydraulic system automatically depressurized? When the gear is retracted and all doors are closed. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: What happens to gear doors during alternate extension?
docs.x: What happens to gear doors during alternate extension? All hydraulically powered gear doors remain open; EICAS message GEAR DOOR is displayed. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: What powers the alternate extension system?
docs.x: What powers the alternate extension system? A dedicated DC-powered electric hydraulic pump using center hydraulic system fluid. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: In the normal compact EICAS gear display, what does an empty white box mean?
docs.x: In the normal compact EICAS gear display, what does an empty white box mean? All landing gear position indicators are inoperative. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: In the expanded gear position display, what does DN in green indicate?
docs.x: In the expanded gear position display, what does DN in green indicate? The associated landing gear is down and locked. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: What is the maximum nosewheel deflection achievable with the tiller?
docs.x: What is the maximum nosewheel deflection achievable with the tiller? 70 degrees in either direction. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: What is the maximum nosewheel deflection achievable with rudder pedals?
docs.x: What is the maximum nosewheel deflection achievable with rudder pedals? 8 degrees in either direction. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: What is the combined maximum nosewheel deflection when tiller and rudder pedal inputs are summed?
docs.x: What is the combined maximum nosewheel deflection when tiller and rudder pedal inputs are summed? 70 degrees (capped at tiller maximum). Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: Are the left and right nosewheel steering tillers interconnected?
docs.x: Are the left and right nosewheel steering tillers interconnected? No - transfer of control during a turn must not be accomplished. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: What is the purpose of the rudder pedal disconnect switch and how does it operate?
docs.x: What is the purpose of the rudder pedal disconnect switch and how does it operate? Temporarily disables rudder pedal inputs during the flight controls check before taxi; must be held down and is spring-loaded to out. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: Do the nosewheels have brakes?
docs.x: Do the nosewheels have brakes? No - only main gear wheels have brakes. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: What type of brakes do the B787 main gear wheels use?
docs.x: What type of brakes do the B787 main gear wheels use? Multiple disc carbon brakes. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: What type of brake system does the B787 use instead of hydraulic brakes?
docs.x: What type of brake system does the B787 use instead of hydraulic brakes? Electro-mechanical brakes. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: What does the antiskid system use for touchdown and hydroplaning protection?
docs.x: What does the antiskid system use for touchdown and hydroplaning protection? Airplane inertial groundspeed. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: How does the antiskid system provide locked wheel protection?
docs.x: How does the antiskid system provide locked wheel protection? By comparison with other wheel speeds. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: What is the data source for antiskid system control?
docs.x: What is the data source for antiskid system control? Each axle Remote Data Concentrator (RDC). Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: Does the antiskid system require flight crew interface?
docs.x: Does the antiskid system require flight crew interface? No - it requires no flight crew interface. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: What EICAS message appears for an antiskid fault, and what type is it?
docs.x: What EICAS message appears for an antiskid fault, and what type is it? ANTISKID - an advisory message. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: What three conditions must ALL be met for RTO autobrake to command maximum braking?
docs.x: What three conditions must ALL be met for RTO autobrake to command maximum braking? (1) Airplane on the ground; (2) Groundspeed above 85 knots; (3) Both thrust levers retarded to idle. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: If an RTO is initiated at or below 85 knots, does the RTO autobrake function operate?
docs.x: If an RTO is initiated at or below 85 knots, does the RTO autobrake function operate? No - it does not operate. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: Can RTO be selected in flight?
docs.x: Can RTO be selected in flight? No - RTO can be selected on the ground only. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: How many autobrake deceleration levels are available for landing?
docs.x: How many autobrake deceleration levels are available for landing? Five (1, 2, 3, 4, and MAX AUTO). Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: What two conditions must be met before autobrake application begins after landing?
docs.x: What two conditions must be met before autobrake application begins after landing? Both thrust levers retarded to idle AND wheels have spun up. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: What does MAX AUTO do initially upon landing, and when does it increase to full MAX AUTO deceleration?
docs.x: What does MAX AUTO do initially upon landing, and when does it increase to full MAX AUTO deceleration? Initially limits deceleration to the AUTOBRAKE 4 level until pitch angle is less than 1 degree, then increases to MAX AUTO level. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: Can the autobrake deceleration level be changed without disarming the system?
docs.x: Can the autobrake deceleration level be changed without disarming the system? Yes - by rotating the selector. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: Name conditions that disarm the autobrake system (any five).
docs.x: Name conditions that disarm the autobrake system (any five). (1) Pedal braking applied; (2) Either thrust lever advanced after landing; (3) Speedbrake lever moved to DOWN detent after spoiler deployment; (4) DISARM or OFF selected; (5) Autobrake fault; (6) Antiskid system fault; (7) Loss of IRU inertial data. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: After autobrake disarms following landing, where does the AUTOBRAKE selector move?
docs.x: After autobrake disarms following landing, where does the AUTOBRAKE selector move? Automatically to the DISARM position. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: After takeoff, where does the AUTOBRAKE selector automatically move?
docs.x: After takeoff, where does the AUTOBRAKE selector automatically move? Automatically to OFF. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: During taxi below 30 knots, how many brakes does the taxi brake release system apply per main gear during a manual brake application?
docs.x: During taxi below 30 knots, how many brakes does the taxi brake release system apply per main gear during a manual brake application? One-half (alternating fore-aft pairs), sequencing through pairs at each application. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: What must the pilot do to transition to the other brake pair during taxi?
docs.x: What must the pilot do to transition to the other brake pair during taxi? Fully release the brake pedal. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: Where is the PARKING BRAKE lever located?
docs.x: Where is the PARKING BRAKE lever located? On the control stand to the right of the Captain. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: Describe the procedure to set the parking brake.
docs.x: Describe the procedure to set the parking brake. Fully depress brake pedals, pull parking brake lever fully aft, then release the pedals. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: How do you release the parking brake?
docs.x: How do you release the parking brake? Simultaneously depress both brake pedals. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: Does the parking brake require continuous electrical power to maintain the clamping force?
docs.x: Does the parking brake require continuous electrical power to maintain the clamping force? No - the electric actuators are clamped in position and require no active power. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: What does the "park and adjust" feature do?
docs.x: What does the "park and adjust" feature do? Monitors brake condition after parking brake application and adjusts clamping force as needed during brake cooling. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: How long do the BSCUs keep braking power ON after parking brake is set, and why?
docs.x: How long do the BSCUs keep braking power ON after parking brake is set, and why? 60 minutes - to allow EBACs to adjust EBAs for thermal changes in the brakes. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: If airplane power goes off after setting the parking brake, what powers the BSCUs?
docs.x: If airplane power goes off after setting the parking brake, what powers the BSCUs? The main battery for the remaining portion of the 60-minute period. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: What EICAS message appears when the parking brake is set, and what type?
docs.x: What EICAS message appears when the parking brake is set, and what type? PARKING BRAKE SET - a memo message. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: What is the recommended action regarding the parking brake if there is a BRAKE TEMP EICAS message?
docs.x: What is the recommended action regarding the parking brake if there is a BRAKE TEMP EICAS message? It is recommended not to set the parking brake, unless needed. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: What is the range of brake temperature values displayed on the GEAR synoptic?
docs.x: What is the range of brake temperature values displayed on the GEAR synoptic? 0.0 to 9.9 in increments of 0.1. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: What color are brake temperature values in the normal range?
docs.x: What color are brake temperature values in the normal range? White (values 0.0 to 4.9). Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: What does a solid white brake symbol on the GEAR synoptic indicate?
docs.x: What does a solid white brake symbol on the GEAR synoptic indicate? The hottest brake on that truck, temperature 3.0 to 4.9. Only one hottest brake symbol is displayed per truck at any time. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: What does a solid amber brake symbol on the GEAR synoptic indicate?
docs.x: What does a solid amber brake symbol on the GEAR synoptic indicate? Brake overheat - temperature value 5.0 to 9.9. Multiple may appear simultaneously. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: At what brake temperature value does the EICAS BRAKE TEMP advisory trigger?
docs.x: At what brake temperature value does the EICAS BRAKE TEMP advisory trigger? 5.0 or higher on any brake. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: When does the EICAS BRAKE TEMP advisory clear?
docs.x: When does the EICAS BRAKE TEMP advisory clear? When all brake temperatures are below 3.0. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: Can the aircraft be dispatched with a BRAKE TEMP EICAS indication?
docs.x: Can the aircraft be dispatched with a BRAKE TEMP EICAS indication? No - dispatch is not possible with a BRAKE TEMP indication. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: Why do pilots use brakes on speed (KIAS) rather than the synoptic display to determine the initial brake cooling schedule?
docs.x: Why do pilots use brakes on speed (KIAS) rather than the synoptic display to determine the initial brake cooling schedule? Because the brake temperature display takes 10-15 minutes after stopping to indicate the resultant value. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: Which spoilers provide wheel well cooling, and how are they activated?
docs.x: Which spoilers provide wheel well cooling, and how are they activated? Spoilers 6 and 9 - activated automatically when temperatures reach a certain value. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: What color are normal tire pressures displayed on the GEAR synoptic?
docs.x: What color are normal tire pressures displayed on the GEAR synoptic? White. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: What color indicates a tire pressure above or below normal range?
docs.x: What color indicates a tire pressure above or below normal range? Amber. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: What triggers the EICAS TIRE PRESS advisory?
docs.x: What triggers the EICAS TIRE PRESS advisory? Any tire pressure above or below normal range, OR an excessive pressure difference between two tires on the same axle. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: What is the normal operations tire speed limit?
docs.x: What is the normal operations tire speed limit? 204 knots (235 MPH). Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: What is the maximum tire speed limit for non-normal landings?
docs.x: What is the maximum tire speed limit for non-normal landings? 226 knots (260 MPH). Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: What is required if a landing exceeds 204 knots tire speed?
docs.x: What is required if a landing exceeds 204 knots tire speed? A logbook entry shall be made. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: What is the maximum crank speed for adjusting rudder pedal position?
docs.x: What is the maximum crank speed for adjusting rudder pedal position? No faster than one turn per second. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: What happens if the rudder pedal adjust crank is not stowed after use?
docs.x: What happens if the rudder pedal adjust crank is not stowed after use? The rudder pedals may move out of the desired position. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: Where are tire pressures displayed on the GEAR synoptic relative to the gear symbols?
docs.x: Where are tire pressures displayed on the GEAR synoptic relative to the gear symbols? Inside each individual gear symbol. Landing Gear deck Landing Gear

docs.t: How many independent FMCs does the B787 have?
docs.x: How many independent FMCs does the B787 have? Three independent FMCs. Navigation and FMS deck Nav and FMS
docs.r: Nav and FMS · Navigation and FMS deck

docs.t: How many GPS receivers does the B787 have, and where is their position output sent?
docs.x: How many GPS receivers does the B787 have, and where is their position output sent? Two (Left and Right). They supply accurate position data to the IRS, which in turn supplies hybrid GPS inertial position to the FMC. All GPS tuning is automatic. Navigation and FMS deck Nav and FMS
docs.r: Nav and FMS · Navigation and FMS deck

docs.t: What EICAS message is generated when both GPS systems have failed?
docs.x: What EICAS message is generated when both GPS systems have failed? EICAS advisory message GPS. Navigation and FMS deck Nav and FMS
docs.r: Nav and FMS · Navigation and FMS deck

docs.t: What are the two major hardware components of the IRS?
docs.x: What are the two major hardware components of the IRS? Two inertial reference units (IRUs) and two attitude heading reference units (AHRUs). Navigation and FMS deck Nav and FMS
docs.r: Nav and FMS · Navigation and FMS deck

docs.t: What is the approximate IRS alignment time at mid latitudes?
docs.x: What is the approximate IRS alignment time at mid latitudes? Approximately 7 to 10 minutes. Navigation and FMS deck Nav and FMS
docs.r: Nav and FMS · Navigation and FMS deck

docs.t: What is the maximum IRS alignment time at high latitudes?
docs.x: What is the maximum IRS alignment time at high latitudes? Up to 17 minutes. Navigation and FMS deck Nav and FMS
docs.r: Nav and FMS · Navigation and FMS deck

docs.t: When can the airplane be moved during IRS alignment?
docs.x: When can the airplane be moved during IRS alignment? The airplane should not move until alignment is complete (IRS changes to navigate mode). Navigation and FMS deck Nav and FMS
docs.r: Nav and FMS · Navigation and FMS deck

docs.t: If GPS is not available during IRS alignment, what must the crew do?
docs.x: If GPS is not available during IRS alignment, what must the crew do? Manually enter present position on the CDU POS INIT page (boxes replace dashes). Navigation and FMS deck Nav and FMS
docs.r: Nav and FMS · Navigation and FMS deck

docs.t: What EICAS message and CDU message appear if the entered position is not close to the origin airport?
docs.x: What EICAS message and CDU message appear if the entered position is not close to the origin airport? EICAS advisory FMC MESSAGE + CDU help window message INERTIAL/ORIGIN DISAGREE. Navigation and FMS deck Nav and FMS
docs.r: Nav and FMS · Navigation and FMS deck

docs.t: What is the automatic realign mode, and what triggers it?
docs.x: What is the automatic realign mode, and what triggers it? When the airplane stops for an extended period, the IRS changes to automatic realign mode and refines alignment until the airplane moves. In this mode, IRS velocity and acceleration errors are reset to zero. Navigation and FMS deck Nav and FMS
docs.r: Nav and FMS · Navigation and FMS deck

docs.t: When is a manual position update recommended in the navigate mode?
docs.x: When is a manual position update recommended in the navigate mode? If total time in navigate mode is expected to exceed 18 hours. Navigation and FMS deck Nav and FMS
docs.r: Nav and FMS · Navigation and FMS deck

docs.t: If both IRUs fail (but AHRUs are intact), what EICAS message is shown and what capability remains?
docs.x: If both IRUs fail (but AHRUs are intact), what EICAS message is shown and what capability remains? EICAS advisory NAV IRU. The FMC continues to receive a hybrid GPS inertial position solution using the AHRUs inertial sensors combined with GPS position. Navigation and FMS deck Nav and FMS
docs.r: Nav and FMS · Navigation and FMS deck

docs.t: If the full IRS fails (both AHRUs and IRUs), what EICAS message is shown and what capability is lost?
docs.x: If the full IRS fails (both AHRUs and IRUs), what EICAS message is shown and what capability is lost? EICAS caution NAV INERTIAL SYS. LNAV and VNAV coupled to autopilot are not available. GPS provides position/track data for FMC to continue navigation. Navigation and FMS deck Nav and FMS
docs.r: Nav and FMS · Navigation and FMS deck

docs.t: Regarding in-flight IRU realignment after a power interruption: how quickly does attitude return, and how quickly is full navigation restored?
docs.x: Regarding in-flight IRU realignment after a power interruption: how quickly does attitude return, and how quickly is full navigation restored? Attitude information available within a few seconds; full navigation capability restored within about 10 minutes. Requires GPS data. Navigation and FMS deck Nav and FMS
docs.r: Nav and FMS · Navigation and FMS deck

docs.t: What are the three pitot-static sources used by the ADRS?
docs.x: What are the three pitot-static sources used by the ADRS? Left, center, and right pitot and static systems. Navigation and FMS deck Nav and FMS
docs.r: Nav and FMS · Navigation and FMS deck

docs.t: What is the relationship between the ADRS and the IRS?
docs.x: What is the relationship between the ADRS and the IRS? The ADRS is completely independent of the IRS. Navigation and FMS deck Nav and FMS
docs.r: Nav and FMS · Navigation and FMS deck

docs.t: If voted ADRS air data becomes invalid with the AIR DATA/ATT switch in AUTO, what backup sources are used?
docs.x: If voted ADRS air data becomes invalid with the AIR DATA/ATT switch in AUTO, what backup sources are used? Backup airspeed (AOA SPD) and/or backup altitude (GPS ALT) automatically provided by the IRS and GPS systems. Navigation and FMS deck Nav and FMS
docs.r: Nav and FMS · Navigation and FMS deck

docs.t: What data source does the ISFD use, and is it dependent on the IRU/AHRU?
docs.x: What data source does the ISFD use, and is it dependent on the IRU/AHRU? The ISFD receives data from the center pitot static system. ISFD altitude, attitude, and airspeed are independent of IRU and AHRU values. Navigation and FMS deck Nav and FMS
docs.r: Nav and FMS · Navigation and FMS deck

docs.t: What data is displayed on the PFD if both voted and backup air data are unavailable?
docs.x: What data is displayed on the PFD if both voted and backup air data are unavailable? ISFD ALT and ISFD SPD. Navigation and FMS deck Nav and FMS
docs.r: Nav and FMS · Navigation and FMS deck

docs.t: What is the IAS/MACH window value when power is first applied?
docs.x: What is the IAS/MACH window value when power is first applied? Upper line displays 200 knots; lower line is blank. Navigation and FMS deck Nav and FMS
docs.r: Nav and FMS · Navigation and FMS deck

docs.t: What is the display range of the IAS/MACH window?
docs.x: What is the display range of the IAS/MACH window? 100-399 KIAS or .400-.950 Mach. Navigation and FMS deck Nav and FMS
docs.r: Nav and FMS · Navigation and FMS deck

docs.t: At what speed does the MCP IAS/MACH window automatically change from IAS to Mach during climb?
docs.x: At what speed does the MCP IAS/MACH window automatically change from IAS to Mach during climb? 0.840 Mach. Navigation and FMS deck Nav and FMS
docs.r: Nav and FMS · Navigation and FMS deck

docs.t: At what speed does the MCP IAS/MACH window automatically change from Mach to IAS during descent?
docs.x: At what speed does the MCP IAS/MACH window automatically change from Mach to IAS during descent? 310 KIAS. Navigation and FMS deck Nav and FMS
docs.r: Nav and FMS · Navigation and FMS deck

docs.t: When is the IAS/MACH window blank?
docs.x: When is the IAS/MACH window blank? When the FMC controls the speed (VNAV active, window closed). Navigation and FMS deck Nav and FMS
docs.r: Nav and FMS · Navigation and FMS deck

docs.t: What happens when you push the IAS/MACH selector with VNAV active?
docs.x: What happens when you push the IAS/MACH selector with VNAV active? Alternately opens or closes the IAS/MACH window. Closed = FMC computed target speed active. Open = FMC speed-intervention active; IAS/MACH selector may set desired speed. Navigation and FMS deck Nav and FMS

docs.x: What altitude restriction applies to OFAR ventilation? The OFAR has no ventilation below 15,000 ft altitude. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: What type of slide/raft deploys at 3L/R exits?

docs.t: Where is the red manual inflation handle located on the 787 door?

docs.t: After pulling the white Quick Release Handle, what keeps the slide/raft attached to the aircraft?

docs.t: What is the normal and overload capacity of the 1L/R slide/raft?

docs.t: What is the normal and overload capacity of the 2L/R slide/raft?

docs.t: What is the normal and overload capacity of the 3L/R slide/raft?
docs.x: What is the normal and overload capacity of the 3L/R slide/raft? Normal: 27; Overload: 34. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: What is the normal and overload capacity of the 4L/R slide/raft?
docs.x: What is the normal and overload capacity of the 4L/R slide/raft? Normal: 53; Overload: 66. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: How many canopy mast attach points does a single-lane slide/raft have? A dual-lane?
docs.x: How many canopy mast attach points does a single-lane slide/raft have? A dual-lane? Single-lane: 5; Dual-lane: 8. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: How much pressure on the mooring line triggers automatic complete release of the slide/raft?

docs.t: How is the raft knife used for complete release, and where is it stored?

docs.t: What happens to inflation valves on the raft when the handpump is removed?
docs.x: What happens to inflation valves on the raft when the handpump is removed? They are self-closing. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: Are aerial flares approved for day use, night use, or both?
docs.x: Are aerial flares approved for day use, night use, or both? Both day and night. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: During a slide/raft transfer, what is the maximum amount the door may be rotated outward and why?
docs.x: During a slide/raft transfer, what is the maximum amount the door may be rotated outward and why? No more than 3 inches - to prevent slide/raft deployment. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: In a slide/raft transfer, what is the first step after deciding to transfer?
docs.x: In a slide/raft transfer, what is the first step after deciding to transfer? Disable the power assist by opening the hinged door and moving the switch downward to the SAFE position. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: What does the pulse oxygen bottle preflight pressure gauge need to read?
docs.x: What does the pulse oxygen bottle preflight pressure gauge need to read? Between 1,500 and 1,850 psi. If below 1,500 psi, notify FFA. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: What type of extinguishing agent is in the 787 chemical fire extinguisher?
docs.x: What type of extinguishing agent is in the 787 chemical fire extinguisher? Non-halon agent. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: How far should you stand from the base of flames when using the 787 chemical fire extinguisher?
docs.x: How far should you stand from the base of flames when using the 787 chemical fire extinguisher? 6 to 8 feet. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: How long does the ELT transmit a distress signal?
docs.x: How long does the ELT transmit a distress signal? 24 to 50 hours with unlimited range. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: What does the ELT LED amber blink indicate, and what does green blink indicate?
docs.x: What does the ELT LED amber blink indicate, and what does green blink indicate? Amber blink: signal not yet detected by GPS. Green blink: detected by GPS. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: How many PED fire containment bags are on the 787, and where are they located?
docs.x: How many PED fire containment bags are on the 787, and where are they located? 3 bags total: 1 in the flight deck and 2 in the cabin. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: What are the MEL installed and required quantities for the Enhanced Emergency Medical Kit (EEMK)?
docs.x: What are the MEL installed and required quantities for the Enhanced Emergency Medical Kit (EEMK)? 1 installed; 1 required. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: What are the MEL installed and required quantities for First Aid Kits?
docs.x: What are the MEL installed and required quantities for First Aid Kits? 4 installed; 3 required. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: During a water evacuation, where does the First Officer retrieve the ELT?
docs.x: During a water evacuation, where does the First Officer retrieve the ELT? From the Door 1L storage space. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: During a water evacuation, through which doors does the Captain exit the aircraft?
docs.x: During a water evacuation, through which doors does the Captain exit the aircraft? L/R AFT entry doors. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: What color are crew life vests? What color are passenger life vests?
docs.x: What color are crew life vests? What color are passenger life vests? Crew vests are orange/red; passenger vests are yellow. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: What is the wing tip turning radius of the 787?
docs.x: What is the wing tip turning radius of the 787? 144 ft 0 in. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: What is the nose turning radius of the 787?
docs.x: What is the nose turning radius of the 787? 110 ft 0 in. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: What is the minimum pavement width required for a 787 180-degree turn?
docs.x: What is the minimum pavement width required for a 787 180-degree turn? 154 ft 0 in. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: What obstacle clearance distances must not be violated when turning the 787?
docs.x: What obstacle clearance distances must not be violated when turning the 787? Do not turn within 15 ft of the wing tip or within 55 ft of the nose. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: When the SEAT BELTS switch is in AUTO, at what flap lever position do the seat belt signs illuminate?
docs.x: When the SEAT BELTS switch is in AUTO, at what flap lever position do the seat belt signs illuminate? Flap lever at 5 or greater. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: When the SEAT BELTS switch is in AUTO, below what aircraft altitude do the seat belt signs illuminate?
docs.x: When the SEAT BELTS switch is in AUTO, below what aircraft altitude do the seat belt signs illuminate? Below 10,000 ft MSL. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: What cabin altitude triggers automatic seat belt sign illumination in AUTO mode?
docs.x: What cabin altitude triggers automatic seat belt sign illumination in AUTO mode? Above 10,000 ft cabin altitude. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: What does a Green "A" on the door synoptic indicate?
docs.x: What does a Green "A" on the door synoptic indicate? Passenger door is closed, latched, and locked; and the slide is in automatic mode. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: What does a White "M" on the door synoptic indicate?
docs.x: What does a White "M" on the door synoptic indicate? Passenger door is closed, latched, and locked; and the slide is in manual mode. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: What does an amber indication on the door synoptic mean?
docs.x: What does an amber indication on the door synoptic mean? Passenger entry or large cargo door is NOT closed, latched, and locked. (Also covers flight deck overhead door, bulk cargo door, or access door not closed and latched.) GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: Which cargo doors are on the right side of the 787?
docs.x: Which cargo doors are on the right side of the 787? Forward and aft cargo doors. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: How is the bulk cargo door operated, and on which side is it located?
docs.x: How is the bulk cargo door operated, and on which side is it located? Mechanically operated; on the left side; opens inward. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: Does opening a cargo door turn off cargo heating, ventilation, or fire detection?
docs.x: Does opening a cargo door turn off cargo heating, ventilation, or fire detection? No. Opening any cargo door does NOT turn off cargo area heating, ventilation, or fire detection. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: What are the three O2 regulator settings and what does each provide?
docs.x: What are the three O2 regulator settings and what does each provide? EMGCY: 100% O2 under positive pressure at all altitudes. 100%: 100% O2 on demand. N (Normal): air/oxygen mixture on demand; auto switches to 100% positive pressure above a preset cabin altitude. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: How long is oxygen available from the passenger oxygen system?
docs.x: How long is oxygen available from the passenger oxygen system? Approximately 22 minutes. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: At what cabin altitude do passenger oxygen masks automatically drop?
docs.x: At what cabin altitude do passenger oxygen masks automatically drop? The greater of 14,500 ft OR origin airfield altitude plus 1,500 ft OR destination airfield altitude plus 1,500 ft. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: How do you manually deploy passenger oxygen masks from the flight deck?
docs.x: How do you manually deploy passenger oxygen masks from the flight deck? Push the PASS OXYGEN switch on the overhead panel to ON. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: Where are the two CCR cabinets located on the 787?
docs.x: Where are the two CCR cabinets located on the 787? In the Forward EE Bay (left cabinet and right cabinet). GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: Are there any CCS controls or indications for normal operations?
docs.x: Are there any CCS controls or indications for normal operations? No. There are no CCS controls or indications during normal operations. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: Where are the two CCR RESET switches located?
docs.x: Where are the two CCR RESET switches located? On the overhead panel (labeled L and R). GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: During battery-only start-up, when does the R CCR begin its start-up cycle?
docs.x: During battery-only start-up, when does the R CCR begin its start-up cycle? After the L CCR completes start-up AND a power source other than the battery (APU or external power) is available. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: How do you know both CCRs are on-line following external power start-up?
docs.x: How do you know both CCRs are on-line following external power start-up? All displays and HUD combiners show their default formats. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: Can EICAS warning messages be canceled using the CANC/RCL switch?
docs.x: Can EICAS warning messages be canceled using the CANC/RCL switch? No. Warning messages cannot be canceled by the CANC/RCL switch. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: Can EICAS communication messages be canceled by the CANC/RCL switch?
docs.x: Can EICAS communication messages be canceled by the CANC/RCL switch? No. Communication messages cannot be canceled by CANC/RCL. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: During what speed/altitude range are EICAS advisory messages inhibited?
docs.x: During what speed/altitude range are EICAS advisory messages inhibited? Between 80 knots and 400 ft AGL. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: When does the EICAS checklist icon disappear?
docs.x: When does the EICAS checklist icon disappear? When the checklist associated with that message is complete. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: What triggers the NO AUTOLAND alert on the PFD?
docs.x: What triggers the NO AUTOLAND alert on the PFD? Flying an ILS approach with the autopilot on an FMC glidepath below 100 ft (rather than the ILS glidepath). GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: What are the four Time Critical Warnings displayed on both the PFD and HUD?
docs.x: What are the four Time Critical Warnings displayed on both the PFD and HUD? ENG FAIL, PULL UP, SPEEDBRAKE, WINDSHEAR. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: When TAMS is reached, what aural and master light are triggered?
docs.x: When TAMS is reached, what aural and master light are triggered? "AIRSPEED, AIRSPEED" aural sounds with Master WARNING light. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: At what altitude can the G/S INHIBIT switch be activated?
docs.x: At what altitude can the G/S INHIBIT switch be activated? Below 1,000 ft radio altitude. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: On takeoff, between what airspeeds does the ENG FAIL alert display if thrust is less than commanded?
docs.x: On takeoff, between what airspeeds does the ENG FAIL alert display if thrust is less than commanded? Between 65 knots and 6 knots prior to V1. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: What condition triggers the EICAS caution ENG FAIL (not on the takeoff roll)?
docs.x: What condition triggers the EICAS caution ENG FAIL (not on the takeoff roll)? An engine unexpectedly decelerates to less than idle speed. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: What clears the EICAS caution ENG FAIL message?
docs.x: What clears the EICAS caution ENG FAIL message? Engine recovers to above idle, OR the fuel control switch is moved to CUTOFF. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: What physical components make up the 787 tail strike detection system?
docs.x: What physical components make up the 787 tail strike detection system? A two-inch blade target and two frangible wires installed on the aft body of the airplane. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: What is the EICAS level (warning/caution/advisory) for the TAIL STRIKE message?
docs.x: What is the EICAS level (warning/caution/advisory) for the TAIL STRIKE message? Caution. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: At what radio altitude does the CONFIG GEAR warning trigger?
docs.x: At what radio altitude does the CONFIG GEAR warning trigger? Radio altitude less than 800 ft (with gear not down and locked, and thrust lever below nominal glideslope thrust level). GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: What triggers the SPEEDBRAKE EXTENDED caution in flight?
docs.x: What triggers the SPEEDBRAKE EXTENDED caution in flight? Radio altitude below 800 ft AND flap lever in landing position; OR thrust lever above idle stop for 15 seconds. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: How far before the MCP selected altitude does the altitude alerting C-chord sound?
docs.x: How far before the MCP selected altitude does the altitude alerting C-chord sound? 900 ft prior to reaching the selected altitude. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: How far from the MCP selected altitude does the ALTITUDE ALERT caution trigger when departing?
docs.x: How far from the MCP selected altitude does the ALTITUDE ALERT caution trigger when departing? 200 ft deviation from the selected altitude. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: When are MCP selected altitude alerts inhibited?
docs.x: When are MCP selected altitude alerts inhibited? When glideslope or glidepath is captured, OR when landing flaps are selected and landing gear is down and locked. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: TRUE or FALSE: Passenger oxygen masks automatically drop at the greater of 14,500 ft, origin airfield altitude plus 1,500 ft, or destination airfield altitude plus 1,500 ft?
docs.x: TRUE or FALSE: Passenger oxygen masks automatically drop at the greater of 14,500 ft, origin airfield altitude plus 1,500 ft, or destination airfield altitude plus 1,500 ft? TRUE. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: TRUE or FALSE: Warning (red) EICAS messages can be cancelled by pushing the Cancel/Recall button?
docs.x: TRUE or FALSE: Warning (red) EICAS messages can be cancelled by pushing the Cancel/Recall button? FALSE. Warning messages cannot be cancelled by the CANC/RCL switch. GenOps deck GenOps

docs.t: When does the EICAS checklist icon disappear?
docs.x: When does the EICAS checklist icon disappear? When the checklist associated with that message is complete. GenOps deck GenOps
