docs.x: How many questions are on the B787 Systems Validation (SV) exam? 100 questions. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: How long do pilots have to complete the SV?
docs.x: How long do pilots have to complete the SV? 3 hours. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: What is the passing standard for the B787 SV?
docs.x: What is the passing standard for the B787 SV? 80% or greater. Pilots who score below 80% are remediated to 100%. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: Is the SV open or closed book? What resources are and are not permitted?
docs.x: Is the SV open or closed book? What resources are and are not permitted? Open book. Company iPad to access resource documents is permitted. Personal notes and study guides are NOT permitted. -- MEMORY ITEMS AND NNC FUNDAMENTALS -- SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: When should memory items be accomplished following an engine fire or engine severe damage/separation?
docs.x: When should memory items be accomplished following an engine fire or engine severe damage/separation? When the flight path is under control, gear has been retracted, and a safe altitude has been attained - minimum 400 feet AGL. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: During an engine fire memory item, when does the PF retard the affected thrust lever?
docs.x: During an engine fire memory item, when does the PF retard the affected thrust lever? After the PM confirms that the PF has identified the correct engine. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: Where is the QRC stored?
docs.x: Where is the QRC stored? Under the MCP glareshield. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: When a non-normal situation occurs, who initiates the memory items and how do both crew respond?
docs.x: When a non-normal situation occurs, who initiates the memory items and how do both crew respond? At the direction of the pilot flying, both crewmembers do all memory items in their areas of responsibility without delay. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: Is verbal "Confirm" required for non-normal checklist items when on the ground?
docs.x: Is verbal "Confirm" required for non-normal checklist items when on the ground? No. Confirmation is NOT needed for non-normal checklist items when on the ground. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: Name five controls that require verbal confirmation before action during an inflight non-normal situation.
docs.x: Name five controls that require verbal confirmation before action during an inflight non-normal situation. Autothrottle arm switch; engine thrust lever; fuel control switch; engine or APU fire switch (or cargo fire arm switch); generator drive disconnect switch. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: The "Confirm" step requirement does not apply to which checklist?
docs.x: The "Confirm" step requirement does not apply to which checklist? The Dual Eng Fail/Stall checklist. -- NORMAL CHECKLISTS -- SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: What EICAS message alerts crew when critical normal checklist items are incomplete?
docs.x: What EICAS message alerts crew when critical normal checklist items are incomplete? CHKL INCOMPLETE NORM (caution level). The normal checklist key also changes to amber. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: At what altitude does the CHKL INCOMPLETE NORM "landing phase" trigger occur?
docs.x: At what altitude does the CHKL INCOMPLETE NORM "landing phase" trigger occur? When the airplane descends below 500 feet above the FMC landing altitude. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: If a normal checklist is interrupted and the crew is unsure where it was stopped, what must be done?
docs.x: If a normal checklist is interrupted and the crew is unsure where it was stopped, what must be done? Do the checklist from the start. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: After completing each normal checklist, what does the pilot reading the checklist call out?
docs.x: After completing each normal checklist, what does the pilot reading the checklist call out? "________ CHECKLIST COMPLETE." -- NON-NORMAL CHECKLISTS -- SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: What is the difference between an annunciated and an unannunciated checklist?
docs.x: What is the difference between an annunciated and an unannunciated checklist? Annunciated checklists correspond to an EICAS alert message. Unannunciated checklists have no EICAS alert message. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: Where are unannunciated checklists found in the QRH?
docs.x: Where are unannunciated checklists found in the QRH? In the associated system section. Those with no associated system are in section 0, Miscellaneous. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: What does the rectangle icon [ ] before an EICAS alert message indicate?
docs.x: What does the rectangle icon [ ] before an EICAS alert message indicate? The checklist has procedural steps, notes, or other crew information. The icon is removed when the checklist is completed. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: Give three examples of annunciated and three examples of unannunciated checklists.
docs.x: Give three examples of annunciated and three examples of unannunciated checklists. Annunciated: FIRE ENG L, CABIN ALTITUDE, HYD PRESS SYS R. Unannunciated: Ditching, ENG Severe Damage/Separation, Overweight Landing. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: When should CANC/RCL be used after completing a NNC?
docs.x: When should CANC/RCL be used after completing a NNC? Before completing any normal checklists, to check if there are other NNCs to be completed. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: What EICAS advisory message alerts the crew to an active checklist in the queue when ECL is not open?
docs.x: What EICAS advisory message alerts the crew to an active checklist in the queue when ECL is not open? CHKL NON-NORMAL. It blanks when ECL is opened. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.x: A NNC occurs a second time on the same flight. The EICAS message shows but without the rectangle icon. Why, and what should the crew do? The checklist is latched in the completed state from the first occurrence (it is a latched checklist). The crew must open the checklist from the ECL non-normal menu and select CHKL RESET to restart it. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: What situations require landing at the nearest suitable airport?
docs.x: What situations require landing at the nearest suitable airport? When the NNC includes "Plan to land at the nearest suitable airport"; fire or smoke continues; only two AC power sources remain; or any other situation with significant adverse effect on safety if flight is continued. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: When a checklist directs an engine shutdown, what must the captain evaluate?
docs.x: When a checklist directs an engine shutdown, what must the captain evaluate? Whether an actual shutdown or operation at reduced thrust is the safest course of action. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: When the PF calls for the checklist, what three conditions must be met?
docs.x: When the PF calls for the checklist, what three conditions must be met? Flight path is under control; airplane is not in a critical phase of flight; all memory items are complete. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: After moving a control during a NNC, who states the checklist response?
docs.x: After moving a control during a NNC, who states the checklist response? The flight crewmember who took the action. -- ECL OPERATIONS -- SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: What does CHKL OVRD do, and what does it also remove?
docs.x: What does CHKL OVRD do, and what does it also remove? Forces the checklist back to the inactive state. Also removes: notes collected on the Notes page, inhibited checklists, and deferred items added to normal checklists. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: When should CHKL OVRD NOT be used?
docs.x: When should CHKL OVRD NOT be used? When the crew wants to pause the checklist and complete it later. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: What does ITEM OVRD do to a line item?
docs.x: What does ITEM OVRD do to a line item? Changes the item to cyan, advances the current line item box to the next incomplete item, and treats the overridden item as complete. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: In an open-loop conditional checklist, what color do inactive items become?
docs.x: In an open-loop conditional checklist, what color do inactive items become? Cyan. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: When can the active ECL database be changed?
docs.x: When can the active ECL database be changed? On the ground when both engines are off. The key is inhibited in flight. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: What happens to all checklists when the active ECL database is changed?
docs.x: What happens to all checklists when the active ECL database is changed? All checklists are reset. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: What revision should the selected AIRLINE DATABASE match?
docs.x: What revision should the selected AIRLINE DATABASE match? The ECL Revision listed on the front page of the current approved QRH. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: When does a checklist timer change from white to amber?
docs.x: When does a checklist timer change from white to amber? When the countdown reaches :00 (timer is done). SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: Can a crew leave the checklist page while a timer is running?
docs.x: Can a crew leave the checklist page while a timer is running? Yes. Timers run in the background. -- WEIGHT AND BALANCE / LOAD CLOSEOUT -- SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: What must happen before the Load Closeout (final numbers) will be sent to the aircraft?
docs.x: What must happen before the Load Closeout (final numbers) will be sent to the aircraft? "Fit-For-Duty" must be submitted and acknowledged. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: What two figures are compared during the LCO crosscheck?
docs.x: What two figures are compared during the LCO crosscheck? Planned Takeoff Weight on the Dispatch Release vs. Actual Takeoff Weight on the Load Closeout. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: The Dispatch Release is valid for TOW up to how many pounds greater than PTOW without requiring a new release?
docs.x: The Dispatch Release is valid for TOW up to how many pounds greater than PTOW without requiring a new release? Up to 3,000 lbs greater. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: If TOW on the LCO exceeds PTOW by 2,000 lbs, what two actions are required?
docs.x: If TOW on the LCO exceeds PTOW by 2,000 lbs, what two actions are required? Increase MIN RLS FUEL and MIN TAKEOFF FUEL by the FUEL BURN ADJUSTMENT per 1,000 lbs increase in TOW, and send an ACARS message to Dispatch with acknowledgment required. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: What exact ACARS message text is used when adjusting MIN RLS and MIN TAKEOFF fuel?
docs.x: What exact ACARS message text is used when adjusting MIN RLS and MIN TAKEOFF fuel? "ADD XXX LB TO MIN RLS AND MIN TO" (inserting the appropriate amount). SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: If TOW exceeds PTOW by more than 3,000 lbs, what is required?
docs.x: If TOW exceeds PTOW by more than 3,000 lbs, what is required? A revised Dispatch Release. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: How is a Load Closeout obtained if ACARS is inoperative?
docs.x: How is a Load Closeout obtained if ACARS is inoperative? Company email (preferred) or VHF radio. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: For a Radio Load Closeout (HAL F-809), what must be read back and what must the Captain do with the form?
docs.x: For a Radio Load Closeout (HAL F-809), what must be read back and what must the Captain do with the form? The asterisked items must be read back for accuracy. The Captain must carry a signed copy to the destination. -- PERFORMANCE -- SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: On a contaminated runway, what is the thrust requirement and what is not permitted?
docs.x: On a contaminated runway, what is the thrust requirement and what is not permitted? Reduced thrust using assumed temperature (AT/FLEX) is NOT authorized. See fleet-specific manuals for guidance on the use of maximum thrust. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: On a wet or slippery (not contaminated) runway, is maximum thrust required?
docs.x: On a wet or slippery (not contaminated) runway, is maximum thrust required? No. It is encouraged but not required. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: What is the maximum normal tire speed on landing?
docs.x: What is the maximum normal tire speed on landing? 204 knots. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: What is the maximum allowable tire speed for a non-normal landing?
docs.x: What is the maximum allowable tire speed for a non-normal landing? 226 knots. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: What factor is applied to normal configuration landing distances?

docs.t: Are non-normal configuration landing distances factored?
docs.x: Are non-normal configuration landing distances factored? No. They are representative of actual landing distance and are NOT factored. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: What is the assumed flare time used for the normal landing reference distance?
docs.x: What is the assumed flare time used for the normal landing reference distance? 7 seconds. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: If brake overheat occurs after takeoff, what action should be taken?
docs.x: If brake overheat occurs after takeoff, what action should be taken? Extend the gear for at least 12 minutes. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: When should brake temperature indication on the MFD be used to determine cooling schedule?
docs.x: When should brake temperature indication on the MFD be used to determine cooling schedule? 10 to 15 minutes after the airplane has come to a complete stop, or in flight with gear retracted. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: What is the Flap Retraction Altitude for all takeoffs?
docs.x: What is the Flap Retraction Altitude for all takeoffs? 1,000 ft AFE, unless a Special Procedure states otherwise. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: Below what altitude are no turns permitted when takeoff weather is below 1,000 ft ceiling and 3 sm visibility?
docs.x: Below what altitude are no turns permitted when takeoff weather is below 1,000 ft ceiling and 3 sm visibility? 1,000 ft AFE (unless a Special Departure Procedure or assigned instrument departure procedure specifically requires otherwise). SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: When is the OPT used?
docs.x: When is the OPT used? For landing calculations only - when the Landing Data Request is not working for normal conditions, or when calculating non-normal/inoperative item landing distances. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: What is the standard missed approach climb gradient used in the OPT?
docs.x: What is the standard missed approach climb gradient used in the OPT? 2.5%. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: What does a non-normal entry affecting flap selection do to the OPT output?
docs.x: What does a non-normal entry affecting flap selection do to the OPT output? The landing flap field is blanked, the missed approach climb gradient is disregarded, and recommended brake cooling time is not displayed. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: How do you convert a climb gradient from ft/NM to a percentage?
docs.x: How do you convert a climb gradient from ft/NM to a percentage? Divide by 60 (representing 6,000 ft per NM, rounded). SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: VREF for flaps 30 at 420,000 lbs is what?
docs.x: VREF for flaps 30 at 420,000 lbs is what? 153 knots (per deck example). SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: For the brake cooling example in the deck (440,000 lbs / 140 kt / OAT 30C / sea level / RTO MAX MANUAL), what is the cooling situation?
docs.x: For the brake cooling example in the deck (440,000 lbs / 140 kt / OAT 30C / sea level / RTO MAX MANUAL), what is the cooling situation? Event Adjusted Brake Energy = 55.0. Ground cooling is in the Caution Zone: delay takeoff and inspect after one hour. -- COLD WEATHER OPERATIONS -- SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: What federal regulation is the Clean Aircraft Concept based on?
docs.x: What federal regulation is the Clean Aircraft Concept based on? 14 CFR 121.629. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: How much frost on lower wing surfaces is allowable for takeoff, and under what condition?
docs.x: How much frost on lower wing surfaces is allowable for takeoff, and under what condition? Light coatings of frost up to 1/8 inch (3mm) on lower wing surfaces due to cold fuel are allowable. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: Are upper wing surfaces, leading-edge devices, and control surfaces subject to any frost tolerance?
docs.x: Are upper wing surfaces, leading-edge devices, and control surfaces subject to any frost tolerance? No. They must be completely free of snow, ice, and frost. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: Where is thin hoarfrost acceptable, and what defines it?
docs.x: Where is thin hoarfrost acceptable, and what defines it? On the upper surface of the fuselage, provided all vents and ports are clear. It is a uniform white deposit of fine crystalline texture, thin enough to distinguish surface features (paint lines, markings, lettering) underneath. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: When does HOT begin?
docs.x: When does HOT begin? When the final application of deicing or anti-icing fluid commences. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: If the deice report does not identify the specific Type IV fluid brand used, what table must be used?
docs.x: If the deice report does not identify the specific Type IV fluid brand used, what table must be used? The generic holdover time table for Type IV fluid from the FAA Holdover Time Guidelines. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: The holdover time table shows a time range. What does the shorter time correspond to?
docs.x: The holdover time table shows a time range. What does the shorter time correspond to? A heavier precipitation intensity within that cell. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: If METAR indicates light snow but the prevailing visibility chart shows moderate snow, which is used for HOT?
docs.x: If METAR indicates light snow but the prevailing visibility chart shows moderate snow, which is used for HOT? Moderate snow is used. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: If visibility drops to 1/2 SM during snowfall, what is the holdover time?
docs.x: If visibility drops to 1/2 SM during snowfall, what is the holdover time? There is no holdover time - no HOT exists for heavy snow. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: When must the flight crew pre-takeoff contamination check (after HOT expiry) be conducted?
docs.x: When must the flight crew pre-takeoff contamination check (after HOT expiry) be conducted? Within five (5) minutes prior to beginning of takeoff. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: During the pre-takeoff contamination check, which wing is inspected last?
docs.x: During the pre-takeoff contamination check, which wing is inspected last? The wing that was de-iced first. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: What must be done with the HAL HOT app when using the holdover timer?
docs.x: What must be done with the HAL HOT app when using the holdover timer? The app must be displayed as the active window on at least one EFB. Use the iPad split window function to display the timer and airport diagram simultaneously. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: When temperature is lower than ISA, how does true altitude compare to indicated altitude?
docs.x: When temperature is lower than ISA, how does true altitude compare to indicated altitude? True altitude is lower than indicated altitude. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: When must pilots request ATC approval for cold temperature altitude corrections?
docs.x: When must pilots request ATC approval for cold temperature altitude corrections? Whenever applying a cold temperature altitude correction. They do NOT need to notify ATC of the final approach segment correction (new MDA or DA). SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: On a Baro-VNAV RNAV (GPS) approach without a temperature compensating system, which line of minima cannot be used if the temperature is outside the charted range?
docs.x: On a Baro-VNAV RNAV (GPS) approach without a temperature compensating system, which line of minima cannot be used if the temperature is outside the charted range? The LNAV/VNAV line of minima. The LNAV line of minima may still be used after applying cold temperature corrections. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: Are cold temperature correction "snowflake" icons shown on Jeppesen charts?
docs.x: Are cold temperature correction "snowflake" icons shown on Jeppesen charts? No. Snowflake icons appear on US Terminal Procedure Publications only, not on Jeppesen charts as used by Hawaiian Airlines crews. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: What temperature inhibits pack inlet anti-ice operation?
docs.x: What temperature inhibits pack inlet anti-ice operation? Inhibited on the ground and when TAT is above 10 degrees C. -- EXTERIOR WALKAROUND -- SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: Who performs the exterior preflight inspection?
docs.x: Who performs the exterior preflight inspection? The pilot monitoring or IRO. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: Are static ports heated?
docs.x: Are static ports heated? No. Static ports are NOT heated - ensure clear of ice/frost during preflight. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: What is the function of the negative pressure relief vents?
docs.x: What is the function of the negative pressure relief vents? Protect the fuselage during abnormal negative pressure conditions. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: What do both outflow valves do at touchdown?
docs.x: What do both outflow valves do at touchdown? Both open to depressurize the cabin. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: If one outflow valve fails, can cabin altitude still be maintained?
docs.x: If one outflow valve fails, can cabin altitude still be maintained? Yes. Cabin altitude and full ventilation rates can be maintained by either valve alone. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: When is the TAT probe heated?
docs.x: When is the TAT probe heated? In flight only - when airspeed is more than 50 knots. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: Pitot probes have two heat power levels. What determines which level is used?
docs.x: Pitot probes have two heat power levels. What determines which level is used? Below 50 knots = low power; above 50 knots = high power. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: Below what ground speed is the automatic ice detection system inhibited?
docs.x: Below what ground speed is the automatic ice detection system inhibited? Below 75 knots. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: What are the cargo door wind speed limits?
docs.x: What are the cargo door wind speed limits? Do not operate with winds at the door of more than 40 knots; do not keep door open if gusts exceed 65 knots. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: What are the B787 fan blades made of, how many are there, and what protects their edges?
docs.x: What are the B787 fan blades made of, how many are there, and what protects their edges? 18 fan blades made from Carbon Fiber Reinforced Plastic (CFRP). Leading and trailing edges are titanium. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: How many T/R drag links and blocker doors are installed per engine, and what is the MEL limit?
docs.x: How many T/R drag links and blocker doors are installed per engine, and what is the MEL limit? 24 installed per engine. More than 1 missing = thrust reverser inoperative. Up to 12 may be missing on one engine per MEL (with weight penalties). SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: How much does the B787 wing flex during takeoff and landing?
docs.x: How much does the B787 wing flex during takeoff and landing? About 12 feet. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: How many static discharge wicks are on each wing?
docs.x: How many static discharge wicks are on each wing? 12. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: When should a brake wear indicator pin be written up?
docs.x: When should a brake wear indicator pin be written up? When the indicator is flush with the guide. (Indicator extending OUT of the guide = brakes are good.) SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: How many Electronic Brake Actuators are installed per wheel?
docs.x: How many Electronic Brake Actuators are installed per wheel? Four (4). SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: On the ground with both engines off, what happens if either APU fire detector loop detects a fire?
docs.x: On the ground with both engines off, what happens if either APU fire detector loop detects a fire? The APU automatically shuts down AND the extinguisher bottle discharges automatically. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: What do the parking brake lights at the nose wheel well indicate?
docs.x: What do the parking brake lights at the nose wheel well indicate? Blue light = parking brakes OFF; amber and red lights = parking brake set and on. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: What is the Hybrid Laminar Flow Control (HLFC) system, and what are the crew requirements?
docs.x: What is the Hybrid Laminar Flow Control (HLFC) system, and what are the crew requirements? A system on the vertical stabilizer to reduce aerodynamic drag. There are NO crew procedures, NO monitoring requirements, and NO alert messages for any failure mode. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: How many static ports are on the vertical stabilizer, and what is their function?
docs.x: How many static ports are on the vertical stabilizer, and what is their function? Four (two on each side). They provide inputs to the lateral gust suppression function. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: Does lateral gust suppression cause control column or rudder pedal movement?
docs.x: Does lateral gust suppression cause control column or rudder pedal movement? No. Operation does not result in control wheel, control column, or rudder pedal movement. Only available in normal mode. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: What does the tail strike detection system consist of, and what EICAS indication does it give?
docs.x: What does the tail strike detection system consist of, and what EICAS indication does it give? A two-inch blade target and two frangible wires installed on the aft body. EICAS caution TAIL STRIKE with beeper and Master CAUTION light. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: What is the APU battery voltage and type, and how quickly is vapor vented?
docs.x: What is the APU battery voltage and type, and how quickly is vapor vented? 32V Lithium-ion. Any vapor in the containment box is vented overboard within 1.5 seconds. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: If aft external power is connected along with both forward power sources, which engine must be started first and why?
docs.x: If aft external power is connected along with both forward power sources, which engine must be started first and why? The right engine must be started first to receive the benefit of reduced load shedding. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: What is the function of the FOD deflector door, and when might it retract on the ground?
docs.x: What is the function of the FOD deflector door, and when might it retract on the ground? Protects CAC inlets from debris during ground operations and landing. May retract on the ground below 35 degrees F or above 95 degrees F. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: Does the B789 have grey water drain masts?
docs.x: Does the B789 have grey water drain masts? No. Grey water is contained in two storage tanks located aft of the bulk cargo. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: What do the raked wingtips do compared to winglets?
docs.x: What do the raked wingtips do compared to winglets? Raked wingtips act similar to a winglet to reduce wingtip vortices but are more efficient than winglets. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: During the HLFC empennage door operation, what happens at low airspeed in flight vs. cruise?
docs.x: During the HLFC empennage door operation, what happens at low airspeed in flight vs. cruise? Low airspeed: forward doors open for purge mode (removes water/debris). Cruise/high airspeed: aft doors open for suction mode (improves laminar flow at leading edge). SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: How many static dischargers are on the rudder?
docs.x: How many static dischargers are on the rudder? 3 at the tip and 7 on the trailing edge. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: What is the purpose of the diverter strips on the radome?
docs.x: What is the purpose of the diverter strips on the radome? Provide an electrostatic lightning shield for the radome and provide a path to bleed off static electricity generated during flight. SV Ground deck SV Ground

docs.t: What does the mnemonic FFLAAPOD stand for for flight deck emergency equipment?
docs.x: What does the mnemonic FFLAAPOD stand for for flight deck emergency equipment? Flashlights (2), Fire extinguisher (1), Life Vests (4), AVSAX and Gloves (1), (Crash) Axe (1), PBE (1), O2 Masks (4), Descent Devices (4) SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: How many descent devices are carried on the B787 flight deck?
docs.x: How many descent devices are carried on the B787 flight deck? 4 SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: How many PBEs are carried on the B787 flight deck?
docs.x: How many PBEs are carried on the B787 flight deck? 1 SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: After the Battery switch is pushed ON, approximately how long does it take for the LEFT CCR to come online?
docs.x: After the Battery switch is pushed ON, approximately how long does it take for the LEFT CCR to come online? Approximately 2-3 minutes SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: What condition must be met before the RIGHT CCR begins its start-up cycle?
docs.x: What condition must be met before the RIGHT CCR begins its start-up cycle? The LEFT CCR must complete start-up AND a power source other than the battery (APU or external power) must be available SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: What is the maximum runway slope for B787-9 takeoff and landing?
docs.x: What is the maximum runway slope for B787-9 takeoff and landing? +/-2% SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: What is the maximum takeoff and landing tailwind for the B787-9?
docs.x: What is the maximum takeoff and landing tailwind for the B787-9? 15 knots SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: What is the maximum takeoff and landing altitude for the B787-9?
docs.x: What is the maximum takeoff and landing altitude for the B787-9? 14,000 feet SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: Is it permissible to operate HF radios during refueling?
docs.x: Is it permissible to operate HF radios during refueling? No - do not operate HF radios when refueling SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: What three conditions must ALL be present for RTO to command maximum braking pressure?
docs.x: What three conditions must ALL be present for RTO to command maximum braking pressure? (1) Airplane is on the ground, (2) groundspeed is above 85 kts, AND (3) both thrust levers are retarded to idle SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: Name the three conditions that cause the RAT to deploy automatically.
docs.x: Name the three conditions that cause the RAT to deploy automatically. (1) Both engines failed OR all 3 hydraulic system pressures are low; (2) loss of all electrical power to CA and FO flight instruments; (3) loss of all four electric motor-driven pumps (EMPs) and an engine fails on takeoff or landing SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: After an APU fire signal, the APU shuts down immediately. How many seconds later does the extinguisher bottle automatically discharge?
docs.x: After an APU fire signal, the APU shuts down immediately. How many seconds later does the extinguisher bottle automatically discharge? 15 seconds (to allow the fuel valve to close) SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: What is the takeoff thrust rating of each GEnx-1B74/75 engine?
docs.x: What is the takeoff thrust rating of each GEnx-1B74/75 engine? 74,100 lbs (FCOM verified) SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: Can the APU start if the common core system is not yet running?
docs.x: Can the APU start if the common core system is not yet running? No - the APU controller delays start until the required common core applications are available SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: How many VHF radios can operate in data mode simultaneously on the B787?
docs.x: How many VHF radios can operate in data mode simultaneously on the B787? Only one VHF radio can operate in data mode at a time SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: What is VHF L configured for?
docs.x: What is VHF L configured for? Voice communication only SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: What does an HF antenna tuning tone lasting more than 7 seconds indicate?
docs.x: What does an HF antenna tuning tone lasting more than 7 seconds indicate? Failure of the system to tune SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: With the SEAT BELTS switch in AUTO, what three conditions cause the seat belt signs to automatically illuminate?
docs.x: With the SEAT BELTS switch in AUTO, what three conditions cause the seat belt signs to automatically illuminate? (1) Landing gear not up and locked; (2) flap lever at 5 or greater; (3) cabin altitude above 10,000 feet SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: At what altitude do the passenger oxygen masks automatically drop from the PSUs?
docs.x: At what altitude do the passenger oxygen masks automatically drop from the PSUs? Prior to the cabin reaching the GREATER of: 14,500 feet, origin airfield altitude +1,500 feet, or destination airfield altitude +1,500 feet SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: How long is passenger oxygen available after mask deployment?
docs.x: How long is passenger oxygen available after mask deployment? Approximately 22 minutes SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: What are the maximum wind limits for Autoland operations (headwind, tailwind, crosswind)?
docs.x: What are the maximum wind limits for Autoland operations (headwind, tailwind, crosswind)? Headwind 25 kts, Tailwind 15 kts, Crosswind 25 kts SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: Without LAND 2 or LAND 3 annunciated, below what height AGL must the autopilot be disengaged?
docs.x: Without LAND 2 or LAND 3 annunciated, below what height AGL must the autopilot be disengaged? 135 feet AGL SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: What is the restriction on using FLCH on final approach?
docs.x: What is the restriction on using FLCH on final approach? Do not use FLCH on final approach below 1,000 feet AFE SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: In what flight control mode(s) is takeoff permitted?
docs.x: In what flight control mode(s) is takeoff permitted? Normal mode ONLY (not Secondary, not Direct) SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: What is the maximum altitude with flaps extended?
docs.x: What is the maximum altitude with flaps extended? 20,000 feet SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: Does placing either RECIRC FAN switch to OFF generate an EICAS message?
docs.x: Does placing either RECIRC FAN switch to OFF generate an EICAS message? Yes SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: Can a single CAC operate its associated PACK in all modes?
docs.x: Can a single CAC operate its associated PACK in all modes? Yes - a single CAC provides sufficient air to operate its associated PACK in all operating modes SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: How many outflow valves does the B787 pressurization system have, and where are they located?
docs.x: How many outflow valves does the B787 pressurization system have, and where are they located? Two outflow valves - one forward and one aft SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: What data inputs does the B787 pressurization system use to calculate the cabin pressurization schedule?
docs.x: What data inputs does the B787 pressurization system use to calculate the cabin pressurization schedule? Ambient pressure and flight plan data from the FMC SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: What is the range of bank limit in AUTO mode, and what does it depend on?
docs.x: What is the range of bank limit in AUTO mode, and what does it depend on? 15 to 25 degrees, depending on TAS SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: If TO/GA is not pushed below 50 knots, when is autothrottle operation available?
docs.x: If TO/GA is not pushed below 50 knots, when is autothrottle operation available? Autothrottle operation is inhibited until reaching 400 feet altitude SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: Pushing the TO/GA switch above what speed disarms LNAV and VNAV?
docs.x: Pushing the TO/GA switch above what speed disarms LNAV and VNAV? Above 80 knots SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: The glideslope attitude stabilizing mode limits descent angle to 3.25 degrees using inertial data. For how long does this mode operate?
docs.x: The glideslope attitude stabilizing mode limits descent angle to 3.25 degrees using inertial data. For how long does this mode operate? Up to 15 seconds (not 25 seconds) SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: Between what radio altimeter heights does the autothrottle begin retarding thrust levers to idle during the flare?
docs.x: Between what radio altimeter heights does the autothrottle begin retarding thrust levers to idle during the flare? Between 25 and 50 feet RA SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: What does the APU battery provide power for?
docs.x: What does the APU battery provide power for? APU start; navigation lights when Towing Power mode is active (does NOT provide backup brake power) SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: How many seconds after reaching idle does the RUNNING indication blank on the secondary engine display?
docs.x: How many seconds after reaching idle does the RUNNING indication blank on the secondary engine display? 30 seconds SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: Which EICAS message types CANNOT be canceled using the CANC/RCL switch?
docs.x: Which EICAS message types CANNOT be canceled using the CANC/RCL switch? Warning messages, Communication messages, and Memo messages SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: Which EICAS message types CAN be canceled using the CANC/RCL switch?
docs.x: Which EICAS message types CAN be canceled using the CANC/RCL switch? Caution messages and Advisory messages SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: What does a rectangle icon preceding an EICAS message indicate?
docs.x: What does a rectangle icon preceding an EICAS message indicate? The message has associated procedural steps SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: What is the difference between an ECL closed loop and an open loop action item?
docs.x: What is the difference between an ECL closed loop and an open loop action item? Closed loop items continuously monitor a switch position and auto-check when correct. Open loop items require manual crew confirmation. SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: What are the two main components of the IRS?
docs.x: What are the two main components of the IRS? Inertial Reference Units (IRUs) and Attitude and Heading Reference Units (AHRUs) SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: In the NAV AIR DATA SYS degraded mode, what is the effect on flight controls and automation?
docs.x: In the NAV AIR DATA SYS degraded mode, what is the effect on flight controls and automation? Primary Flight Controls enter Secondary Mode; AFDS is INOP; Autopilot is INOP; Autothrottles are INOP SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: In the NAV AIR DATA SYS degraded mode, where does the ISFD get its data from?
docs.x: In the NAV AIR DATA SYS degraded mode, where does the ISFD get its data from? Center pitot/static only (altitude and airspeed data may be unreliable) SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: How many FMCs does the B787 have, and what are they called?
docs.x: How many FMCs does the B787 have, and what are they called? 3 FMCs - Master, Spare, and Backup SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: Is a single FMC failure apparent to the crew? What action is required?
docs.x: Is a single FMC failure apparent to the crew? What action is required? Not apparent to the crew. No crew action is necessary. LNAV/VNAV remain active. SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: What EICAS message is displayed for a dual FMC failure?
docs.x: What EICAS message is displayed for a dual FMC failure? SINGLE FMC (advisory) SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: After a dual FMC failure, can LNAV and VNAV be used?
docs.x: After a dual FMC failure, can LNAV and VNAV be used? LNAV/VNAV are deselected but can be reselected. The flight plan needs to be reactivated and executed. SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: What EICAS message is displayed for a triple FMC failure?
docs.x: What EICAS message is displayed for a triple FMC failure? FMC (advisory) SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: After a triple FMC failure, what navigation capability remains via the TCPs?
docs.x: After a triple FMC failure, what navigation capability remains via the TCPs? Capability to enter a single LAT/LONG waypoint; track, distance to go, and groundspeed to that waypoint SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: After a triple FMC failure, is the autopilot available?
docs.x: After a triple FMC failure, is the autopilot available? Yes - autopilot roll and/or pitch modes remain available. Autothrottles also remain available. SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: What are the requirements for the Systems Validation (SV) exam?
docs.x: What are the requirements for the Systems Validation (SV) exam? 100 questions, 3-hour time limit, open book, 80% passing score, plus a Memory Items Quiz SFTD 1 deck SFTD 1

docs.t: What are the maximum wind component limits for Autoland operations?
docs.x: What are the maximum wind component limits for Autoland operations? Headwind 25 kts, Tailwind 15 kts, Crosswind 25 kts. (L.10.4) SFTD 2 deck SFTD 2

docs.t: Without LAND 2 or LAND 3 annunciated, below what altitude AGL must the autopilot be disengaged?
docs.x: Without LAND 2 or LAND 3 annunciated, below what altitude AGL must the autopilot be disengaged? 135 feet AGL. (L.10.4) SFTD 2 deck SFTD 2

docs.t: FLCH must not be used on final approach below what altitude?
docs.x: FLCH must not be used on final approach below what altitude? 1,000 feet AFE. (L.10.5) SFTD 2 deck SFTD 2

docs.t: Takeoff is permitted in Normal, Secondary, or Direct flight control mode. Which is correct?
docs.x: Takeoff is permitted in Normal, Secondary, or Direct flight control mode. Which is correct? Normal mode ONLY. Takeoff is prohibited in Secondary and Direct modes. (L.10.6) SFTD 2 deck SFTD 2

docs.t: What is the maximum altitude for flap extension on the B787?
docs.x: What is the maximum altitude for flap extension on the B787? 20,000 feet. (L.10.6) SFTD 2 deck SFTD 2

docs.t: If either the upper or lower RECIRC FAN switch is placed OFF, is an EICAS message displayed?
docs.x: If either the upper or lower RECIRC FAN switch is placed OFF, is an EICAS message displayed? Yes. (FCOM 2.10.3) SFTD 2 deck SFTD 2

docs.t: Can a single CAC operate its associated PACK in all modes?
docs.x: Can a single CAC operate its associated PACK in all modes? Yes, a single CAC provides sufficient air for its PACK in all operating modes. (FCOM 2.20.1) SFTD 2 deck SFTD 2

docs.t: How many outflow valves does the B787 pressurization system have, and where are they located?
docs.x: How many outflow valves does the B787 pressurization system have, and where are they located? Two outflow valves - one forward and one aft. (FCOM 2.30.1) SFTD 2 deck SFTD 2

docs.t: With BACKUP WINDOW HEAT switches ON, what happens if the primary window heat fails?
docs.x: With BACKUP WINDOW HEAT switches ON, what happens if the primary window heat fails? Backup anti-fogging is commanded on for the selected windows. (FCOM 3.10.3) SFTD 2 deck SFTD 2

docs.t: Where is the EAI (Engine Anti-Ice) indication displayed on EICAS?
docs.x: Where is the EAI (Engine Anti-Ice) indication displayed on EICAS? Above the EICAS N1 indication. (FCOM) SFTD 2 deck SFTD 2

docs.t: Can engine anti-ice be operated on the ground?
docs.x: Can engine anti-ice be operated on the ground? Yes, it can be operated in flight or on the ground. However, automatic operation is inhibited on the ground. (FCOM) SFTD 2 deck SFTD 2

docs.t: The BANK LIMIT Selector in AUTO varies between what range, and what does it depend on?
docs.x: The BANK LIMIT Selector in AUTO varies between what range, and what does it depend on? 15 to 25 degrees, depending on TAS. (FCOM 4.10.10) SFTD 2 deck SFTD 2

docs.t: If TO/GA is not pushed before 50 knots during the takeoff roll, when does autothrottle operation resume?
docs.x: If TO/GA is not pushed before 50 knots during the takeoff roll, when does autothrottle operation resume? Autothrottle operation is inhibited until reaching 400 feet altitude. (FCOM 4.10.21) SFTD 2 deck SFTD 2

docs.t: What happens to LNAV and VNAV if either TO/GA switch is pushed above 80 knots?
docs.x: What happens to LNAV and VNAV if either TO/GA switch is pushed above 80 knots? LNAV and VNAV are disarmed. (FCOM 4.10.21) SFTD 2 deck SFTD 2

docs.t: How long is passenger oxygen available after deployment?
docs.x: How long is passenger oxygen available after deployment? Approximately 22 minutes. (FCOM 1.30.31/1.40.14) SFTD 2 deck SFTD 2

docs.t: In the glideslope attitude stabilizing mode, for how long does the AFDS use inertial data when the G/S signal is unreliable?
docs.x: In the glideslope attitude stabilizing mode, for how long does the AFDS use inertial data when the G/S signal is unreliable? 15 seconds. (FCOM 4.20.4) SFTD 2 deck SFTD 2

docs.t: What is the maximum descent angle the AFDS holds in glideslope attitude stabilizing mode?
docs.x: What is the maximum descent angle the AFDS holds in glideslope attitude stabilizing mode? 3.25 degrees. (FCOM 4.20.4) SFTD 2 deck SFTD 2

docs.t: During an autoland flare, between what radio altimeter heights does the autothrottle begin retarding thrust levers to idle?
docs.x: During an autoland flare, between what radio altimeter heights does the autothrottle begin retarding thrust levers to idle? Between 25 and 50 feet RA. (FCOM - section not specified) SFTD 2 deck SFTD 2

docs.t: What does the APU battery provide power for on the ground?
docs.x: What does the APU battery provide power for on the ground? APU start and navigation lights when Towing Power mode is active. It does NOT power the aircraft brakes. (FCOM 6.20.4) SFTD 2 deck SFTD 2

docs.t: How long after an engine reaches idle does the RUNNING indication on the Secondary Engine Display blank?
docs.x: How long after an engine reaches idle does the RUNNING indication on the Secondary Engine Display blank? 30 seconds. (FCOM 7.10.8) SFTD 2 deck SFTD 2

docs.t: How many FMCs does the B787 have, and what are they called?
docs.x: How many FMCs does the B787 have, and what are they called? 3 FMCs: Master, Spare, and Backup. (FCOM 11.30.1) SFTD 2 deck SFTD 2

docs.t: What EICAS message is generated by a dual FMC failure?
docs.x: What EICAS message is generated by a dual FMC failure? SINGLE FMC (advisory). (FCOM 11.32.5) SFTD 2 deck SFTD 2

docs.t: After a dual FMC failure with the 3rd FMC taking over, can LNAV/VNAV be used?
docs.x: After a dual FMC failure with the 3rd FMC taking over, can LNAV/VNAV be used? LNAV/VNAV is deselected but can be reselected. The flight plan must be reactivated and executed. (FCOM 11.32.5) SFTD 2 deck SFTD 2

docs.t: What EICAS message indicates a triple FMC failure?
docs.x: What EICAS message indicates a triple FMC failure? FMC (advisory). (FCOM 11.32.6) SFTD 2 deck SFTD 2

docs.t: Following a triple FMC failure, are autothrottles available?
docs.x: Following a triple FMC failure, are autothrottles available? Yes, autothrottles are still available. (FCOM 11.32.6) SFTD 2 deck SFTD 2

docs.t: After a triple FMC failure, what ILS/GLS information is still available on the ISFD?
docs.x: After a triple FMC failure, what ILS/GLS information is still available on the ISFD? LEFT side ILS or GLS deviations are displayed on the ISFD. (FCOM 11.32.6) SFTD 2 deck SFTD 2

docs.t: Which EICAS message types CANNOT be canceled with the CANC/RCL switch?
docs.x: Which EICAS message types CANNOT be canceled with the CANC/RCL switch? Warning Messages, Communication Messages, and Memo Messages. (FCOM 15.10.1) SFTD 2 deck SFTD 2

docs.t: Which EICAS message types CAN be canceled with the CANC/RCL switch?
docs.x: Which EICAS message types CAN be canceled with the CANC/RCL switch? Caution Messages and Advisory Messages. (FCOM 15.10.1) SFTD 2 deck SFTD 2

docs.t: What does the rectangle icon preceding an EICAS alert message indicate?
docs.x: What does the rectangle icon preceding an EICAS alert message indicate? That the message has associated procedural steps. (FCOM 15.10.1) SFTD 2 deck SFTD 2

docs.t: What is the difference between a closed-loop and open-loop ECL action item?
docs.x: What is the difference between a closed-loop and open-loop ECL action item? A closed-loop item continuously monitors the position of a flight deck switch (confirmed automatically). An open-loop item needs a manual confirmation by the crew. (FCOM 10.60.2) SFTD 2 deck SFTD 2

docs.t: In the printed non-normal QRH, how are memory items separated from reference items?
docs.x: In the printed non-normal QRH, how are memory items separated from reference items? By a dashed horizontal line following the last memory item. (QRH CI2.2) SFTD 2 deck SFTD 2

docs.t: In the electronic ECL, how are memory items identified?
docs.x: In the electronic ECL, how are memory items identified? They are NOT identified in the electronic ECL. (QRH CI2.2) SFTD 2 deck SFTD 2

docs.t: What are the two major components of the IRS?
docs.x: What are the two major components of the IRS? Inertial Reference Units (IRUs) and Attitude and Heading Reference Units (AHRUs). (FCOM 11.20.3) SFTD 2 deck SFTD 2

docs.t: During a NAV AIR DATA SYS failure, what is the impact on flight control mode and automation?
docs.x: During a NAV AIR DATA SYS failure, what is the impact on flight control mode and automation? Primary flight controls enter Secondary Mode; AFDS, Autopilot, and Autothrottles are all INOP. (FCOM 11.20.8) SFTD 2 deck SFTD 2

docs.t: During a NAV AIR DATA SYS failure, what does the ISFD display, and is it reliable?
docs.x: During a NAV AIR DATA SYS failure, what does the ISFD display, and is it reliable? The ISFD displays Altitude and Airspeed, but the data may be unreliable (based on center pitot/static only). (FCOM 11.20.8) SFTD 2 deck SFTD 2

docs.t: During a NAV AIRSPEED DATA failure, what airspeed source remains available to the displays?
docs.x: During a NAV AIRSPEED DATA failure, what airspeed source remains available to the displays? IRS provides AOA Airspeed. ISFD airspeed may be unreliable. Voted ADRS airspeed to main displays is lost. (FCOM 11.20.9) SFTD 2 deck SFTD 2

docs.t: What is the ECL Checklist Condition field used for?
docs.x: What is the ECL Checklist Condition field used for? It defines the EICAS message (what triggered the procedure). (FCOM 10.60.2 / slide 23) SFTD 2 deck SFTD 2

docs.t: What is the ECL Checklist Objective field used for?
docs.x: What is the ECL Checklist Objective field used for? It explains the end-state goal of the procedure. (slide 23) SFTD 2 deck SFTD 2

docs.t: Where are unannunciated checklists accessed from on the ECL?
docs.x: Where are unannunciated checklists accessed from on the ECL? Via the NON-NORMAL MENU. (QRH Unann.Index.1 / QRH CI.2.1 / FCOM 10.50.16) SFTD 2 deck SFTD 2

docs.t: What is the Systems Validation (SV) exam passing score and format?
docs.x: What is the Systems Validation (SV) exam passing score and format? 100 questions, 3-hour time limit, open book, passing score of 80%. Also includes a Memory Items Test. (FOTM 3.7.2.1) SFTD 2 deck SFTD 2
